TL;DR

Feasibility pilot. Nothing here feeds data/final. The module takes the two tables written by utils.scraping.scraper_amaterskedivadlo (places, ensembles) and asks the one question that decides whether the source is worth building on: how evenly is it documented — across town sizes, across Bohemia and Moravia, across Czech- and German-speaking districts — before any of it is read as a measure of associational life.

How it works

(Not to be confused with utils.parsing.theater, which is the war theatre — Russia / Italy / France.)

What "before 1914" means when a year is fuzzy

An ensemble's start is printed as a year, a decade (191x) or a century (19xx) and is carried with its precision. starts_before is the single rule:

year      1913            -> yes        1914            -> no
decade    190x (≤1909)    -> yes        191x (1910–19)  -> ambiguous     192x -> no
century   18xx (≤1899)    -> yes        19xx            -> ambiguous

"Before 1914" in every table below means yes — the ambiguous are counted and shown beside it, never folded in.

The join

A database place (present-day obec / místní část, with coordinates) is tied to a row of settlements_1910 (the ČSÚ lexikon crosswalk; coordinates for about half the obce and few hamlets) in three tiers, most trusted first:

name+coords     same normalised name, both geocoded, ≤ `max_km` apart
name+okres      same normalised name, the settlement not geocoded, and the place's
                present-day okres on the settlement's okres timeline (`okres_all`)
                — accepted only where that leaves exactly one candidate on each side
name+polygon    same normalised name, the settlement not geocoded, and the place's own
                point inside the settlement's 1910 okres (MPIDR court polygons, 1 km
                near-miss repair) — again only one candidate on each side
fuzzy+coords    names ≥ `min_similarity` alike, ≤ `fuzzy_km` apart

A place's names are its own, the former names the database prints and a city part's own name (place_name_keys); a settlement is a candidate only if it has a 1910 okres (has_okres_1910; Prague's eight quarters are given okres Praha, audit 2026-11-11 C1).

The match is one-to-one on both sides and the result has exactly one row per place — both asserted. Inside one build the settlement is addressed by its row position, settlement_row; the saved settlement table is keyed by settlement_id, the key settlements_1910 has carried since it was given one (a name alone is no key: it can be an obec and an osada in the same okres).

Town size

There is no settlement-level 1910 population in the repo (the ČSÚ lexikon volume that carries it is a PDF whose digits do not extract), so size is proxied by three classes read off what the crosswalk does carry: the seat of a 1910 judicial district, any other commune, and a dependent hamlet or part. If the settlements frame is given a population_1910 column, coverage_tables bands on that instead.

The chronicle (0.2.0)

Each place's chronicle_text is a run of notes, one per line, two in three opening with a date (1895-1938 DS Sokola, Od 1881, Koncem 19. stol., V 80. letech). chronicle_lines reads every line into a table keyed (geo_id, line_no): its kind (dated event, undated note, periodical citation, the database's admin note on the present okres, heading, separator), its leading date as start and end intervals (so 191x, kolem 1850 and před 1900 each keep their width), the associations it names and whether it is puppet theatre. Rules only; a bare decade takes its century from the dated line above it, and century_inference_check measures that rule where the century is printed. Nothing here is written to data/final.

Clauses (0.4.0)

One line is often several events (1887-1934 SDO, 1914 32 členů.), so chronicle_clauses cuts each note wherever a new date opens after a comma, a semicolon or a full stop — never inside brackets, a quoted title, the line's leading date, or a dated newspaper report — keyed (geo_id, line_no, clause_no). Each clause carries its own date interval, the other years it prints, and the EVENT_CUES its words point to: the codebook's draft, which the author rules on before any of it is a code (D-140).

The measure (0.5.0)

The author ruled each type's role and twelve design calls (D-141; CODEBOOK_ROLES and the constants beside it). code_clauses applies them; evidence_table puts the ensemble list, the coded clauses and the first reports into one interval form and gives each company one company_id across sources; place_year_panel turns that into Czech amateur theatre per place and year, 1780–1913, every measure certain and possible; place_units gives each place its 1910 settlement, okres and court (D-222) and area_year_tables sums the panel to them and to the census's pooled okres. Written to data/interim/theatre/ by the pilot runner; nothing reaches the persons.

Ensemble pages (0.6.0)

An ensemble's own page (scraper step C) gives the decades it was active (Působení), an end or last report, and a chronicle of its own. By the author's rulings (D-145): a listed decade makes the company possible across it, never certain, and a page that lists decades replaces B1's open end, so the company is possible only in those decades (a "…" gap adds nothing); a printed end closes the span, certain from start to end; and the ensemble's chronicle is cut and coded like a place's, its company clauses tied to that ensemble (ensemble_chronicle_clauses). A company's possible years are the union of its records' ranges, no longer the hull, so a gap between two decades stays empty.

The codebook rulings (0.13.0)

The author's fourteen rulings on what the blind check (D-228) found the codebook did not settle (D-254, reference/places/theatre_codebook_rulings.csv). In the rules: company evidence on a place's chronicle needs a local theatre body the clause names (Q1: active alone is activity; school, student, church and travelling players and an umbrella union never a company), and on a company's own page every dated note of it is a company act unless it names another performer (Q5, Q7, Q13); Czech means Czech played (Q4: a Czech title counts, české hry nepovolovány does not; pre-1848 school or church theatre of unstated language is possible, never a company); a bare date + name line is listed only with a body word, else name_only, which the model reads (Q8); a century's end is its last decade and its middle the half ±5 (Q9); a decline is not a pause, and a pause never turns a dated performance possible (Q11); a hedge covers what it qualifies, not a title or a detail (Q12); a dated clause printing more years for the theatre goes to the model, whose interval then stands, and the rules read the last printed end and an earlier od start (Q6). Plus the rare cases: a pointer to a list records nothing, a word in a play's title is no cue, a building's founding is not the company's, a year in a full date (8.2.1903) is read, a cast list is members, and a hired hall on a company's page is the company's act with its theatre possible only.

Usage

from utils.parsing import amateur_theatre as at
tables = at.coverage_tables(places, ensembles, settlements, districts,
                            okresy=["Kutná Hora", "Trutnov", "Přerov"])
at.coverage_report(tables)

def normalise_name(name) -> str:
    """A place name reduced to what should be equal across the two sources.

    Case-folded; parentheticals, ``X viz Y`` cross-reference tails, the database's
    ``, do 1925 Bračice`` / ``, dříve Bračice`` former-name notes and its ``, o. Svitavy``
    okres qualifiers dropped; punctuation and hyphens turned into single spaces.
    **Diacritics are kept** — in Czech they separate different villages (*Bělá* / *Bílá*).
    """
    if name is None or (isinstance(name, float) and np.isnan(name)):
        return ""
    return _NON_WORD.sub(" ", _strip_notes(str(name))).strip().casefold()

def place_name_keys(name) -> list[str]:
    """Every key a database place may be filed under in 1910, its own name first.

    Besides :func:`normalise_name`: each former name the database prints (``Týnec nad
    Labem, dříve Labská Týnice`` → *labská týnice*; ``Hřivčice, dříve Dřívčice / Řivčice``
    → both), since the former name is often the one of 1910; and a city part's own name
    (``Praha-Žižkov`` → *žižkov*, ``Plzeň 5-Křimice`` → *křimice*, :data:`CITY_PREFIXES`),
    since in 1910 the part was a commune of its own.  Duplicates and empty keys dropped.
    """
    own = normalise_name(name)
    if not own:
        return []
    raw = str(name)
    keys = [own]
    formers = _FORMER_NAME.findall(_PAREN.sub(lambda m: m.group(0).replace("(", ", ").replace(")", ""), raw))
    formers += _UNTIL_YEAR.findall(raw)                 # ", do 1925 Bračice": the name until 1925
    for former in formers:
        keys += [normalise_name(part) for part in former.split("/")]
    part = _CITY_PREFIX.match(_strip_notes(raw))
    if part:
        keys.append(normalise_name(part.group(1)))
    return list(dict.fromkeys(k for k in keys if k))

def city_part_name(name_key: str) -> str | None:
    """The part's own name where the lexikon files it under its city.

    The register heads a village since absorbed by a town as ``HRANICE IV-DRAHOTUŠE`` or
    ``PŘEROV VII-ČEKYNĚ``; the database calls it *Drahotuše*, *Čekyně*.  Returns the part
    after the roman numeral, or None for an ordinary name.
    """
    m = _CITY_PART.match(name_key or "")
    return m.group(1) if m else None

def strip_diacritics(text: str) -> str:
    return "".join(c for c in unicodedata.normalize("NFD", text) if not unicodedata.combining(c))

def haversine_km(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2):
    """Great-circle distance in km (vectorised; broadcasts)."""
    lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2 = (np.radians(np.asarray(v, dtype=float)) for v in (lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2))
    a = np.sin((lat2 - lat1) / 2) ** 2 + np.cos(lat1) * np.cos(lat2) * np.sin((lon2 - lon1) / 2) ** 2
    return 2 * EARTH_RADIUS_KM * np.arcsin(np.sqrt(a))

def okres_tokens(okres_all) -> list[str]:
    """The okres timeline of a settlement as a list (stray brackets and spaces removed)."""
    if not isinstance(okres_all, str):
        return []
    return [t for t in (re.sub(r"\s+", " ", tok.strip(" ()")) for tok in okres_all.split("|")) if t]

def settlement_frame(settlements: pd.DataFrame, districts: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """``settlements_1910`` with the columns the join and the tabulation need.

    Adds ``settlement_row`` (row position, the working key inside one build; what is saved
    is keyed by the table's own ``settlement_id``, :data:`AREA_LEVELS`), ``name_key``,
    ``name_key_alt`` (:func:`city_part_name`), ``okres_tokens``, ``okres_now`` (the last
    okres on the timeline), ``in_1910`` (the
    settlement has a resolved 1910 okres and status), ``okres_1910_cs`` (the district's
    name from ``districts_1910``, free of the register's OCR breaks) and ``size_class``.
    """
    out = settlements.reset_index(drop=True).copy()
    out.insert(0, "settlement_row", np.arange(len(out)))
    out["name_key"] = out["cs_name"].map(normalise_name)
    out["name_key_alt"] = out["name_key"].map(city_part_name)
    out["okres_tokens"] = out["okres_all"].map(okres_tokens)
    out["okres_now"] = out["okres_tokens"].map(lambda t: t[-1] if t else None)
    out = _prague_quarters(out)
    out["in_1910"] = out["okres_id"].notna() & out["status_1910"].notna()
    # what the area sums need is the 1910 okres; the status only sizes the place (audit C1:
    # a row whose status the lexicon's OCR broke, "Kosmanosy o bec", still has its okres)
    out["has_okres_1910"] = out["okres_id"].notna()

    seats: set[tuple[int, str]] = set()
    out["okres_1910_cs"] = out["okres_1910"]
    if districts is not None:
        codes = districts["okres_code"].str.split("-", expand=True).astype(int)
        okres_id = codes[0] * 1000 + codes[1]
        names = dict(zip(okres_id, districts["okres_cs"]))
        out["okres_1910_cs"] = out["okres_id"].map(names).fillna(out["okres_1910"])
        seats = set(zip(okres_id, districts["gerichtsbezirk_cs"].map(normalise_name)))

    is_seat = pd.Series([(o, n) in seats for o, n in zip(out["okres_id"], out["name_key"])],
                        index=out.index)
    commune = out["status_1910"].eq("obec")
    out["size_class"] = pd.Series("3 hamlet / part", index=out.index, dtype=object)
    out.loc[commune, "size_class"] = "2 other commune"
    out.loc[commune & is_seat, "size_class"] = "1 court-seat town"
    out.loc[~out["in_1910"], "size_class"] = None
    if "population_1910" in out.columns:
        out["size_class"] = pd.cut(out["population_1910"], POPULATION_BANDS,
                                   labels=POPULATION_LABELS, right=False).astype(object)
    return out

def join_places_to_settlements(
    places: pd.DataFrame,
    settlements: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    max_km: float = 5.0,
    fuzzy_km: float = 2.0,
    min_similarity: float = 85.0,
    locator=None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Tie each database place to at most one 1910 settlement, by distance with a name check.

    Args:
        places: the scraper's places table (``geo_id, name, type, lat, lon, okres``).
        settlements: :func:`settlement_frame` output.
        max_km: furthest an exact-name pair may be apart.
        fuzzy_km: furthest a near-name pair may be apart.
        min_similarity: rapidfuzz ratio (0–100) on the normalised, de-accented names.
        locator: a :class:`utils.parsing.spatial.CourtLocator`; with it, tier 2b
            (``name+polygon``) runs.  Without it the join is the three tiers above.

    Returns:
        One row per place — ``geo_id, settlement_row, match_method, distance_km,
        name_similarity`` — with ``settlement_row`` missing where nothing matched and
        ``match_method`` saying why (``unmatched: no such name`` / ``… too far`` /
        ``… ambiguous``).  Asserted: one row per place, no settlement used twice.
    """
    P = places[["geo_id", "name", "type", "lat", "lon", "okres"]].copy()
    P["name_key"] = P["name"].map(normalise_name)
    # a place is reachable under its former name and, a city part, its own (place_name_keys)
    P_keys = (P.drop(columns="name_key").assign(name_key=P["name"].map(place_name_keys))
              .explode("name_key").dropna(subset=["name_key"]))
    # only a row with a 1910 okres can carry a place into the area sums; a present-day merged
    # town with none ("BENÁTKY NAD JIZEROU") would otherwise win on distance (audit C1)
    candidates = settlements[settlements["has_okres_1910"]] if "has_okres_1910" in settlements else settlements
    S = candidates[["settlement_row", "name_key", "status_1910", "lat", "lon", "okres_tokens", "okres_id"]]
    # a city part is reachable under its own name as well as under "CITY IV-PART"
    alt = candidates.loc[candidates["name_key_alt"].notna(), S.columns.drop("name_key")].assign(
        name_key=candidates["name_key_alt"].dropna())
    by_name = pd.concat([S, alt[S.columns]], ignore_index=True)

    pairs = P_keys.merge(by_name, on="name_key", suffixes=("", "_s"))
    pairs = pairs[pairs["name_key"] != ""]
    geocoded = pairs["lat_s"].notna()
    pairs["distance_km"] = np.where(
        geocoded, haversine_km(pairs["lat"], pairs["lon"], pairs["lat_s"].fillna(0),
                               pairs["lon_s"].fillna(0)), np.nan)
    pairs["okres_ok"] = [o in toks for o, toks in zip(pairs["okres"], pairs["okres_tokens"])]
    pairs["penalty"] = [_type_penalty(t, s) for t, s in zip(pairs["type"], pairs["status_1910"])]

    used_places: dict[int, tuple] = {}
    used_settlements: set[int] = set()

    def accept(geo_id, row, method, km, similarity) -> None:
        used_places[int(geo_id)] = (int(row), method, km, similarity)
        used_settlements.add(int(row))

    # tier 1 — exact name, both geocoded, close: nearest pair first
    near = pairs[geocoded & (pairs["distance_km"] <= max_km)].sort_values(["distance_km", "penalty"])
    for r in near.itertuples():
        if r.geo_id not in used_places and r.settlement_row not in used_settlements:
            accept(r.geo_id, r.settlement_row, "name+coords", round(float(r.distance_km), 2), 100.0)

    # tier 2 — exact name, settlement not geocoded, okres on its timeline, unique both ways
    loose = pairs[~geocoded & pairs["okres_ok"]
                  & ~pairs["geo_id"].isin(list(used_places))
                  & ~pairs["settlement_row"].isin(used_settlements)]
    loose = loose[loose["penalty"] == loose.groupby("geo_id")["penalty"].transform("min")]
    n_for_place = loose.groupby("geo_id")["settlement_row"].transform("nunique")
    n_for_settlement = loose.groupby("settlement_row")["geo_id"].transform("nunique")
    ambiguous = set(loose.loc[(n_for_place > 1) | (n_for_settlement > 1), "geo_id"])
    for r in loose[(n_for_place == 1) & (n_for_settlement == 1)].itertuples():
        accept(r.geo_id, r.settlement_row, "name+okres", np.nan, 100.0)

    # tier 2b — exact name, settlement not geocoded, and the place's own point lies in the
    # settlement's 1910 okres (MPIDR polygons, near misses of 1 km repaired), unique both ways.
    # Reaches what tier 2 cannot: a city part whose 1910 row has no coordinates and whose
    # okres timeline never names today's okres (Praha-Žižkov → ŽIŽKOV, okres Žižkov; audit C1)
    if locator is not None:
        rest = pairs[~geocoded & pairs["okres_id"].notna() & pairs["lat"].notna()
                     & ~pairs["geo_id"].isin(list(used_places))
                     & ~pairs["settlement_row"].isin(used_settlements)].copy()
        rest["in_okres"] = _point_in_okres(rest, locator)
        rest = rest[rest["in_okres"]]
        rest = rest[rest["penalty"] == rest.groupby("geo_id")["penalty"].transform("min")]
        n_for_place = rest.groupby("geo_id")["settlement_row"].transform("nunique")
        n_for_settlement = rest.groupby("settlement_row")["geo_id"].transform("nunique")
        ambiguous |= set(rest.loc[(n_for_place > 1) | (n_for_settlement > 1), "geo_id"])
        for r in rest[(n_for_place == 1) & (n_for_settlement == 1)].drop_duplicates(
                ["geo_id", "settlement_row"]).itertuples():
            accept(r.geo_id, r.settlement_row, "name+polygon", np.nan, 100.0)

    # tier 3 — near-identical name, very close
    left = P[~P["geo_id"].isin(list(used_places)) & P["lat"].notna() & (P["name_key"] != "")]
    right = S[~S["settlement_row"].isin(used_settlements) & S["lat"].notna()]
    fuzzy_rows = []
    if len(left) and len(right):
        right_lat, right_lon = right["lat"].to_numpy(), right["lon"].to_numpy()
        right_keys = right["name_key"].map(strip_diacritics).to_numpy()
        right_ids = right["settlement_row"].to_numpy()
        for p in left.itertuples():
            km = haversine_km(p.lat, p.lon, right_lat, right_lon)
            key = strip_diacritics(p.name_key)
            for j in np.flatnonzero(km <= fuzzy_km):
                similarity = fuzz.ratio(key, right_keys[j])
                if similarity >= min_similarity:
                    fuzzy_rows.append((float(km[j]), -similarity, p.geo_id, right_ids[j]))
    for km, neg_similarity, geo_id, row in sorted(fuzzy_rows):
        if geo_id not in used_places and row not in used_settlements:
            accept(geo_id, row, "fuzzy+coords", round(km, 2), float(-neg_similarity))

    # why the rest did not match
    has_name = set(pairs["geo_id"])
    too_far = set(pairs.loc[geocoded & (pairs["distance_km"] > max_km), "geo_id"])
    rows = []
    for geo_id in P["geo_id"]:
        if int(geo_id) in used_places:
            rows.append((geo_id, *used_places[int(geo_id)]))
            continue
        reason = ("unmatched: ambiguous" if geo_id in ambiguous
                  else "unmatched: too far" if geo_id in too_far
                  else "unmatched: name elsewhere" if geo_id in has_name
                  else "unmatched: no such name")
        rows.append((geo_id, pd.NA, reason, np.nan, np.nan))
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["geo_id", "settlement_row", "match_method",
                                      "distance_km", "name_similarity"])
    out["settlement_row"] = out["settlement_row"].astype("Int64")

    assert len(out) == len(places) and out["geo_id"].is_unique, "join: not one row per place"
    assert not out["settlement_row"].dropna().duplicated().any(), "join: a settlement matched twice"
    return out

def starts_before(year, precision, cutoff: int = PRE_WAR_CUTOFF) -> str:
    """Does a (possibly fuzzy) year fall before ``cutoff``?  ``yes / no / ambiguous / unknown``."""
    if precision not in _SPAN_OF or pd.isna(year):
        return "unknown"
    earliest, latest = int(year), int(year) + _SPAN_OF[precision]
    if latest < cutoff:
        return "yes"
    if earliest >= cutoff:
        return "no"
    return "ambiguous"

def first_record_period(year, precision) -> str:
    """The period a place's first report falls in, for the distribution table.

    An exact year goes to its bin.  A decade does too, except ``191x`` — the one decade
    the 1914 line cuts — which is shown as its own row rather than assigned to a side.
    """
    if pd.isna(year) or precision not in _SPAN_OF:
        return "not recorded"
    if precision == "century":
        return "century only"
    if precision == "decade" and int(year) == 1910:
        return "191x (decade only)"
    return _PERIOD_LABELS[int(np.searchsorted(_PERIOD_EDGES, int(year), side="right")) - 1]

def place_dates(places: pd.DataFrame, ensembles: pd.DataFrame,
                cutoff: int = PRE_WAR_CUTOFF) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per place: how many ensembles, and whether theatre is recorded before ``cutoff``.

    ``ensemble_pre`` is True when at least one ensemble certainly starts before the
    cutoff; ``ensemble_ambiguous`` when none certainly does but one may (``191x``);
    ``first_record_pre`` reads the place page's own 'První zpráva'.  Key ``geo_id``.
    """
    E = ensembles.copy()
    E["pre"] = [starts_before(y, p, cutoff) for y, p in zip(E["year_from"], E["year_from_precision"])]
    per_place = E.groupby("geo_id").agg(
        n_ensembles=("ensemble_id", "size"),
        n_pre=("pre", lambda s: int((s == "yes").sum())),
        n_ambiguous=("pre", lambda s: int((s == "ambiguous").sum())),
        n_undated=("pre", lambda s: int((s == "unknown").sum())),
    )
    out = places[["geo_id"]].merge(per_place, on="geo_id", how="left", validate="1:1")
    counts = ["n_ensembles", "n_pre", "n_ambiguous", "n_undated"]
    out[counts] = out[counts].fillna(0).astype(int)
    out["ensemble_pre"] = out["n_pre"] > 0
    out["ensemble_ambiguous"] = (out["n_pre"] == 0) & (out["n_ambiguous"] > 0)
    first = [starts_before(y, p, cutoff) for y, p in
             zip(places["first_record_year"], places["first_record_precision"])]
    out["first_record_pre"] = [f == "yes" for f in first]
    out["first_record_known"] = [f != "unknown" for f in first]
    assert len(out) == len(places)
    return out

def association_counts(ensembles: pd.DataFrame, cutoff: int = PRE_WAR_CUTOFF) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series]:
    """Counts of pre-``cutoff`` ensembles by association, and the unclassified names.

    Returns:
        ``(counts, unclassified)`` — counts has one row per label plus *unclassified*,
        *more than one label* and *all pre-1914 ensembles*; ``unclassified`` is the
        frequency table of the names nothing matched, so the remainder can be read.
    """
    E = ensembles.drop_duplicates("ensemble_id").copy()
    E = E[[starts_before(y, p, cutoff) == "yes" for y, p in zip(E["year_from"], E["year_from_precision"])]]
    labels = E["name"].map(classify_association)
    rows = [(label, int(labels.map(lambda found, lab=label: lab in found).sum()))
            for label in ASSOCIATION_PATTERNS]
    rows += [("unclassified", int((labels.str.len() == 0).sum())),
             ("more than one label", int((labels.str.len() > 1).sum())),
             (f"all ensembles starting before {cutoff}", len(E))]
    counts = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["association", "ensembles"])
    counts["share"] = (counts["ensembles"] / max(len(E), 1)).round(3)
    return counts, E.loc[labels.str.len() == 0, "name"].value_counts()

def year_span(token: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """``1873`` → (1873, 1873); ``187x`` → (1870, 1879); ``18xx`` → (1800, 1899)."""
    tok = token.strip()
    if tok[-2:].lower() == "xx":
        return int(tok[:2]) * 100, int(tok[:2]) * 100 + 99
    if tok[-1].lower() == "x":
        return int(tok[:3]) * 10, int(tok[:3]) * 10 + 9
    return int(tok), int(tok)

def infer_century(decade: int, context_year) -> int | None:
    """The century of a bare ``80. léta``, from the line above it.

    The chronicle runs forward in time, so the decade is put in the earliest century that
    does not end it before the last dated line: after a 1977 line, ``V 80. letech`` is the
    1980s.  With nothing dated above it there is no reading, and None is returned.
    """
    if context_year is None or pd.isna(context_year):
        return None
    for century in range(1500, 2100, 100):
        if century + decade + 9 >= int(context_year):
            return century
    return None

def parse_leading_date(line: str, context_year=None) -> dict:
    """The date a chronicle line opens with, as start/end intervals and a ``date_form``.

    Only the **leading** date is read — a later year inside the line (``1934 22
    představení, 1935 19``) is the line's content, not its date.  Forms: ``year`` /
    ``decade`` / ``century`` (one printed year), ``range``, ``season`` (``1911/12``),
    ``list`` (``1887 a 1912``), ``from``, ``until``, ``before``, ``after``, ``circa``,
    ``period`` (a century or decade phrase), ``era`` (the wars, the First Republic).
    ``context_year`` is the last dated line above, used only to give a bare ``80. léta``
    its century (``century_inferred``).  No date: every field empty, ``date_form`` None.
    """
    text = (line or "").strip()
    for pattern, start, end in _ERA_PATTERNS:
        if (m := pattern.match(text)):
            return _date("era", m.group(0), start=start, end=end or (np.nan, np.nan))
    if (m := _PERIOD.match(text)):
        return _period(m, context_year)
    if (m := _WORD_YEAR.match(text)):
        return _word_year(m)
    if (date := _numeric(text)):
        return date
    # an ensemble's abbreviation before its years: `ŠS 1932 - 1938`, `LS 1928-1929`
    if (m := _ABBREVIATION_FIRST.match(text)) and (date := _numeric(text[m.end():])):
        return date
    return dict(_NO_DATE)

def attests_before(start_lo, start_hi, end_lo, end_hi, cutoff: int = PRE_WAR_CUTOFF) -> str:
    """Does a dated line put theatre activity before ``cutoff``?  ``yes / no / ambiguous / unknown``.

    With a start: *yes* if it certainly began before the cutoff, *no* if certainly not.
    With only an end (``do 1910``): the activity was going on before that end, so *yes*
    if the end is before the cutoff — otherwise *ambiguous*, never *no*.
    """
    if _is_known(start_lo) or _is_known(start_hi):
        lo = start_lo if _is_known(start_lo) else -np.inf
        hi = start_hi if _is_known(start_hi) else np.inf
        return "yes" if hi < cutoff else "no" if lo >= cutoff else "ambiguous"
    if _is_known(end_hi):
        return "yes" if end_hi < cutoff else "ambiguous"
    return "unknown"

def chronicle_line_kind(line: str) -> str | None:
    """``separator`` / ``heading`` / ``citation`` / ``admin``, or None for a note.

    A *citation* is a periodical and a full date and nothing else (``Moravský deník
    13.9.1935.``) — the source of the line above, dated by publication.  *Admin* is the
    database's own note on which okres the place belongs to now (``Od 1. 1. 2007 okres
    Praha-východ``), which opens with a date but is no event.
    """
    text = line.strip()
    if _SEPARATOR.match(text):
        return "separator"
    if not re.search(r"\d", text) and len(text) <= 45 and (
            text.endswith(":") or text.isupper() or _HEADING_START.match(text)):
        return "heading"
    if _CITATION.match(text):
        return "citation"
    if len(text) < 120 and _ADMIN.search(text):
        return "admin"
    return None

def read_chronicle(geo_id: int, text: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Every non-blank line of one place's chronicle, classified and dated.

    ``kind`` is ``event`` (a note with a leading date), ``undated`` (a note without one —
    often a continuation of the line above), or one of :func:`chronicle_line_kind`'s.  A
    heading opens a ``section`` (``puppet`` for *Loutkové divadlo*), which holds until the
    next heading.  ``associations`` are the :data:`ASSOCIATION_PATTERNS` labels the line
    names, ``|``-joined, and ``ambiguous_abbreviations`` any of them that rest on an
    abbreviation the key reads two ways (``ČOS``); ``umdoc`` marks a line naming the
    national union of amateur theatres; ``puppet`` marks puppet theatre, by section or by
    the line's words.
    """
    rows, section, context = [], "main", None
    for line_no, raw in enumerate(text.splitlines()):
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        kind = chronicle_line_kind(line)
        date = dict(_NO_DATE) if kind in ("separator", "heading") else parse_leading_date(line, context)
        if kind in ("heading", "separator"):    # a new block starts its own chronology
            context = None
        if kind == "heading":
            section = "puppet" if _PUPPET.search(line) else line.rstrip(":").strip().casefold()
        if kind is None:
            kind = "event" if _anchor_year(date) is not None else "undated"
        if kind == "event":
            context = _anchor_year(date)
        if kind == "citation":
            year = int(_CITATION.match(line).group("y"))
            date = _date("publication", line, start=(year, year))
        notes = kind in ("event", "undated")
        rows.append({"geo_id": geo_id, "line_no": line_no, "kind": kind, "section": section,
                     **date,
                     "associations": "|".join(classify_association(line)) if notes else "",
                     "ambiguous_abbreviations":
                         "|".join(dict.fromkeys(_AMBIGUOUS.findall(line))) if notes else "",
                     "umdoc": notes and bool(_UMDOC.search(line)),
                     "puppet": notes and (section == "puppet" or bool(_PUPPET.search(line))),
                     "text": line})
    return rows

def chronicle_lines(places: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The chronicle of every place as one table — key ``(geo_id, line_no)``, asserted.

    ``line_no`` is the line's position in the place's ``chronicle_text`` (0-based, blank
    lines counted), so any row leads back to its text.  The events are the rows with
    ``kind == "event"`` (:func:`chronicle_events`).  The text is the database's own and,
    like ``places.csv``, never leaves ``data/``.
    """
    rows = []
    for geo_id, text in zip(places["geo_id"], places["chronicle_text"]):
        if isinstance(text, str):
            rows.extend(read_chronicle(int(geo_id), text))
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=CHRONICLE_COLUMNS)
    assert not out.duplicated(["geo_id", "line_no"]).any(), "chronicle: key not unique"
    out["before_1914"] = [attests_before(*r) for r in
                          out[["start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo", "end_hi"]].itertuples(index=False)]
    out.loc[out["kind"] != "event", "before_1914"] = "unknown"
    return out

    """Per place: how many chronicle events, how many before 1914, which associations.

    bound = pre[["start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo", "end_hi"]].min(axis=1)
    per_place = pd.DataFrame({
        "n_events": events.groupby("geo_id").size(),
        "n_pre": pre.groupby("geo_id").size(),
        "n_ambiguous": events[events["before_1914"] == "ambiguous"].groupby("geo_id").size(),
        "n_pre_puppet": events[(events["before_1914"] == "yes") & events["puppet"]]
        .groupby("geo_id").size(),
        "earliest_pre_year": bound.groupby(pre["geo_id"]).min(),
        "associations_pre": pre.groupby("geo_id")["associations"].agg(
            lambda s: "|".join(sorted({a for v in s for a in v.split("|") if a}))),
        "ambiguous_abbreviation_pre": pre.groupby("geo_id")["ambiguous_abbreviations"].agg(
            lambda s: bool((s != "").any())),
        "umdoc_pre": pre.groupby("geo_id")["umdoc"].any(),
    })
    out = places[["geo_id"]].merge(per_place, left_on="geo_id", right_index=True,
                                   how="left", validate="1:1")
    counts = ["n_events", "n_pre", "n_ambiguous", "n_pre_puppet"]
    out[counts] = out[counts].fillna(0).astype(int)
    out["associations_pre"] = out["associations_pre"].fillna("")
    flags = ["ambiguous_abbreviation_pre", "umdoc_pre"]
    out[flags] = out[flags].astype("boolean").fillna(False).astype(bool)
    assert len(out) == len(places) and out["geo_id"].is_unique
    return out

def century_inference_check(lines: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
    """How often :func:`infer_century` would have been right where the century is printed.

    Takes every decade phrase that names its century (``V 80. letech 19. stol.``), drops
    the century, infers it from the dated line above as a bare one would be, and compares.
    """
    pattern = re.compile(r"(?P<d>\d0)\.?.*?(?:léta|let|letech|létech)\b\s*(?P<c>\d{1,2})\.", re.I)
    # the parser's context: the dated line above, inside the same block (headings and
    # separators start a new one)
    block = lines["kind"].isin(["heading", "separator"]).groupby(lines["geo_id"]).cumsum()
    events = lines.assign(block=block)[lines["kind"] == "event"].copy()
    events["anchor"] = events[["start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo", "end_hi"]].bfill(axis=1).iloc[:, 0]
    events["previous"] = events.groupby(["geo_id", "block"])["anchor"].shift()
    checked = right = 0
    for raw, inferred, previous in zip(events["date_raw"], events["century_inferred"],
                                       events["previous"]):
        m = pattern.search(raw or "") if not inferred else None
        if m is None or pd.isna(previous):
            continue
        checked += 1
        right += infer_century(int(m.group("d")), previous) == (int(m.group("c")) - 1) * 100
    return {"checked": checked, "right": right, "share_right": round(right / max(checked, 1), 3)}

    no_ensemble = ~dates.set_index("geo_id")["ensemble_pre"]
    print(f"\nplaces with a pre-1914 (non-puppet) chronicle event: {int(has_pre.sum()):,}"
          f" — of them with no ensemble certainly before 1914: {int((has_pre & no_ensemble).sum()):,}")
    pre = events[(events["before_1914"] == "yes") & ~events["puppet"]]
    labels = pre["associations"].str.split("|").explode()
    print("\n── pre-1914 events by association named (an event can name several)\n"
          + labels[labels != ""].value_counts().to_string()
          + f"\nnaming none: {int((pre['associations'] == '').sum()):,} of {len(pre):,}")
    print(f"pre-1914 events resting on an abbreviation read two ways (ČOS):"
          f" {int((pre['ambiguous_abbreviations'] != '').sum()):,};"
          f" naming ÚMDOČ: {int(pre['umdoc'].sum()):,}"
          f" (places: {int(summary['umdoc_pre'].sum()):,})")

def clause_cuts(line: str, context_year=None) -> list[int]:
    """Character offsets at which a line is cut into clauses (the first, 0, included)."""
    text = line or ""
    cuts = [0]
    if is_report(text):
        return cuts
    lead = parse_leading_date(text.strip(), context_year)
    lead_end = text.find(lead["date_raw"]) + len(lead["date_raw"]) if lead["date_raw"] else 0
    spans = _protected_spans(text)
    for m in _CLAUSE_BOUNDARY.finditer(text):
        at = m.end()
        if at <= lead_end or any(a <= m.start() < b for a, b in spans):
            continue
        if text[m.start()] == "." and _ends_abbreviation(text, m.start()):
            continue
        if parse_leading_date(_after_lead(text[at:]), context_year)["date_form"] is not None:
            cuts.append(at)
    return cuts

def split_clauses(line: str, line_date: dict | None = None, context_year=None) -> list[dict]:
    """One chronicle line as its dated clauses.

    The first clause carries the line's own date (``line_date``, the dict
    :func:`parse_leading_date` returns — ``date_source = "line"``, or ``"none"`` for an
    undated line); every later one starts with its own (``"own"``), and a bare decade in it
    takes its century from the clause before.  ``years_inside`` lists every other year the
    clause prints (``zanikl 1931``, a bracketed `zal. 1895`), ``years_listed`` the years of
    a leading list (``1910 a 1913`` — two years, not a span), ``date_only`` marks a clause
    that is nothing but its date (``…, 1907, 1910`` — the activity of the clause before,
    again).  A trailing periodical citation is moved to ``citation``.
    """
    text = (line or "").strip()
    report, citation = is_report(text), ""
    if (m := _TRAILING_CITATION.search(text)) and m.start() > 0:
        citation, text = m.group(0).strip(), text[:m.start()].rstrip()
    first = dict(line_date) if line_date is not None else parse_leading_date(text, context_year)
    cuts = [0] if report else clause_cuts(text, context_year)
    clauses, context = [], _anchor_year(first) if first["date_form"] else context_year
    for i, (a, b) in enumerate(zip(cuts, cuts[1:] + [len(text)])):
        piece = re.sub(r"[\s,;]+$", "", text[a:b]).strip()
        if i == 0:
            date, source = first, "line" if _anchor_year(first) is not None else "none"
        else:
            date, source = parse_leading_date(_after_lead(piece), context), "own"
            context = _anchor_year(date) if _anchor_year(date) is not None else context
        raw = date["date_raw"] or ""
        rest = piece[piece.find(raw) + len(raw):] if raw and raw in piece else piece
        listed = _YEAR_TOKEN.findall(raw) if date["date_form"] == "list" else []
        clauses.append({
            "clause_no": i, "date_source": source, **date,
            "years_listed": "|".join(listed),
            "years_inside": "|".join(_YEAR_TOKEN.findall(rest)),
            "date_only": bool(raw) and not re.search(r"\w", rest),
            "citation": citation if i == len(cuts) - 1 else "",
            "text": piece})
    return clauses

def chronicle_clauses(lines: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Every event and undated note of :func:`chronicle_lines` cut into dated clauses.

    Key ``(geo_id, line_no, clause_no)``, asserted; every line yields at least one clause
    and the clauses of a line, joined, give back its text less the trailing citation.  The
    first clause keeps the line's date exactly as :func:`chronicle_lines` read it.
    ``report`` marks a line kept whole (:func:`is_report`).  ``associations`` and
    ``puppet`` are the clause's own (a puppet section makes every clause in it puppet);
    the line's are in ``chronicle_lines``.  ``cues`` are :func:`event_cues`, not codes.
    """
    notes = lines[lines["kind"].isin(["event", "undated"])]
    date_cols = ["date_form", "date_raw", "start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo", "end_hi",
                 "century_inferred"]
    rows = []
    for r in notes.itertuples(index=False):
        line_date = {c: getattr(r, c) for c in date_cols}
        line_date["date_raw"] = line_date["date_raw"] if isinstance(line_date["date_raw"], str) else None
        line_date["date_form"] = line_date["date_form"] if isinstance(line_date["date_form"], str) else None
        context = _anchor_year(line_date) if line_date["date_form"] else None
        report = is_report(r.text)
        for clause in split_clauses(r.text, line_date, context):
            rows.append({
                "geo_id": r.geo_id, "line_no": r.line_no, "line_kind": r.kind,
                "section": r.section, "report": report, **clause,
                "associations": "|".join(classify_association(clause["text"])),
                "ambiguous_abbreviations": "|".join(dict.fromkeys(_AMBIGUOUS.findall(clause["text"]))),
                "puppet": r.section == "puppet" or bool(_PUPPET.search(clause["text"])),
                "cues": "|".join(event_cues(clause["text"], clause["date_raw"]))})
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=CLAUSE_COLUMNS)
    assert not out.duplicated(["geo_id", "line_no", "clause_no"]).any(), "clauses: key not unique"
    assert out[["geo_id", "line_no"]].drop_duplicates().shape[0] == len(notes), "clauses: a line lost"
    out["before_1914"] = [attests_before(*r) for r in
                          out[["start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo", "end_hi"]].itertuples(index=False)]
    return out

def title_spans(text: str, date_raw=None) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """Where a clause names a play: its quoted titles and a repertoire line's titles, as
    character spans of ``text``.  Words there are the title's, not the clause's."""
    # a quotation longer than a title (reported speech, a press extract) keeps its words
    spans = [m.span() for m in _QUOTED.finditer(text) if 2 <= len(m.group(0)) - 2 <= 80]
    rest, at = _rest(text, date_raw)
    for title, a, b in _repertoire_titles(rest, whole=True):
        # a title stops at a spaced dash, or at a comma before a lowercase word that is no
        # title's continuation (`aneb`, `čili`): what follows describes the play (`, hráno v sále`)
        stop = _TITLE_TAIL.search(title)
        spans.append((at + a, at + a + (stop.start() if stop else len(title))))
    return spans

def mask_titles(text: str, date_raw=None) -> str:
    """``text`` with its play titles (:func:`title_spans`) blanked, offsets kept: a venue word
    inside `Paní hostinská` or a ban inside `Zakázané ovoce` is no cue (D-254, rare case 7)."""
    chars = list(text)
    for a, b in title_spans(text, date_raw):
        chars[a:b] = " " * (b - a)
    return "".join(chars)

def hedge_applies(text, date_raw=None) -> bool:
    """Does the clause hedge its own theatre event (B4 as D-254 Q12 scopes it)?"""
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        return False
    masked = mask_titles(text, date_raw)
    later = _LATER_EVENT.search(masked) if isinstance(date_raw, str) and date_raw else None
    # a later event's hedge leaves the dated one standing only if the dated part is theatre
    lead_is_theatre = bool(later and _THEATRE_WORD.search(masked[:later.start()]))
    rest, _ = _rest(text, date_raw)
    bare = len(re.findall(r"\w+", rest)) <= LISTED_MAX_WORDS
    for m in EVENT_CUES["hedged"].finditer(masked):
        before, after = masked[:m.start()], masked[m.end():]
        if _HEDGE_ORDINAL.search(before) or _HEDGE_ON_DETAIL.match(after) \
                or (not bare and _HEDGE_AFTER_NAME.search(before)) \
                or (m.group(0) == "?" and not bare and _HEDGE_IN_NAME_BRACKET.search(before)):
            continue
        if later and m.start() > later.start() and lead_is_theatre:
            continue                           # a later event's hedge; the dated one stands
        return True
    return False

def event_cues(text, date_raw=None) -> list[str]

The EVENT_CUES types a clause's words point to (possibly none).

With date_raw (the clause's leading date) a clause that is a date and a short name and nothing any cue reads is listed — a company recorded as active — when the name is a body's (_BODY_WORD) or the date runs over years (a span or an open date: a play is not given for forty years); a single year and a name that may as well be a play (1903 Veselosť.) is name_only, which the model reads (D-254 Q8). The people a listing names (its director r. M. Štěpaník, its members) do not stop it being one (D-221: officers and members are LISTED_MAY_NAME). A date, an author and a play (1898 Josef Štolba: Na letním bytě) is a performance with its title instead, however long, when the author runs to at most AUTHOR_MAX_WORDS words (audit A3) — also beside other cues (a genre word, a venue, a benefit: 1898 v hostinci – Tyl: Paličova dcera), but not beside a permit, a ban or a pause, which are not a play staged (review of D-224).

D-254: words inside a play's title are no cue (mask_titles); hedged only where the hedge qualifies the event (hedge_applies); a pointer to a list elsewhere has no type; a building's founding (divadle (zal. 1860)) is no founded.

def event_cues(text, date_raw=None) -> list[str]:
    """The :data:`EVENT_CUES` types a clause's words point to (possibly none).

    With ``date_raw`` (the clause's leading date) a clause that is a date and a short name
    and nothing any cue reads is ``listed`` — a company recorded as active — when the name
    is a body's (:data:`_BODY_WORD`) or the date runs over years (a span or an open date: a
    play is not given for forty years); a single year and a name that may as well be a play
    (`1903 Veselosť.`) is ``name_only``, which the model reads (D-254 Q8).  The people a
    listing names (its director `r. M. Štěpaník`, its members) do not stop it being one
    (D-221: ``officers`` and ``members`` are :data:`LISTED_MAY_NAME`).  A date, an author
    and a play (``1898 Josef Štolba: Na letním bytě``) is a ``performance`` with its
    ``title`` instead, however long, when the author runs to at most
    :data:`AUTHOR_MAX_WORDS` words (audit A3) — also beside other cues (a genre word, a venue,
    a benefit: `1898 v hostinci – Tyl: Paličova dcera`), but not beside a permit, a ban or a
    pause, which are not a play staged (review of D-224).

    D-254: words inside a play's title are no cue (:func:`mask_titles`); ``hedged`` only
    where the hedge qualifies the event (:func:`hedge_applies`); a pointer to a list
    elsewhere has no type; a building's founding (`divadle (zal. 1860)`) is no ``founded``.
    """
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        return []
    if _POINTER.search(text):
        rest = _POINTER.sub(" ", _rest(text, date_raw)[0])
        if _POINTER_CLAUSE.match(text) or len(re.findall(r"\w+", rest)) <= 2:
            return []                          # the clause is a pointer to a list: nothing (rare case 108)
        text = _POINTER.sub(lambda m: " " * len(m.group(0)), text)   # the pointer cut out, offsets kept
    masked = mask_titles(text, date_raw)
    found = [label for label, pattern in EVENT_CUES.items()
             if label not in ("title", "hedged") and pattern.search(masked)]
    # rare case 3: in a cast list (`Kryšpína hrál Václav Kadlec`) `hrál` names a member's role
    if "active" in found and not EVENT_CUES["active"].search(_CAST_LIST.sub(lambda m: " " * len(m.group(0)), masked)):
        found.remove("active")
    if EVENT_CUES["title"].search(text):
        found.append("title")
    if "founded" in found and not EVENT_CUES["founded"].search(_BUILDING_FOUNDED.sub(" ", masked)):
        found.remove("founded")
    # Q4, read both ways: German plays named as not played (`usnesla nehrát německé hry`) are no
    # German theatre, as Czech ones named as forbidden are no Czech theatre
    if "german" in found and all(_negated(masked, m) for m in EVENT_CUES["german"].finditer(masked)):
        found.remove("german")
    # D-254 Q3, as written: plays given vaguely in the plural (`mnohá představení`) or over a
    # span, with no title or number, is players active, not a particular performance
    if "performance" in found and not {"title", "count"} & set(found):
        over_span = isinstance(date_raw, str) and bool(date_raw) and (
            _date_kind(date_raw) == "span" or bool(_OPEN_DATE.match(date_raw))) and not _PERFORMANCE_VERB.search(masked)
        particular = bool(_PARTICULAR_PLAY.search(text)) or bool(_repertoire_entry(_rest(text, date_raw)[0]))
        if (over_span or _VAGUE_PLURAL.search(masked)) and not particular:
            found.remove("performance")
            if "active" not in found:
                found.append("active")
    if hedge_applies(text, date_raw):
        found.append("hedged")
    if isinstance(date_raw, str) and date_raw:
        rest = text[text.find(date_raw) + len(date_raw):] if date_raw in text else text
        words = re.findall(r"\w+", rest)
        bare = not set(found) - {"hedged", "title", "company_note", *LISTED_MAY_NAME}   # a note: see below
        # beside other cues, only when a play is actually parsed (second review of D-224)
        staged = not set(found) & NOT_STAGED and not _PLANNED.search(text)
        if staged and _repertoire_entry(rest) and (bare or repertoire_plays(rest)):
            found += [label for label in ("performance", "title") if label not in found]
        elif bare and 0 < len(words) <= LISTED_MAX_WORDS and "title" not in found \
                and ("company_note" not in found or _BODY_WORD.search(rest)):
            # a body's name, or a date over years (`1851-1893 Thalia`, `Od 1885 …`): a company
            over_years = _date_kind(date_raw) == "span" or bool(_OPEN_DATE.match(date_raw))
            found.append("listed" if _BODY_WORD.search(rest) or over_years else "name_only")
            if "company_note" in found and _BODY_WORD.search(rest):
                found.remove("company_note")        # `1909 Hospodářská beseda.` names a body
    return found

def cue_table(clauses: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Pre-1914 non-puppet clauses by cue type, with the remainder no cue reaches.

    ``hedged`` and ``title`` are attributes, so a clause carrying only them counts as
    having no type.
    """
    pre = clauses[(clauses["before_1914"] == "yes") & ~clauses["puppet"]]
    cues = pd.Series([event_cues(t, d) for t, d in zip(pre["text"], pre["date_raw"])],
                     index=pre.index)
    rows = [(label, int(cues.map(lambda found, lab=label: lab in found).sum()))
            for label in [*EVENT_CUES, "listed"]]
    typed = cues.map(lambda found: bool(set(found) - {"hedged", "title"}))
    rows += [("no type (only an attribute, or nothing)", int((~typed).sum())),
             ("pre-1914 non-puppet clauses", len(pre))]
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["cue", "clauses"])
    out["share"] = (out["clauses"] / max(len(pre), 1)).round(3)
    return out

def clause_report(clauses: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    """Print what the splitter did: lines cut, clauses per line, the pre-1914 yield."""
    per_line = clauses.groupby(["geo_id", "line_no"]).size()
    print("\n── chronicle clauses: lines by number of clauses\n"
          + per_line.value_counts().sort_index().to_string())
    print(f"lines kept whole as reports: {int(clauses.drop_duplicates(['geo_id', 'line_no'])['report'].sum()):,}")
    print("\n── clauses by where their date comes from\n"
          + clauses["date_source"].value_counts().to_string())
    pre = clauses[(clauses["before_1914"] == "yes") & ~clauses["puppet"]]
    lines_pre = clauses[(clauses["clause_no"] == 0) & (clauses["before_1914"] == "yes") & ~clauses["puppet"]]
    print(f"\npre-1914 non-puppet clauses: {len(pre):,} (from the lines' own dates alone: {len(lines_pre):,})"
          f"; in {pre['geo_id'].nunique():,} places")
    undated = clauses[(clauses["date_source"] == "none") & clauses["years_inside"].ne("")]
    early = undated["years_inside"].map(lambda s: any(int(y[:4].replace("x", "0")) < PRE_WAR_CUTOFF
                                                      for y in s.split("|")))
    print(f"undated clauses printing a year inside: {len(undated):,}, a pre-1914 one: {int(early.sum()):,}")

def names_company(text) -> bool:
    """Does the clause name a local amateur theatre body (Q1)?  An umbrella union's name is
    read out first, so `Ústřední matice divadelního ochotnictva` alone names none."""
    if not isinstance(text, str):

def czech_named(text, titles_raw: list[str] | tuple = ()) -> bool:
    """Does the clause name Czech *played* (B8 as D-254 Q4 reads it)?  A Czech word for the
    plays or players that does not stand by a negation (`české hry nepovolovány`), or a
    title spelt with a letter only Czech uses — a Czech repertoire with one German title
    is Czech."""
    if any(isinstance(t, str) and _CZECH_LETTERS.search(t) for t in titles_raw):
        return True
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        return False
    return any(not _negated(text, m) for m in _CZECH_WORD.finditer(text))

def code_clause(text: str, date_raw, types: list[str]) -> dict

What the rules read in one clause beyond its cue types.

end_inside is an end year printed after the leading date (činný do 1938); count_stated the performances it numbers in its own time: performances and plays are each summed (2 hry a 3 operety is 5) and the larger taken, never added (28 premiér, 128 představení is 128, a play being performed at least once); a number after z toho is part of one before it and is not counted; a running total or an ordinal (dosud sehráno 127, jako 51. představení) is no count (audit A4); titles the play titles, as keys — quoted, or after the author of a repertoire entry (Josef Štolba: Na letním bytě, audit A3); attendance_n the largest audience it numbers; bilingual a German clause that also names Czech. D-254: end_inside is the last end printed; start_inside an earlier start printed for the theatre (již od roku 1860 in a line of 1868, Q6); czech_named the clause names Czech played (czech_named, Q4).

def code_clause(text: str, date_raw, types: list[str]) -> dict:
    """What the rules read in one clause beyond its cue types.

    ``end_inside`` is an end year printed after the leading date (``činný do 1938``);
    ``count_stated`` the performances it numbers in its own time: performances and plays are
    each summed (``2 hry a 3 operety`` is 5) and the larger taken, never added (``28 premiér,
    128 představení`` is 128, a play being performed at least once); a number after ``z toho``
    is part of one before it and is not counted; a running total or an ordinal (``dosud
    sehráno 127``, ``jako 51. představení``) is no count (audit A4); ``titles`` the play
    titles, as keys — quoted, or after the author of a repertoire entry (``Josef Štolba: Na
    letním bytě``, audit A3);
    ``attendance_n`` the largest audience it numbers; ``bilingual`` a German clause that
    also names Czech.  D-254: ``end_inside`` is the *last* end printed; ``start_inside`` an
    earlier start printed for the theatre (`již od roku 1860` in a line of 1868, Q6);
    ``czech_named`` the clause names Czech played (:func:`czech_named`, Q4).
    """
    raw = date_raw if isinstance(date_raw, str) else ""
    rest = text[text.find(raw) + len(raw):] if raw and raw in text else text
    lead = [int(y) for y in re.findall(_YEAR4, raw)]
    ends = [m for m in _END_INSIDE.finditer(rest) if not lead or int(m.group(1)) >= max(lead)]
    end = ends[-1] if ends else None
    earlier = [int(y) for y in _START_INSIDE.findall(rest) if lead and int(y) < min(lead)]
    audience = [int(n) for n in _ATTENDANCE_NUMBER.findall(rest)]
    quoted_raw = [next(g for g in m.groups() if g) for m in _QUOTED_TITLE.finditer(text)]
    titles = {_title_key(t) for t in quoted_raw}
    kind = "open" if _cut_short(raw, rest) else _date_kind(raw)
    # the plays of a repertoire entry, read for the clause's own year (review of D-224: also
    # beside a quoted phrase, which may be praise, `„výtečně provedeny“`, not a title)
    year = int(re.search(_YEAR4, raw).group(1)) if kind == "point" else None
    plays_raw = [t for t, _, _ in _repertoire_titles(rest, year)] if {"performance", "title"} & set(types) else []
    plays = [_title_key(t) for t in plays_raw]
    if plays:
        titles = set(plays)               # a repertoire line's titles are its plays, not its quotes
    titles = sorted(titles)
    # a season the date read cut short is stored as its first year, which the number
    # outruns (`1880-81 … 34 představení` would all land in 1880): no year's count; nor on a
    # list of years, each a point of its own (`1905 a 1907 sehráli 10 her` is not 10 a year)
    count = _stated_count(rest, kind)
    # a repertoire line of n plays is at least n performances — unless the clause says its
    # numbers are not this year's (a rate, a running total, another year: the same refusals
    # as a stated number's, second review of D-224) or that the plays were only planned
    # read up to where the line passes to another stretch, as the plays are
    stretch = _OTHER_STRETCH.search(rest)
    scope = rest[:stretch.start()] if stretch else rest
    refused = kind == "point" and (_COUNT_PERIOD.search(scope) or _ALREADY.search(scope)
                                   or _ORDINAL.search(scope) or _another_year_before_count(scope))
    if pd.isna(count) and len(plays) >= 2 and kind in ("point", "span") and not refused \
            and not _PLANNED.search(text):
        count = float(len(plays))
    # a quoted name is a play's title only after a play word (`hru „Loupež“`); an inn's name is not
    play_quotes = [next(g for g in m.groups() if g) for m in _QUOTED_TITLE.finditer(text)
                   if _PLAY_BEFORE_QUOTE.search(text[max(0, m.start() - 30):m.start()])]
    czech = czech_named(text, play_quotes + plays_raw)
    return {"end_inside": int(end.group(1)) if end else np.nan,
            "start_inside": float(min(earlier)) if earlier else np.nan,
            "count_stated": count,
            "titles": "|".join(t for t in titles if t),
            "attendance_n": max(audience) if audience else np.nan,
            "czech_named": czech,
            "bilingual": "german" in types and czech}

def code_clauses(clauses: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame

chronicle_clauses with the rulings applied (D-141): one row per clause, same key.

Adds code_clause's fields and czech_activity — the clause puts Czech amateur theatre in its place: some type has an Activity role (a quoted title is a performance), or it is a company's act or end (D-221, below); and it is not German or Latin unless it also names Czech players or plays (B8 as amended by D-221: a Czech company that also plays in German is Czech activity, recorded as bilingual), not puppet theatre, and not school or church theatre before 1848 unless the plays are Czech (B6 as amended by D-221; one that may straddle 1848 counts, and is possible only by its interval); company — it records a company over time (listed, active, founded, statutes), or a company's act (D-221: officers, members, a merger, a stage of its own — on the company's own page; the first three on a place's chronicle when a theatre company is named); company_act marks a clause that is company evidence by D-221 alone, which is a point in time and never open-ended; hedged — read as possible only (B4), and so is a company's end recorded with no other activity (D-221: a dissolution is often formal, years after the last play); needs_model — the rules leave it open: an undated clause printing a year inside (B11), or a dated one no type reaches.

As the codebook rulings of D-254 amend it (Q-numbers of reference/places/theatre_codebook_rulings.csv):

  • company, on a place's chronicle (Q1) — active is company evidence only when the clause names a local theatre body (names_company); a founding or statutes only when the body founded is not another kind (a DTJ, a choir: _OTHER_BODY); school, student, church or travelling players and an umbrella union are never a company unless a local company is named beside them;
  • company, on a company's own page (Q5, Q7, Q13) — every dated note of the page's company is its act, a point in its year: a play, a list of titles, a meeting, an evening, its end; not one that names another performer (a travelling company, the model's named_group); a hired hall alone (venue) is the company's act with its theatre possible only (activity_hedged, rare case 127);
  • Czech (Q4) — czech_named; pre-1848 school or church theatre of unstated language is Czech activity possible only and never a company;
  • a decline is activity, possible only (Q11); name_only activity, no company (Q8);
  • a body founded and theatre taken up postupně / později starts after the founding (after: possible, certain in no year, Q10);
  • needs_model also for a dated clause printing other years (Q6) and a name_only (Q8);
  • the model's readings (amateur_theatre_model.apply_readings) add performer_kind (Q1, Q7), elsewhere — theatre played in another place, which counts nowhere here (Q7) — and model_titles_raw (Q4), when present.

def code_clauses(clauses: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """:func:`chronicle_clauses` with the rulings applied (D-141): one row per clause, same key.

    Adds :func:`code_clause`'s fields and
    ``czech_activity`` — the clause puts *Czech* amateur theatre in its place: some type
    has an Activity role (a quoted title is a performance), or it is a company's act or end
    (D-221, below); and it is not German or Latin unless it also names Czech players or
    plays (B8 as amended by D-221: a Czech company that also plays in German is Czech
    activity, recorded as bilingual), not puppet theatre, and not school or church theatre
    before 1848 unless the plays are Czech (B6 as amended by D-221; one that may straddle
    1848 counts, and is possible only by its interval);
    ``company`` — it records a company over time (listed, active, founded, statutes), or a
    company's act (D-221: officers, members, a merger, a stage of its own — on the
    company's own page; the first three on a place's chronicle when a theatre company is
    named); ``company_act`` marks a clause that is company evidence by D-221 alone, which
    is a point in time and never open-ended;
    ``hedged`` — read as possible only (B4), and so is a company's end recorded with no
    other activity (D-221: a dissolution is often formal, years after the last play);
    ``needs_model`` — the rules leave it open: an undated clause printing a year inside
    (B11), or a dated one no type reaches.

    As the codebook rulings of D-254 amend it (Q-numbers of
    ``reference/places/theatre_codebook_rulings.csv``):

    * *company, on a place's chronicle* (Q1) — ``active`` is company evidence only when the
      clause names a local theatre body (:func:`names_company`); a founding or statutes
      only when the body founded is not another kind (a DTJ, a choir: :data:`_OTHER_BODY`);
      school, student, church or travelling players and an umbrella union are never a
      company unless a local company is named beside them;
    * *company, on a company's own page* (Q5, Q7, Q13) — every dated note of the page's
      company is its act, a point in its year: a play, a list of titles, a meeting, an
      evening, its end; not one that names another performer (a travelling company, the
      model's ``named_group``); a hired hall alone (``venue``) is the company's act with its
      theatre possible only (``activity_hedged``, rare case 127);
    * *Czech* (Q4) — :func:`czech_named`; pre-1848 school or church theatre of unstated
      language is Czech activity *possible only* and never a company;
    * a ``decline`` is activity, possible only (Q11); ``name_only`` activity, no company (Q8);
    * a body founded and theatre taken up ``postupně`` / ``později`` starts after the
      founding (``after``: possible, certain in no year, Q10);
    * ``needs_model`` also for a dated clause printing other years (Q6) and a ``name_only`` (Q8);
    * the model's readings (:func:`amateur_theatre_model.apply_readings`) add
      ``performer_kind`` (Q1, Q7), ``elsewhere`` — theatre played in another place, which
      counts nowhere here (Q7) — and ``model_titles_raw`` (Q4), when present.
    """
    out = clauses.copy()
    types = out["cues"].fillna("").str.split("|").map(lambda t: [x for x in t if x])
    coded = pd.DataFrame([code_clause(t, d, ty) for t, d, ty in zip(out["text"], out["date_raw"], types)],
                         index=out.index, columns=CODE_CLAUSE_FIELDS)
    out = pd.concat([out.drop(columns=[c for c in coded if c in out]), coded], axis=1)
    has = lambda name: types.map(lambda t, n=name: n in t)                      # noqa: E731
    any_of = lambda names: types.map(lambda t, s=frozenset(names): bool(s & set(t)))   # noqa: E731
    activity = types.map(lambda t: bool(ACTIVITY_TYPES & (set(t) | ({"performance"} if "title" in t else set()))))
    text = out["text"].fillna("")
    blank = pd.Series(False, index=out.index)
    czech = out["czech_named"].astype(bool)
    if "model_titles_raw" in out:
        czech |= out["model_titles_raw"].fillna("").map(lambda s: bool(_CZECH_LETTERS.search(str(s))))
    on_page = (out["ensemble_id"].notna() if "ensemble_id" in out else blank).astype(bool)
    performer = out["performer_kind"].fillna("") if "performer_kind" in out else pd.Series("", index=out.index)
    named = text.map(names_company)
    umbrella = text.str.contains(_UMBRELLA) & ~named
    other_body = text.str.contains(_OTHER_BODY) & ~named
    # Q1: players who are no local company, on a place's chronicle
    not_local = ~on_page & (((has("school_church") | has("travelling") | umbrella) & ~named)
                            | performer.isin(NOT_LOCAL_PERFORMERS))
    # Q7, Q13: on a company's page, a clause that names another performer is not the page's —
    # also plain amateurs on the page of a body that is no theatre company (`zde ochotníci h.
    # operu` on a singing society's page, clause 137 of the blind check)
    ensemble_name = out["ensemble_name"].fillna("") if "ensemble_name" in out else pd.Series("", index=out.index)
    page_not_theatre = on_page & ensemble_name.str.contains(_OTHER_BODY) & ~ensemble_name.map(names_company) \
        & ~ensemble_name.str.contains(r"(?i:\bdivadl\w*|\bdivadeln\w*|\bochotn\w*)")
    # amateurs the clause does not tie to the page's own body (no `spolkoví`, no `ochotnický
    # odbor`, no word of the page's name); the model's `page_ensemble` overrides the text
    tied = pd.Series([_tied_to_page(t, n) for t, n in zip(text, ensemble_name)], index=out.index, dtype=bool)
    amateurs = performer.eq("unnamed_amateurs") | (
        text.str.contains(r"(?i:\bochotn\w*)") & ~tied & ~performer.eq("page_ensemble"))
    # another body organised or gave it, or another kind of body was founded (clause 34; a DTJ founding)
    organiser = pd.Series([_other_organiser(t, n) for t, n in zip(text, ensemble_name)], index=out.index, dtype=bool)
    other_founding = any_of({"founded", "statutes"}) & text.str.contains(_OTHER_BODY) & ~named \
        & ~ensemble_name.str.contains(_OTHER_BODY)
    other_performer = on_page & (performer.isin(OTHER_PERFORMERS) | (has("travelling") & ~named)
                                 | (page_not_theatre & amateurs) | organiser | other_founding)
    # a short line that names only people (`1907 předseda Jan Khom.`) is read as `listed`
    # (D-141), but it records an act, not a company existing on: a point, as D-221's acts are
    named_listing = has("listed") & (has("officers") | has("members"))
    founding = any_of({"founded", "statutes"}) & ~other_body
    place_strict = (has("active") & named) | founding | (has("listed") & ~named_listing)
    # a play, a count or a cast list beside `active` is a dated act, a point — not a company recorded on (Q13)
    page_strict = (has("active") & ~any_of({"performance", "title", "count", "members"})) \
        | any_of({"founded", "statutes"}) | (has("listed") & ~named_listing)
    strict_company = (~on_page & place_strict & ~not_local) | (on_page & page_strict & ~other_performer)
    # D-221 on a place's chronicle; D-254 Q5/Q13 on a company's page: any dated note of it
    typed = types.map(lambda t: bool(set(t) - {"hedged"}))
    dated = out["date_source"].ne("none") | out["start_lo"].notna() | out["start_hi"].notna() | out["end_hi"].notna()
    place_act = ~on_page & named & any_of(PLACE_COMPANY_ACT_TYPES) & ~not_local
    pause_alone = has("pause") & types.map(lambda t: not ((ACTIVITY_TYPES - {"active"}) & set(t)))
    page_act = on_page & typed & dated & ~other_performer & ~pause_alone
    act = place_act | page_act
    ended_alone = has("ended") & (on_page | named) & ~activity
    # Q10: a body founded, then theatre taken up gradually or later — a start after the founding
    later_start = has("founded") & ~named & text.str.contains(_LATER_THEATRE) & out["start_lo"].notna()
    out.loc[later_start, "start_hi"] = np.nan
    out.loc[later_start, "date_form"] = "after"
    # B6 as D-254 Q4 reads it: pre-1848 school or church theatre of unstated language is possible
    early_school = has("school_church") & (out["start_hi"] < SCHOOL_CHURCH_FROM) & ~czech
    # Latin school drama is a thing of the years before 1848; after, `latina` is a play's
    # title (Myslivecká latina), not the language played
    latin = has("latin") & (out["start_hi"] < SCHOOL_CHURCH_FROM)
    foreign = (has("german") | latin) & ~czech
    elsewhere = out["elsewhere"].fillna(False).astype(bool) if "elsewhere" in out else blank
    # Q1: a theatre union of the district (`Divadelní župa Pojizerská, 25 jednot`) is theatre
    # there — activity, never a company
    union_theatre = text.str.contains(_UMBRELLA) & text.str.contains(r"(?i:\bdivadeln\w*|\bochotn\w*)") & dated
    out["czech_activity"] = (activity | act | ended_alone | union_theatre) & ~foreign & ~out["puppet"] & ~elsewhere
    out["company"] = (strict_company | (named_listing & ~not_local & ~other_performer) | act) \
        & ~out["puppet"] & ~foreign & ~early_school & ~has("name_only").where(~on_page, False) & ~elsewhere
    out["company"] &= ~(later_start & ~on_page)
    out["company_act"] = out["company"] & ~strict_company
    out["performance"] = (has("performance") | has("title") | has("count")) & ~elsewhere
    decline_alone = has("decline") & ~any_of({"performance", "title", "count", "founded", "statutes", "listed"})
    out["hedged"] = has("hedged") | ended_alone | decline_alone | early_school
    # rare case 127: a hall the company hired, and nothing else — the company that year, its plays unknown in time
    venue_alone = types.map(lambda t: set(t) - {"hedged"} == {"venue"})
    titled = pd.Series([bool(title_spans(t, d)) for t, d in zip(text, out["date_raw"])], index=out.index, dtype=bool)
    hall_only = venue_alone & text.str.contains(_HALL) & ~text.str.contains(_STAGE_OR_PLAY) & ~titled
    out["activity_hedged"] = hall_only & act
    no_type = types.map(lambda t: not (set(t) - {"hedged", "title"})) | (
        ~on_page & types.map(lambda t: not (set(t) - {"hedged", "title", "company_note"})))
    # Q6: a dated clause that prints other years than its date's — the model reads them
    other_years = [_other_years(y, lo, hi, ehi, elo) for y, lo, hi, ehi, elo in
                   zip(out["years_inside"].fillna(""), out["start_lo"], out["start_hi"], out["end_hi"], out["end_lo"])]
    permit_title = has("permit") & ~has("title") & text.str.contains(r"\bhr[auy]\s+[A-ZČŘŠŽÚ]")
    out["needs_model"] = ((out["date_source"] == "none") & out["years_inside"].fillna("").ne("")) | (
        (out["date_source"] != "none") & (no_type | has("name_only") | permit_title
                                          | pd.Series(other_years, index=out.index)))
    for column in ("founded", "statutes", "permit", "first", "proceeds", "national_theatre",
                   "school_church", "travelling", "german", "latin", "attendance"):
        out[column] = has(column)
    out["elsewhere"] = elsewhere
    # B12 as the audit narrowed it (A2): a pause is a clause that records the pause and no
    # other activity — `činnost přerušena` names the activity it pauses (`active`), but
    # `1885 založen, později přerušena` is a founding first and dates the founding
    out["pause"] = has("pause") & types.map(lambda t: not ((ACTIVITY_TYPES - {"active"}) & set(t)))
    # and such a clause is what the codebook rules a pause, coded only: not activity, not a company
    out.loc[out["pause"], ["czech_activity", "company", "company_act", "activity_hedged"]] = False
    return out

def active_decade_list(value) -> list[int]:
    """``ensemble_pages.active_decades`` (``1880|1890``) as first years of decades."""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return [int(x) for x in value.split("|") if x.strip()]
    if value is None or pd.isna(value):
        return []
    return [int(value)]

def ensemble_chronicle_clauses(pages: pd.DataFrame, ensembles: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Each ensemble page's own chronicle, read and cut as a place's is (D-145).

    One block per ensemble and place it is listed under (as :func:`_ensemble_evidence`
    has one row per ensemble and place), read by :func:`read_chronicle` and
    :func:`chronicle_clauses`.  Key ``(ensemble_id, geo_id, line_no, clause_no)``,
    asserted.  A puppet ensemble's clauses are all puppet; ``ensemble_german`` marks a
    German ensemble's, whose evidence never counts as Czech; ``ensemble_name`` is the name it
    is listed under (D-254 Q7: whose page it is decides whose its players are).
    """
    columns = ["ensemble_id", *CLAUSE_COLUMNS, "before_1914", "ensemble_german", "ensemble_name"]
    text = pages.set_index("ensemble_id")["chronicle_text"]
    listed = ensembles[["ensemble_id", "geo_id", "name"]].drop_duplicates(["ensemble_id", "geo_id"])
    parts = []
    for ensemble_id, geo_id, name in listed.itertuples(index=False):
        chronicle = text.get(ensemble_id)
        if not isinstance(chronicle, str):
            continue
        lines = pd.DataFrame(read_chronicle(int(geo_id), chronicle), columns=CHRONICLE_COLUMNS)
        clauses = chronicle_clauses(lines)
        if clauses.empty:
            continue
        name = name if isinstance(name, str) else ""
        clauses.insert(0, "ensemble_id", int(ensemble_id))
        clauses["puppet"] = clauses["puppet"] | bool(_PUPPET.search(name))
        clauses["ensemble_german"] = bool(EVENT_CUES["german"].search(name))
        clauses["ensemble_name"] = name
        parts.append(clauses)
    out = pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True) if parts else pd.DataFrame(columns=columns)
    assert not out.duplicated(["ensemble_id", "geo_id", "line_no", "clause_no"]).any(), \
        "ensemble clauses: key not unique"
    return out[columns]

def assign_companies(evidence: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """One ``company_id`` per company, across the ensemble list and the chronicle (B2).

    Within a place, a chronicle company clause joins the ensemble row whose start lies
    within :data:`MATCH_START_YEARS` and whose end does not contradict it — the closest
    start first, each ensemble row taken at most once, names not used.  The chronicle
    clauses left over join one another by the same rule, so ``1887 zal. SDO`` and
    ``1887-1934 SDO`` are one company.  Rows that are no company get <NA>.
    """
    company_id = pd.Series(pd.NA, index=evidence.index, dtype="string")
    companies = evidence[evidence["company"]]
    for geo_id, group in companies.groupby("geo_id"):
        anchors: list[tuple] = []          # (company_id, start_lo, end_lo, end_hi, from_ensemble, used)
        for idx, r in group[group["source"] == "ensemble"].iterrows():
            cid = f"{geo_id}:e{r['source_key']}"
            company_id[idx] = cid
            anchors.append([cid, r["start_lo"], r["end_lo"], r["end_hi"], True, False])
        clauses = group[group["source"] == "chronicle"].sort_values("start_lo", na_position="last")
        for idx, r in clauses.iterrows():
            best, best_gap = None, None
            for anchor in anchors:
                if anchor[4] and anchor[5]:
                    continue                    # an ensemble row already matched
                gap = abs(anchor[1] - r["start_lo"]) if pd.notna(r["start_lo"]) else np.inf
                if gap <= MATCH_START_YEARS and _ends_agree(anchor[2], anchor[3], r["end_lo"], r["end_hi"]):
                    if best_gap is None or gap < best_gap:
                        best, best_gap = anchor, gap
            if best is None:
                best = [f"{geo_id}:c{r['source_key']}", r["start_lo"], r["end_lo"], r["end_hi"], False, False]
                anchors.append(best)
            elif best[4]:
                best[5] = True
            company_id[idx] = best[0]
    return company_id

def drop_copied_place_clauses(place_ev: pd.DataFrame, ensemble_ev: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame

The place-chronicle evidence less the clauses an ensemble page of the same place prints again (D-213): the same text and the same dates, matched one for one, so k place copies against m page copies lose min(k, m) (earliest line first).

The page's copy is kept: it belongs to its company (D-145), where the place copy would be matched by B2 or stand alone, and both were being counted. A text repeated within the place chronicle is left alone — 2014 aktivní. under each of four companies is four records — and so is one printed on two companies' pages (a joint performance, or two records of one company: a lineage question for the settlement check, not this rule). attrs["copied_place_clauses"] holds the number dropped.

def drop_copied_place_clauses(place_ev: pd.DataFrame, ensemble_ev: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The place-chronicle evidence less the clauses an ensemble page of the same place
    prints again (D-213): the same text and the same dates, matched one for one, so ``k``
    place copies against ``m`` page copies lose ``min(k, m)`` (earliest line first).

    The page's copy is kept: it belongs to its company (D-145), where the place copy would
    be matched by B2 or stand alone, and both were being counted.  A text repeated *within*
    the place chronicle is left alone — ``2014 aktivní.`` under each of four companies is
    four records — and so is one printed on two companies' pages (a joint performance, or
    two records of one company: a lineage question for the settlement check, not this rule).
    ``attrs["copied_place_clauses"]`` holds the number dropped.
    """
    if place_ev.empty or ensemble_ev.empty:
        out = place_ev.copy()
        out.attrs["copied_place_clauses"] = 0
        return out
    page_copies = _repeat_key(ensemble_ev).value_counts()
    key = _repeat_key(place_ev)
    order = place_ev.assign(_k=key.values).sort_values(["_k", "line_no", "clause_no"])
    rank = order.groupby("_k").cumcount()
    copied = rank < order["_k"].map(page_copies).fillna(0).astype(int)
    out = place_ev.drop(index=order.index[copied.values])
    out.attrs["copied_place_clauses"] = int(copied.sum())
    return out
