def evidence_table(places: pd.DataFrame, ensembles: pd.DataFrame, coded: pd.DataFrame,
                   pages: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
                   ensemble_coded: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Ensemble spans, chronicle clauses and first reports as one table of dated evidence.

    Key ``evidence_id`` (``source:geo_id:source_key``), asserted unique.  Every row has
    a start or an end interval.  Columns as :data:`EVIDENCE_COLUMNS`.  With the ensemble
    pages (``pages``, scraper step C) and their coded chronicles (``ensemble_coded``,
    :func:`code_clauses` of :func:`ensemble_chronicle_clauses`), sources
    ``ensemble_decade`` and ``ensemble_chronicle`` join, both under the ensemble's own
    ``company_id`` (D-145).  A place-chronicle clause that an ensemble page of the same
    place prints again is dropped in favour of the page's copy (D-213,
    :func:`drop_copied_place_clauses`); ``attrs["copied_place_clauses"]`` holds the count.
    """
    place_ev = _clause_evidence(coded)
    parts = [_ensemble_evidence(ensembles, pages), place_ev, _first_report_evidence(places)]
    copied = 0
    if ensemble_coded is not None and len(ensemble_coded):
        assert pages is not None, "evidence: an ensemble chronicle needs its pages"
        page_ev = _ensemble_chronicle_evidence(ensemble_coded)
        kept = drop_copied_place_clauses(place_ev, page_ev)
        copied = kept.attrs.get("copied_place_clauses", 0)
        parts = [_ensemble_evidence(ensembles, pages), kept, _first_report_evidence(places), page_ev]
    ev = pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True, sort=False)
    preset = (ev["company_id"] if "company_id" in ev else pd.Series(pd.NA, index=ev.index)).astype("string")
    for column in EVIDENCE_COLUMNS:
        if column not in ev:
            ev[column] = np.nan
    flags = ["open_end", "hedged", "activity_hedged", "czech_activity", "company", "performance", "pause", "puppet",
             *[c for c in EVENT_COLUMNS if c not in ("performance", "attendance")], "attendance"]
    ev[flags] = ev[flags].astype("boolean").fillna(False).astype(bool)
    ev["titles"] = ev["titles"].fillna("")
    ev["evidence_id"] = ev["source"] + ":" + ev["geo_id"].astype(int).astype(str) + ":" + ev["source_key"]
    ev["company_id"] = preset.where(preset.notna(), assign_companies(ev))
    # D-145: a company whose page lists decades is possible in those decades only, so no
    # record of it — a place-chronicle clause matched to it by B2 included — stays open;
    # unless its own page records it after its last listed decade (D-214), which the
    # listing cannot then be the whole of: B1's open end stands
    listed = set(ev.loc[ev["source"] == "ensemble_decade", "company_id"].dropna().unique())
    outlived = outlived_listings(ev, pages) if pages is not None else set()
    ev.loc[ev["company_id"].isin(listed - outlived), "open_end"] = False
    reopen = (ev["source"] == "ensemble") & ev["company_id"].isin(outlived) & ev["end_lo"].isna() & ev["end_hi"].isna()
    ev.loc[reopen, "open_end"] = True
    bridges = company_bridges(ev, pages) if pages is not None else pd.DataFrame(columns=EVIDENCE_COLUMNS)
    ev = pd.concat([ev[EVIDENCE_COLUMNS], bridges[EVIDENCE_COLUMNS]], ignore_index=True)
    assert ev["evidence_id"].is_unique, "evidence: key not unique"
    assert (ev[["start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo", "end_hi"]].notna().any(axis=1)).all()
    ev.attrs.update(copied_place_clauses=copied, outlived_listings=len(outlived), company_bridges=len(bridges))
    return ev

def outlived_listings(ev: pd.DataFrame, pages: pd.DataFrame) -> set[str]:
    """Companies whose page lists decades but whose own page chronicle records them in a later
    decade (D-214, the narrow R2): the listing is contradicted by the page itself, so it does
    not close the company's open end."""
    page = _page_records(ev)
    if page.empty:
        return set()
    last = {e: max(d) for e, d in zip(pages["ensemble_id"], pages["active_decades"].map(active_decade_list)) if d}
    page["last_listed"] = page["ensemble_id"].map(last)
    first_year = page["start_lo"].fillna(page["start_hi"])
    later = page["last_listed"].notna() & (first_year >= page["last_listed"] + 10)
    return set(page.loc[later, "page_company"])

One company_bridge record per company that its own records pin to two or more years (D-214, R4): certain from the first to the last of them, as a span.

A record pins a year when it is printed to the year and not hedged: a Czech-activity clause on the company's own page (a performance there attests that the company existed), or any record already under its company_id (the list row's start, a place clause matched by B2). The bridge is drawn only when the page lists every decade between the two years, so a company whose page leaves a decade out is not carried across it; a recorded pause still turns its years possible (B12).

def company_bridges(ev: pd.DataFrame, pages: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One ``company_bridge`` record per company that its own records pin to two or more
    years (D-214, R4): certain from the first to the last of them, as a span.

    A record pins a year when it is printed to the year and not hedged: a Czech-activity
    clause on the company's own page (a performance there attests that the company
    existed), or any record already under its ``company_id`` (the list row's start, a
    place clause matched by B2).  The bridge is drawn only when the page lists every decade
    between the two years, so a company whose page leaves a decade out is not carried across
    it; a recorded pause still turns its years possible (B12).
    """
    page = _page_records(ev)
    # a hall the company hired (rare case 127) leaves its plays possible only: it pins no year
    exact = lambda f: f["start_lo"].notna() & (f["start_lo"] == f["start_hi"]) & ~f["hedged"] \
        & ~(f["activity_hedged"].astype(bool) if "activity_hedged" in f else False) \
        & (f["end_lo"].isna() | (f["end_lo"] == f["start_lo"]))  # noqa: E731
    pins = page.loc[exact(page), ["geo_id", "page_company", "start_lo"]].rename(columns={"page_company": "company_id"})
    own = ev[ev["company_id"].isin(set(pins["company_id"])) & exact(ev) & (ev["source"] != "ensemble_decade")]
    pins = pd.concat([pins, own[["geo_id", "company_id", "start_lo"]]], ignore_index=True)
    decades = {_ensemble_company_id(g, e): set(active_decade_list(d)) for g, e, d in
               zip(ev.loc[ev["source"] == "ensemble", "geo_id"], ev.loc[ev["source"] == "ensemble", "source_key"].astype(int),
                   ev.loc[ev["source"] == "ensemble", "source_key"].astype(int).map(
                       pages.set_index("ensemble_id")["active_decades"]))}
    rows = []
    for (geo_id, company_id), group in pins.groupby(["geo_id", "company_id"]):
        years = sorted(set(group["start_lo"].astype(int)))
        listed = decades.get(company_id, set())
        if len(years) < 2 or not listed:
            continue
        lo, hi = years[0], years[-1]
        if not all(d in listed for d in range(lo // 10 * 10, hi // 10 * 10 + 1, 10)):
            continue
        rows.append({"evidence_id": f"company_bridge:{int(geo_id)}:{company_id.split(':e')[1]}",
                     "geo_id": int(geo_id), "source": "company_bridge", "source_key": company_id.split(":e")[1],
                     "company_id": company_id, "start_lo": float(lo), "start_hi": float(lo),
                     "end_lo": float(hi), "end_hi": float(hi)})
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["evidence_id", "geo_id", "source", "source_key", "company_id",
                                      "start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo", "end_hi"])
    for column in EVIDENCE_COLUMNS:
        if column not in out:
            out[column] = False if column in ev and ev[column].dtype == bool else np.nan
    out["titles"] = ""
    out["czech_activity"] = out["company"] = True
    return out[EVIDENCE_COLUMNS]

def year_bounds(start_lo, start_hi, end_lo, end_hi, open_end: bool, hedged: bool, last_year: int=PANEL_LAST_YEAR) -> tuple[tuple | None, tuple | None]

The years a record makes theatre certain and possible, as closed ranges or None.

A span with an end is certain from its latest possible start to its earliest possible end, and possible over its whole width. Open-ended (B1): certain only in a start year printed exactly, possible from there to last_year. A point is certain only when printed to the year; a decade or a kolem is possible across its width and certain in none (B10). Known only by its end (do 1910): possible in the end year, certain in none. A start with one bound missing — před 1880 (no earliest), po 1900 (no latest) — is printed to no year, so certain in none (audit A5). Hedged (B4): never certain.

def year_bounds(start_lo, start_hi, end_lo, end_hi, open_end: bool, hedged: bool,
                last_year: int = PANEL_LAST_YEAR) -> tuple[tuple | None, tuple | None]:
    """The years a record makes theatre *certain* and *possible*, as closed ranges or None.

    A span with an end is certain from its latest possible start to its earliest
    possible end, and possible over its whole width.  Open-ended (B1): certain only in a
    start year printed exactly, possible from there to ``last_year``.  A point is certain
    only when printed to the year; a decade or a ``kolem`` is possible across its width
    and certain in none (B10).  Known only by its end (``do 1910``): possible in the end
    year, certain in none.  A start with one bound missing — ``před 1880`` (no earliest),
    ``po 1900`` (no latest) — is printed to no year, so certain in none (audit A5).
    Hedged (B4): never certain.
    """
    has_start = not pd.isna(start_lo) or not pd.isna(start_hi)
    has_end = not pd.isna(end_lo) or not pd.isna(end_hi)
    if not has_start:
        if not has_end:
            return None, None
        lo, hi = (end_lo if not pd.isna(end_lo) else end_hi), (end_hi if not pd.isna(end_hi) else end_lo)
        return None, (int(lo), int(hi))
    exact = not pd.isna(start_lo) and not pd.isna(start_hi) and start_lo == start_hi
    s_lo = start_lo if not pd.isna(start_lo) else start_hi
    s_hi = start_hi if not pd.isna(start_hi) else start_lo
    if has_end:
        e_lo = end_lo if not pd.isna(end_lo) else end_hi
        e_hi = end_hi if not pd.isna(end_hi) else end_lo
        # `po 1882` to an end: the start may be as late as the end, so the end year alone
        latest_start = e_lo if pd.isna(start_hi) else s_hi
        certain = (int(latest_start), int(e_lo)) if latest_start <= e_lo else None
        possible = (int(s_lo), int(max(e_hi, s_hi)))
    elif open_end:
        certain = (int(s_lo), int(s_lo)) if exact else None
        possible = (int(s_lo), max(int(s_hi), last_year))
    else:
        certain = (int(s_lo), int(s_lo)) if exact else None
        possible = (int(s_lo), int(s_hi))
    return (None if hedged else certain), possible

def place_year_panel(evidence: pd.DataFrame, geo_ids, first_year: int = PANEL_FIRST_YEAR,
                     last_year: int = PANEL_LAST_YEAR) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Every place × year, ``first_year``–``last_year``: Czech amateur theatre, certain and possible.

    Balanced: one row per place of ``geo_ids`` and year, key ``(geo_id, year)`` asserted.
    Columns, each ``_certain`` and ``_possible``:
    ``any_activity`` (some Czech-activity record, the first report included, B3);
    ``ensembles_active`` (distinct companies whose span covers the year);
    ``performances_min`` (certain: performance records printed to one year, each counting
    the number it states or 1; possible: records whose interval covers the year); one
    count per :data:`EVENT_COLUMNS` (German, bilingual and Latin are
    counted, never activity, B8).  Also ``performances_period_avg`` (a count stated over
    a span, ``1883-1910 173 her``, spread evenly over its certain years — an average, so
    kept apart from the minimum), ``plays_distinct_certain``, ``attendance_max``
    (largest audience stated in a record certain in the year), and
    ``activity_decade_certain`` (Czech activity certainly inside this year's decade, B10).
    A recorded pause (B12) turns certain activity and companies into possible for its
    certain years — but never a performance printed to its year, nor the company that gave
    it, in that year (D-254 Q11).  A hall a company hired is the company's act with its
    activity possible only (``activity_hedged``, D-254).  Puppet theatre is ``puppet_*`` only.
    """
    geo_ids = pd.Index(sorted(set(int(g) for g in geo_ids)))
    years = np.arange(first_year, last_year + 1)
    shape = (len(geo_ids), len(years))
    row_of = {g: i for i, g in enumerate(geo_ids)}
    arrays: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}

    def add(name: str, i: int, bounds, amount: float = 1.0, mask=None) -> None:
        """Add ``amount`` over ``bounds``, except in the years ``mask`` (a pause) holds."""
        if bounds is None:
            return
        a, b = max(bounds[0], first_year) - first_year, min(bounds[1], last_year) - first_year
        if a <= b:
            keep = 1.0 if mask is None or mask is False else ~np.asarray(mask)[a:b + 1]
            arrays.setdefault(name, np.zeros(shape))[i, a:b + 1] += amount * keep

    ev = evidence[evidence["geo_id"].isin(geo_ids)]
    titles: dict[tuple[int, int], set] = {}
    attendance = np.full(shape, np.nan)
    decade = np.zeros(shape, dtype=bool)
    companies_seen: dict[tuple[int, str], tuple] = {}
    place_pause, company_pause = _pauses(ev, row_of, shape, first_year, last_year)

    performed = _performed_years(ev, row_of, len(years), first_year, last_year)

    def paused(i: int, owner) -> np.ndarray:
        """The years a record of ``owner`` (a company, or None) in place ``i`` is paused."""
        return place_pause[i] | company_pause.get((i, owner), False)

    for r in ev.itertuples(index=False):
        i = row_of[int(r.geo_id)]
        certain, possible = year_bounds(r.start_lo, r.start_hi, r.end_lo, r.end_hi,
                                        bool(r.open_end), bool(r.hedged), last_year)
        prefix = "puppet_" if r.puppet else ""
        if r.czech_activity and not r.puppet:
            # rare case 127: a hall the company hired — the company certain, its plays possible
            hall_only = bool(getattr(r, "activity_hedged", False))
            # D-254 Q11: a pause never turns a performance dated to its year possible
            dated_play = bool(r.performance) and certain is not None and certain[0] == certain[1]
            add("any_activity_certain", i, None if hall_only else certain,
                mask=None if dated_play else paused(i, _owner(r)))
            add("any_activity_possible", i, possible)
            # audit A6: a hedged record is never certain (B4), of its decade neither
            if possible is not None and possible[0] // 10 == possible[1] // 10 and not r.hedged \
                    and not hall_only:
                d0 = possible[0] // 10 * 10
                add("_decade", i, (d0, d0 + 9))
        if r.puppet and (r.czech_activity or r.company):
            add("puppet_activity_certain", i, certain)
            add("puppet_activity_possible", i, possible)
        if r.company and isinstance(r.company_id, str) and not r.puppet:
            seen = companies_seen.setdefault((i, r.company_id), [None, []])
            seen[0] = _hull(seen[0], certain)
            if possible is not None:
                seen[1].append(possible)
        if r.performance and r.czech_activity:
            single = certain is not None and certain[0] == certain[1]
            stated = not pd.isna(r.count_stated)
            if single:
                add(f"{prefix}performances_min_certain", i, certain, r.count_stated if stated else 1.0)
            elif certain is not None and stated and not r.puppet:
                # `1883-1910 173 her`: an average over the span, not a minimum in any year
                add("performances_period_avg", i, certain, r.count_stated / (certain[1] - certain[0] + 1))
            add(f"{prefix}performances_min_possible", i, possible)
            if single and r.titles and not r.puppet:
                titles.setdefault((i, certain[0]), set()).update(r.titles.split("|"))
        for column in EVENT_COLUMNS:
            if column != "performance" and getattr(r, column):
                add(f"{column}_certain", i, certain)
                add(f"{column}_possible", i, possible)
        if not pd.isna(r.attendance_n) and certain is not None and certain[0] == certain[1]:
            j = certain[0] - first_year
            if 0 <= j < len(years):
                attendance[i, j] = np.nanmax([attendance[i, j], r.attendance_n])
    for (i, company_id), (certain, possibles) in companies_seen.items():
        # a company that performed in a paused year was active that year (D-254 Q11)
        played = performed.get((i, company_id))
        mask = paused(i, company_id)
        add("ensembles_active_certain", i, certain, mask=mask if played is None else mask & ~played)
        covered = np.zeros(len(years), dtype=bool)
        for bounds in ([certain] if certain else []) + possibles:
            a, b = max(bounds[0], first_year) - first_year, min(bounds[1], last_year) - first_year
            if a <= b:
                covered[a:b + 1] = True
        arrays.setdefault("ensembles_active_possible", np.zeros(shape))[i] += covered
    for (i, year), found in titles.items():
        if first_year <= year <= last_year:
            arrays.setdefault("plays_distinct_certain", np.zeros(shape))[i, year - first_year] = len(found)
    decade = arrays.pop("_decade", np.zeros(shape)) > 0
    any_company_pause = np.zeros(shape, dtype=bool)
    for (i, _), years_paused in company_pause.items():
        any_company_pause[i] |= years_paused
    return _panel_frame(arrays, attendance, decade, geo_ids, years, place_pause | any_company_pause)

def register_courts(register_places: pd.DataFrame, courts=None) -> pd.Series:
    """``settlement_id`` → its 1910 court as the 1910 register prints it
    (``data/final/register_rechecked/register_places``).  Where a settlement is anchored
    twice — a detached part filed under its town (``Škarez … viz Prachatice``) or the two
    Bohemian volumes differing — the municipality row wins, then the edition of record.

    ``courts``, given (the 1910 backbone's court ids, ``districts_1910``), drops a register court
    outside it: Zlabings (Slavonice, ``302006900``) and Triesch (Třešť, ``302012900``) were set up
    after 1910 and keep ids of their own in the register only to keep their numbering apart
    (D-205). Their municipalities were in a 1910 court (D-122, D-208), which the settlement's own
    point then gives, as it does for a person's ``birth_court_id`` (D-255)."""
    r = register_places.dropna(subset=["settlement_id", "court_id"])
    if courts is not None:
        r = r[r["court_id"].astype("int64").isin(pd.Series(courts).astype("int64"))]
    r = r.assign(_part=r["place_level"].ne("municipality"),
                 _edition=r["edition"].map(_REGISTER_EDITION_ORDER).fillna(2))
    r = r.sort_values(["settlement_id", "_part", "_edition"], kind="stable")
    return r.drop_duplicates("settlement_id").set_index("settlement_id")["court_id"].astype("int64")

okres_id — the tied settlement's 1910 okres (okres_source = "settlement", the name-based key, as for the persons); for a place tied to none, the okres whose MPIDR court polygon holds the place's own point ("polygon", needs places and locator; agrees with the name on 89 % of the places that have both, 2026-11-11). court_id — always inside okres_id (audit C2: courts did not nest in okresy): the register's court for the tied settlement (court_source = "register", register_courts); else the settlement's own point-in-polygon court; else the place's point snapped into the okres (1 km, D-35); else the okres's only court (districts); else missing, and the place reaches the okres sum but no court's.

def place_units(join: pd.DataFrame, settlements: pd.DataFrame, *,
                places: pd.DataFrame | None = None, register_places: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
                locator=None, districts: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Each database place's 1910 settlement, okres and court, and where each came from.

    One row per place of ``join`` (:func:`join_places_to_settlements`):

    ``okres_id`` — the tied settlement's 1910 okres (``okres_source = "settlement"``, the
    name-based key, as for the persons); for a place tied to none, the okres whose MPIDR
    court polygon holds the place's own point (``"polygon"``, needs ``places`` and
    ``locator``; agrees with the name on 89 % of the places that have both, 2026-11-11).
    ``court_id`` — always inside ``okres_id`` (audit C2: courts did not nest in okresy):
    the register's court for the tied settlement (``court_source = "register"``,
    :func:`register_courts`); else the settlement's own point-in-polygon court; else the
    place's point snapped into the okres (1 km, D-35); else the okres's only court
    (``districts``); else missing, and the place reaches the okres sum but no court's.
    """
    S = settlements[settlements["has_okres_1910"]] if "has_okres_1910" in settlements else settlements
    S = S[["settlement_row", "settlement_id", "okres_id", "court_id"]].rename(columns={"court_id": "_s_court"})
    out = (join[["geo_id", "settlement_row"]].astype({"settlement_row": "Int64"})
           .merge(S, on="settlement_row", how="left", validate="m:1"))
    assert len(out) == len(join), "place_units: the join gained or lost rows"
    out["okres_id"] = out["okres_id"].astype("Int64")
    out["okres_source"] = np.where(out["okres_id"].notna(), "settlement", None).astype(object)
    out["court_id"] = pd.array([pd.NA] * len(out), dtype="Int64")
    out["court_source"] = pd.Series([None] * len(out), dtype=object)

    def fill(candidate, source: str) -> None:
        """Take ``candidate`` as the court where none is set yet and it lies in the okres."""
        candidate = pd.Series(candidate, index=out.index, dtype="Int64")
        ok = out["court_id"].isna() & candidate.notna() & _okres_of_court(candidate).eq(out["okres_id"]).fillna(False)
        out.loc[ok, "court_id"] = candidate[ok]
        out.loc[ok, "court_source"] = source

    backbone = None if districts is None else districts["court_id"]
    if register_places is not None:
        fill(out["settlement_id"].map(register_courts(register_places, backbone)), "register")
    fill(out["_s_court"], "settlement_polygon")
    if places is not None and locator is not None:
        from utils.parsing import spatial as sp
        pts = out[["geo_id"]].merge(places[["geo_id", "lat", "lon"]], on="geo_id", how="left", validate="1:1")
        # a place tied to no settlement: its okres from its own point (no okres to snap toward)
        bare = sp.add_court_ids(pts.assign(okres_id=out["okres_id"]), locator, okres_col="okres_id")
        lone = out["okres_id"].isna() & bare["court_id"].notna()
        out.loc[lone, "okres_id"] = _okres_of_court(bare.loc[lone, "court_id"])
        out.loc[lone, "okres_source"] = "polygon"
        fill(bare["court_id"], "place_polygon")
    if districts is not None:
        courts = districts["court_id"].astype("int64")
        per_okres = courts.groupby(courts // 1000).agg(["size", "first"])
        only = per_okres.loc[per_okres["size"] == 1, "first"]
        fill(out["okres_id"].map(only), "only_court")
    out = out.drop(columns=["settlement_row", "_s_court"])
    assert out["geo_id"].is_unique, "place_units: geo_id not unique"
    nested = out["court_id"].isna() | (_okres_of_court(out["court_id"]) == out["okres_id"])
    assert nested.all(), "place_units: a court outside its okres"
    return out

def place_units_report(units: pd.DataFrame, panel: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    """Print where the places' okresy and courts came from, by places and by certain
    place-years of Czech activity, and how much of the panel reaches no okres or no court."""
    certain = panel.groupby("geo_id")["any_activity_certain"].sum().rename("certain_place_years")
    U = units.merge(certain, left_on="geo_id", right_index=True, how="left").fillna({"certain_place_years": 0})
    total = U["certain_place_years"].sum()
    for column in ("okres_source", "court_source"):
        table = U.assign(**{column: U[column].fillna("none")}).groupby(column).agg(
            places=("geo_id", "size"), certain_place_years=("certain_place_years", "sum"))
        table["share"] = (table["certain_place_years"] / total).round(3) if total else 0.0
        print(f"\n── {column}\n" + table.to_string())

def area_year_tables(panel: pd.DataFrame, units: pd.DataFrame, settlements: pd.DataFrame, crosswalk: pd.DataFrame | None=None, register_places: pd.DataFrame | None=None, districts: pd.DataFrame | None=None) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]

The place panel summed to 1910 settlement, court, okres and census okres × year.

units is place_units (one row per place); settlements is settlement_frame; crosswalk is data/final/geo/okres_census_crosswalk (okres_id → census_okres_id) and, given, adds the census_okres table; register_places, given, adds the register's courts of the settlements to the court grid (only courts of districts, the 1910 backbone, where that is given: D-255). Every 1910 settlement with a 1910 okres gets every year, and so does every okres and court any of them or any place falls in — a unit with no database place is a row of zeros (D-141: the treatment's zero, memory of the German areas). Counts are summed; any_activity_* becomes places_active_* (places with activity) and any_activity_* (any); attendance_max the maximum. places_in_database is the number of database places in the unit. A place with an okres but no settlement (okres_source = "polygon") counts in its court and okres, not in the settlement table; one with neither is in no table. Keys asserted; the courts of an okres asserted to sum to the okres, less the places with no court.

def area_year_tables(panel: pd.DataFrame, units: pd.DataFrame, settlements: pd.DataFrame,
                     crosswalk: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
                     register_places: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
                     districts: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """The place panel summed to 1910 settlement, court, okres and census okres × year.

    ``units`` is :func:`place_units` (one row per place); ``settlements`` is
    :func:`settlement_frame`; ``crosswalk`` is ``data/final/geo/okres_census_crosswalk``
    (``okres_id`` → ``census_okres_id``) and, given, adds the ``census_okres`` table;
    ``register_places``, given, adds the register's courts of the settlements to the court grid
    (only courts of ``districts``, the 1910 backbone, where that is given: D-255).
    Every 1910 settlement with a 1910 okres gets every year, and so does every okres and
    court any of them or any place falls in — a unit with no database place is a row of
    zeros (D-141: the treatment's zero, memory of the German areas).  Counts are summed;
    ``any_activity_*`` becomes ``places_active_*`` (places with activity) and
    ``any_activity_*`` (any); ``attendance_max`` the maximum.  ``places_in_database`` is
    the number of database places in the unit.  A place with an okres but no settlement
    (``okres_source = "polygon"``) counts in its court and okres, not in the settlement
    table; one with neither is in no table.  Keys asserted; the courts of an okres asserted
    to sum to the okres, less the places with no court.
    """
    S = settlements[settlements["has_okres_1910"]] if "has_okres_1910" in settlements else settlements
    assert S["settlement_id"].is_unique, "settlements: settlement_id not unique"
    U = units[["geo_id", "settlement_id", "court_id", "okres_id"]].copy()
    U["okres_id"] = U["okres_id"].astype("Int64")
    grids = {"settlement_id": S["settlement_id"],
             "okres_id": pd.concat([S["okres_id"], U["okres_id"]]).astype("Int64"),
             "court_id": pd.concat([S["court_id"].astype("Int64").where(
                                        _okres_of_court(S["court_id"]).eq(S["okres_id"].astype("Int64")).fillna(False)),
                                    U["court_id"]]).astype("Int64")}
    if register_places is not None:
        backbone = None if districts is None else districts["court_id"]
        reg = S["settlement_id"].map(register_courts(register_places, backbone)).astype("Int64")
        reg = reg.where(_okres_of_court(reg).eq(S["okres_id"].astype("Int64")).fillna(False))
        grids["court_id"] = pd.concat([grids["court_id"], reg]).astype("Int64")
    levels = dict(AREA_LEVELS)
    if crosswalk is not None:
        pooled = crosswalk.set_index("okres_id")["census_okres_id"]
        missing = set(grids["okres_id"].dropna()) - set(pooled.index)
        assert not missing, f"okres not in the census crosswalk: {sorted(missing)}"
        U["census_okres_id"] = U["okres_id"].map(pooled).astype("Int64")
        grids["census_okres_id"] = grids["okres_id"].map(pooled)
    else:
        levels.pop("census_okres")
    P = panel.merge(U, on="geo_id", how="inner", validate="m:1")
    assert len(P) <= len(panel)
    bools = [c for c in panel.columns if panel[c].dtype == bool]
    counts = [c for c in panel.columns if c not in bools + PANEL_KEY + ["attendance_max"]]
    years = np.sort(panel["year"].unique())
    tables = {}
    for level, key in levels.items():
        agg = P.dropna(subset=[key]).groupby([key, "year"]).agg(
            **{c: (c, "sum") for c in counts},
            **{c: (c, "any") for c in bools},
            **{c.replace("any_activity", "places_active"): (c, "sum")
               for c in ("any_activity_certain", "any_activity_possible")},
            attendance_max=("attendance_max", "max"))
        ids = pd.Series(grids[key]).dropna().unique()
        grid = pd.MultiIndex.from_product([np.sort(ids), years], names=[key, "year"])
        assert set(agg.index) <= set(grid), f"{level}: a unit outside the grid"
        out = agg.reindex(grid).reset_index()
        filled = [c for c in out.columns if c not in (key, "year", "attendance_max")]
        for c in filled:
            out[c] = (out[c].astype("boolean").fillna(False).astype(bool) if c in bools
                      else out[c].fillna(0).astype(agg[c].dtype))
        per_unit = U.dropna(subset=[key]).groupby(key).size().rename("places_in_database")
        out = out.merge(per_unit, left_on=key, right_index=True, how="left", validate="m:1")
        out["places_in_database"] = out["places_in_database"].fillna(0).astype(int)
        assert not out.duplicated([key, "year"]).any(), f"{level} panel: key not unique"
        tables[level] = out
    _assert_courts_sum_to_okresy(tables, P)
    if "census_okres" in tables:
        t, o = tables["census_okres"], tables["okres"]
        assert t["places_active_certain"].sum() == o["places_active_certain"].sum(), "census okres ≠ okres sum"
    return tables

def panel_report(panel: pd.DataFrame, evidence: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    """Print what the panel holds: evidence by source, places and place-years active."""
    print("\n── evidence by source\n" + evidence.groupby("source").agg(
        rows=("evidence_id", "size"), czech_activity=("czech_activity", "sum"),
        companies=("company_id", "nunique")).to_string())
    if "copied_place_clauses" in evidence.attrs:
        print(f"place-chronicle clauses dropped as copies of an ensemble page's (D-213): "
              f"{evidence.attrs['copied_place_clauses']:,}")
    if "company_bridges" in evidence.attrs:
        print(f"companies bridged between their own records (D-214): {evidence.attrs['company_bridges']:,}; "
              f"listings their own page outlives, left open: {evidence.attrs['outlived_listings']:,}")
    active = panel.groupby("geo_id")[["any_activity_certain", "any_activity_possible"]].any()
    print(f"\nplaces with Czech activity {PANEL_FIRST_YEAR}–{PANEL_LAST_YEAR}: certain "
          f"{int(active['any_activity_certain'].sum()):,}, possible {int(active['any_activity_possible'].sum()):,}"
          f" of {panel['geo_id'].nunique():,}")
    by_decade = panel.assign(decade=panel["year"] // 10 * 10).groupby("decade")[
        ["any_activity_certain", "any_activity_possible", "ensembles_active_certain",
         "performances_min_certain", "german_certain"]].sum()
    print("\n── place-years by decade (sums over place-years)\n" + by_decade.to_string())

def ensemble_page_summary(pages: pd.DataFrame, ensembles: pd.DataFrame,
                          cutoff: int = PRE_WAR_CUTOFF) -> dict[str, int]:
    """What the ensemble pages add to the list's start (D-145), one count per ensemble.

    ``end_year``: the page prints an end or last report as a year or decade.
    ``decades``: it lists a decade.  ``decade_after_start``: a listed decade after the
    start's decade and before ``cutoff``.  ``closes_before_cutoff``: its last listed decade
    ends before ``cutoff`` (the open end it replaces ran to the cutoff).
    ``decade_before_start``: it lists a decade before the start's (kept as printed).
    ``chronicle_after_start``: its own chronicle has a dated line after the start and
    before ``cutoff``.  ``uninformative``: none of the end, a later decade or a later line.
    """
    start = ensembles.groupby("ensemble_id")["year_from"].min()
    P = pages.set_index("ensemble_id")
    P = P.assign(start=start.reindex(P.index))
    decades = P["active_decades"].map(active_decade_list)
    start_decade = P["start"] // 10 * 10
    later = [any(s < d < cutoff for d in ds) for ds, s in zip(decades, start_decade)]
    before = [any(d < s for d in ds) for ds, s in zip(decades, start_decade)]
    closes = [bool(ds) and max(ds) + 9 < cutoff - 1 for ds in decades]
    line_year = re.compile(rf"^\s*{_DAY_MONTH}(1[5-9]\d\d)\b")
    chron = [isinstance(t, str) and any(s < int(m.group(1)) < cutoff for m in map(line_year.match, t.splitlines()) if m)
             for t, s in zip(P["chronicle_text"], P["start"])]
    end = P["ended_precision"].isin(["year", "decade"]).to_numpy()
    informative = end | np.array(later) | np.array(chron)
    return {"pages": len(P), "end_year": int(end.sum()), "decades": int(decades.map(bool).sum()),
            "decade_after_start": int(sum(later)), "closes_before_cutoff": int(sum(closes)),
            "decade_before_start": int(sum(before)), "chronicle_after_start": int(sum(chron)),
            "uninformative": int((~informative).sum())}

def coverage_tables(
    places: pd.DataFrame,
    ensembles: pd.DataFrame,
    settlements: pd.DataFrame,
    districts: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    *,
    okresy: list[str] | None,
    census: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    cutoff: int = PRE_WAR_CUTOFF,
) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Every table of the pilot, for the scraped sample and (from step A) the country.

    Args:
        places: scraper ``places.csv`` (all places; page fields filled for the sample).
        ensembles: scraper ``ensembles.csv``.
        settlements: ``data/final/geo/settlements_1910``.
        districts: ``data/final/geo/districts_1910`` (district names + court seats).
        okresy: the present-day okresy that were scraped; ``None`` once all of them are,
            in which case the denominator is every 1910 settlement rather than those whose
            okres timeline ends in a sample okres.
        census: ``census_okres_1910`` — if given, each 1910 okres gets its Czech-speaking
            share, the first thing coverage of a *Czech* theatre database depends on.

    Returns:
        A dict of DataFrames; :func:`coverage_report` prints them.
    """
    S = settlement_frame(settlements, districts)
    whole_country = okresy is None
    okresy = sorted(places["okres"].dropna().unique()) if whole_country else list(okresy)
    sample = places.copy() if whole_country else places[places["okres"].isin(okresy)].copy()
    missing_pages = int((~sample["page_cached"]).sum())
    tables: dict[str, pd.DataFrame] = {}

    # ── the join, on the sample ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    join = join_places_to_settlements(sample, S)
    n_before = len(sample)
    sample = sample.merge(join, on="geo_id", how="left", validate="1:1")
    assert len(sample) == n_before, "place ↔ join merge changed the row count"
    dates = place_dates(sample, ensembles[ensembles["geo_id"].isin(sample["geo_id"])], cutoff)
    sample = sample.merge(dates, on="geo_id", how="left", validate="1:1")
    assert len(sample) == n_before
    sample["matched"] = sample["settlement_row"].notna()
    # a place's crown land is that of the 1910 settlement it ties to
    sample = sample.merge(S[["settlement_row", "land"]].astype({"settlement_row": "Int64"}),
                          on="settlement_row", how="left", validate="m:1")
    assert len(sample) == n_before

    tables["join_by_method"] = (sample.groupby(["type", "match_method"]).size()
                                .unstack("type", fill_value=0).assign(all=lambda t: t.sum(axis=1)))
    tables["join_rate"] = sample.groupby("okres").agg(
        places=("geo_id", "size"), matched=("matched", "sum"),
        match_rate=("matched", "mean")).round(3).reset_index()
    tables["unmatched_places"] = sample.loc[~sample["matched"],
                                            ["geo_id", "name", "type", "okres", "match_method",
                                             "n_ensembles", "first_record_year"]]

    # ── the 1910 settlements of the sample area ─────────────────────────────
    in_scope = S["in_1910"] if whole_country else S["in_1910"] & S["okres_now"].isin(okresy)
    scope = S[in_scope]
    n_scope = len(scope)
    tied = sample.loc[sample["matched"], ["settlement_row", "geo_id", "ensemble_pre",
                                          "ensemble_ambiguous", "first_record_pre",
                                          "n_ensembles"]].astype({"settlement_row": "int64"})
    outside_scope = int((~tied["settlement_row"].isin(scope["settlement_row"])).sum())
    cover = scope.merge(tied, on="settlement_row", how="left", validate="1:1")
    assert len(cover) == n_scope, "settlement ↔ place merge changed the row count"
    for col in ("ensemble_pre", "ensemble_ambiguous", "first_record_pre"):
        cover[col] = cover[col].eq(True)          # no database place → not recorded
    by_okres = _share_table(cover, ["okres_now", "land", "okres_id", "okres_1910_cs"])
    if census is not None:
        by_okres = by_okres.merge(census[["okres_id", "lang_czech_share"]], on="okres_id",
                                  how="left", validate="m:1")
        by_okres["lang_czech_share"] = by_okres["lang_czech_share"].round(3)
    tables["settlements_by_okres_1910"] = by_okres
    tables["settlements_by_land"] = _share_table(cover, ["land"])
    tables["settlements_by_size"] = _share_table(cover, ["size_class"])
    tables["settlements_by_land_and_size"] = _share_table(cover, ["land", "size_class"])
    if census is not None:
        # a database of *Czech* theatre: coverage has to be read within language bands
        banded = cover.merge(census[["okres_id", "lang_czech_share"]], on="okres_id",
                             how="left", validate="m:1")
        assert len(banded) == n_scope, "settlement ↔ census merge changed the row count"
        banded["okres_language"] = pd.cut(
            banded["lang_czech_share"], LANGUAGE_BANDS, right=False,
            labels=LANGUAGE_LABELS).astype(object).fillna("no census row")
        czech = banded[banded["okres_language"] == LANGUAGE_LABELS[-1]]
        tables["settlements_by_land_and_language"] = _share_table(banded, ["land", "okres_language"])
        tables["settlements_czech_okresy_by_land_and_size"] = _share_table(czech, ["land", "size_class"])
        spread = _share_table(czech, ["land", "okres_id", "okres_1910_cs"])
        spread = spread[spread["settlements"] >= MIN_OKRES_SETTLEMENTS]
        tables["czech_okresy_spread_by_land"] = spread.groupby("land")["share_ensemble_pre1914"].describe(
            percentiles=[0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9]).round(3).reset_index()
    tables["scope_note"] = pd.DataFrame({
        "what": ["1910 settlements in the denominator (whole country: all; a sample: those "
                 "whose latest okres is a sample okres)",
                 "sample okres on the timeline but not its latest okres (left out)",
                 "sample places tied to a settlement outside that denominator",
                 "sample places whose page is not cached"],
        "n": [n_scope,
              int((S["in_1910"] & ~in_scope
                   & S["okres_tokens"].map(lambda t: bool(set(t) & set(okresy)))).sum()),
              outside_scope, missing_pages]})

    # ── how the database documents a place, by okres ────────────────────────
    paged = sample[sample["page_cached"]]
    tables["documentation_by_okres"] = _documentation_table(paged, "okres")
    tables["documentation_by_land"] = _documentation_table(paged, "land")

    period = pd.Series([first_record_period(y, p) for y, p in
                        zip(paged["first_record_year"], paged["first_record_precision"])],
                       index=paged.index).rename("period")
    for name, by in (("first_record_distribution", "okres"),
                     ("first_record_distribution_by_land", "land")):
        dist = pd.crosstab(period, paged[by].fillna("(no 1910 settlement)")).reindex(
            PERIOD_ORDER, fill_value=0)
        dist["all"] = dist.sum(axis=1)
        tables[name] = dist
    # heaping: a year that many places share is a source being read, not theatre beginning
    exact = paged[paged["first_record_precision"].eq("year")]
    tables["first_record_heaping"] = (
        exact.groupby("okres")["first_record_year"]
        .apply(lambda s: ", ".join(f"{int(y)}×{n}" for y, n in s.value_counts().head(6).items()))
        .rename("commonest first-report years (year×places)").reset_index())
    tables["first_record_precision"] = (paged.groupby(["first_record_precision",
                                                       "first_record_qualified"]).size()
                                        .rename("places").reset_index())

    counts, unclassified = association_counts(
        ensembles[ensembles["geo_id"].isin(sample["geo_id"])], cutoff)
    tables["associations_pre1914"] = counts
    tables["unclassified_names"] = unclassified.head(25).rename("ensembles").reset_index()
    tables["ensemble_year_precision"] = (ensembles.groupby(
        ["year_from_precision", "year_to_precision", "open_ended"]).size()
        .rename("ensembles").reset_index())

    # ── the whole country, from step A alone ────────────────────────────────
    tables.update(country_tables(places, S))
    return tables

def country_tables(places: pd.DataFrame, settlement_frame_: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """From step A alone: which 1910 communes have *any* entry in the database.

    Presence only — the map XML has no dates.  The denominator is the 1910 communes
    (``status_1910 == "obec"``) of ``settlements_1910``; each is assigned to a present-day
    kraj through the latest okres on its timeline that the database knows.
    """
    S = settlement_frame_
    join = join_places_to_settlements(places, S)
    matched = join.dropna(subset=["settlement_row"])
    okres_kraj = (places.dropna(subset=["okres", "kraj"]).groupby("okres")["kraj"]
                  .agg(lambda s: s.mode().iloc[0]).to_dict())
    # the database files Prague under its numbered districts; the lexikon under "Praha"
    prague = next((k for k in okres_kraj.values() if k.startswith("Praha")), None)
    if prague:
        okres_kraj.setdefault("Praha", prague)

    def kraj_of(tokens: list[str]):
        for okres in reversed(tokens):
            if okres in okres_kraj:
                return okres_kraj[okres]
        return None

    communes = S[S["in_1910"] & S["status_1910"].eq("obec")].copy()
    communes["kraj"] = communes["okres_tokens"].map(kraj_of)
    communes["in_database"] = communes["settlement_row"].isin(matched["settlement_row"])

    def share(by: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
        table = communes.groupby(by, dropna=False).agg(
            communes_1910=("settlement_row", "size"),
            in_database=("in_database", "sum")).reset_index()
        table["share"] = (table["in_database"] / table["communes_1910"]).round(3)
        return table

    by_kraj = share("kraj").merge(
        places.groupby("kraj").agg(
            database_places=("geo_id", "size"),
            database_obce=("type", lambda s: int((s == "Obec").sum()))).reset_index(),
        on="kraj", how="outer", validate="1:1")
    return {
        "country_join": (join["match_method"].value_counts().rename("places").reset_index()),
        "country_communes_by_kraj": by_kraj.sort_values("share", ascending=False),
        "country_communes_by_land": share("land"),
        "country_places_by_type": places.groupby("type").agg(
            places=("geo_id", "size"),
            matched=("geo_id", lambda s: int(s.isin(matched["geo_id"]).sum()))).reset_index(),
    }

"""
amateur_theatre.py — is the amateur-theatre database usable as a pre-1914 covariate?
====================================================================================
**Feasibility pilot.**  Nothing here feeds ``data/final``.  The module takes the two
tables written by :mod:`utils.scraping.scraper_amaterskedivadlo` (places, ensembles) and
asks the one question that decides whether the source is worth building on: *how evenly
is it documented* — across town sizes, across Bohemia and Moravia, across Czech- and
German-speaking districts — before any of it is read as a measure of associational life.

(Not to be confused with :mod:`utils.parsing.theater`, which is the *war* theatre —
Russia / Italy / France.)

What "before 1914" means when a year is fuzzy
---------------------------------------------
An ensemble's start is printed as a year, a decade (``191x``) or a century (``19xx``) and
is carried with its precision.  :func:`starts_before` is the single rule:

    year      1913            -> yes        1914            -> no
    decade    190x (≤1909)    -> yes        191x (1910–19)  -> ambiguous     192x -> no
    century   18xx (≤1899)    -> yes        19xx            -> ambiguous

"Before 1914" in every table below means **yes** — the ambiguous are counted and shown
beside it, never folded in.

The join
--------
A database place (present-day obec / místní část, with coordinates) is tied to a row of
``settlements_1910`` (the ČSÚ lexikon crosswalk; coordinates for about half the obce and
few hamlets) in three tiers, most trusted first:

    name+coords     same normalised name, both geocoded, ≤ ``max_km`` apart
    name+okres      same normalised name, the settlement not geocoded, and the place's
                    present-day okres on the settlement's okres timeline (``okres_all``)
                    — accepted only where that leaves exactly one candidate on each side
    name+polygon    same normalised name, the settlement not geocoded, and the place's own
                    point inside the settlement's 1910 okres (MPIDR court polygons, 1 km
                    near-miss repair) — again only one candidate on each side
    fuzzy+coords    names ≥ ``min_similarity`` alike, ≤ ``fuzzy_km`` apart

A place's names are its own, the former names the database prints and a city part's own
name (:func:`place_name_keys`); a settlement is a candidate only if it has a 1910 okres
(``has_okres_1910``; Prague's eight quarters are given okres Praha, audit 2026-11-11 C1).

The match is one-to-one on both sides and the result has exactly one row per place —
both asserted.  Inside one build the settlement is addressed by its row position,
``settlement_row``; the saved settlement table is keyed by ``settlement_id``, the key
``settlements_1910`` has carried since it was given one (a name alone is no key: it can
be an *obec* and an *osada* in the same okres).

Town size
---------
There is **no settlement-level 1910 population in the repo** (the ČSÚ lexikon volume that
carries it is a PDF whose digits do not extract), so size is proxied by three classes read
off what the crosswalk does carry: the seat of a 1910 judicial district, any other
commune, and a dependent hamlet or part.  If the settlements frame is given a
``population_1910`` column, :func:`coverage_tables` bands on that instead.

The chronicle (0.2.0)
---------------------
Each place's ``chronicle_text`` is a run of notes, one per line, two in three opening
with a date (``1895-1938 DS Sokola``, ``Od 1881``, ``Koncem 19. stol.``, ``V 80.
letech``).  :func:`chronicle_lines` reads every line into a table keyed ``(geo_id,
line_no)``: its kind (dated *event*, *undated* note, periodical *citation*, the
database's *admin* note on the present okres, *heading*, *separator*), its leading date
as start and end **intervals** (so ``191x``, ``kolem 1850`` and ``před 1900`` each keep
their width), the associations it names and whether it is puppet theatre.  Rules only;
a bare decade takes its century from the dated line above it, and
:func:`century_inference_check` measures that rule where the century is printed.
Nothing here is written to ``data/final``.

Clauses (0.4.0)
---------------
One line is often several events (``1887-1934 SDO, 1914 32 členů.``), so
:func:`chronicle_clauses` cuts each note wherever a new date opens after a comma, a
semicolon or a full stop — never inside brackets, a quoted title, the line's leading
date, or a dated newspaper report — keyed ``(geo_id, line_no, clause_no)``.  Each clause
carries its own date interval, the other years it prints, and the :data:`EVENT_CUES` its
words point to: the codebook's draft, which the author rules on before any of it is a
code (D-140).

The measure (0.5.0)
-------------------
The author ruled each type's role and twelve design calls (D-141; :data:`CODEBOOK_ROLES`
and the constants beside it).  :func:`code_clauses` applies them; :func:`evidence_table`
puts the ensemble list, the coded clauses and the first reports into one interval form
and gives each company one ``company_id`` across sources; :func:`place_year_panel` turns
that into Czech amateur theatre per place and year, 1780–1913, every measure *certain*
and *possible*; :func:`place_units` gives each place its 1910 settlement, okres and court
(D-222) and :func:`area_year_tables` sums the panel to them and to the census's pooled okres.
Written to ``data/interim/theatre/`` by the pilot runner; nothing reaches the persons.

Ensemble pages (0.6.0)
----------------------
An ensemble's own page (scraper step C) gives the decades it was active (*Působení*), an
end or last report, and a chronicle of its own.  By the author's rulings (D-145): a
listed decade makes the company *possible* across it, never certain, and a page that
lists decades replaces B1's open end, so the company is possible only in those decades
(a "…" gap adds nothing); a printed end closes the span, certain from start to end; and
the ensemble's chronicle is cut and coded like a place's, its company clauses tied to
that ensemble (:func:`ensemble_chronicle_clauses`).  A company's possible years are the
union of its records' ranges, no longer the hull, so a gap between two decades stays
empty.

The codebook rulings (0.13.0)
-----------------------------
The author's fourteen rulings on what the blind check (D-228) found the codebook did not
settle (D-254, ``reference/places/theatre_codebook_rulings.csv``).  In the rules:
company evidence on a place's chronicle needs a local theatre body the clause names
(Q1: `active` alone is activity; school, student, church and travelling players and an
umbrella union never a company), and on a company's own page every dated note of it is
a company act unless it names another performer (Q5, Q7, Q13); Czech means Czech played
(Q4: a Czech title counts, `české hry nepovolovány` does not; pre-1848 school or church
theatre of unstated language is possible, never a company); a bare *date + name* line is
`listed` only with a body word, else `name_only`, which the model reads (Q8); a century's
end is its last decade and its middle the half ±5 (Q9); a decline is not a pause, and a
pause never turns a dated performance possible (Q11); a hedge covers what it qualifies,
not a title or a detail (Q12); a dated clause printing more years for the theatre goes to
the model, whose interval then stands, and the rules read the last printed end and an
earlier `od` start (Q6).  Plus the rare cases: a pointer to a list records nothing, a
word in a play's title is no cue, a building's founding is not the company's, a year in
a full date (`8.2.1903`) is read, a cast list is members, and a hired hall on a company's
page is the company's act with its theatre possible only.

Usage
-----
    from utils.parsing import amateur_theatre as at
    tables = at.coverage_tables(places, ensembles, settlements, districts,
                                okresy=["Kutná Hora", "Trutnov", "Přerov"])
    at.coverage_report(tables)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import unicodedata

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from rapidfuzz import fuzz

__version__ = "0.13.1"  # 0.13.1 D-255: a register court the 1910 backbone lacks (Slavonice, Třešť) is not taken, so the place falls to its 1910 court (D-122, D-208); clause rules unchanged from 0.13.0. 0.13.0 D-254: the codebook rulings; 0.12.0 D-224; 0.11.0 D-223: audit A2–A7
# 0.10.0 D-222: city/former-name join, register courts, census okres; 0.9.0 D-221; 0.8.0 D-214
# 0.5.0: the rulings, evidence table, place × year panel, area sums (D-141)

PRE_WAR_CUTOFF = 1914
EARTH_RADIUS_KM = 6371.0088          # IUGG mean radius
POPULATION_BANDS = [0, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, np.inf]
POPULATION_LABELS = ["<500", "500–999", "1,000–1,999", "2,000–4,999", "5,000+"]
# 1910 okres by its Czech-speaking share (census Umgangssprache)
LANGUAGE_BANDS = [0, 0.5, 0.9, 1.01]
LANGUAGE_LABELS = ["German-majority (<50% Czech)", "mixed (50–90% Czech)", "Czech (90%+)"]
MIN_OKRES_SETTLEMENTS = 20           # smaller 1910 okresy are left out of the spread table


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Names and distance
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_PAREN = re.compile(r"\s*\([^)]*\)")
_VIZ = re.compile(r"\s+viz\s+.*$", re.I)
_FORMERLY = re.compile(r",\s*do\s+\d{4}\b.*$", re.I)
# the database's other notes on a name (audit 2026-11-11 C1): a former name — ", dříve X",
# "/dříve X/", ", původně X", ", někdy X" — and an okres qualifier, ", o. X" / ", okres X"
_FORMER_NAME = re.compile(r"(?:,|/|\(|^|\s)\s*(?:dříve|původně|někdy)\s+([^,()]+?)\s*[/)]?\s*(?=,|$)", re.I)
_UNTIL_YEAR = re.compile(r",\s*do\s+\d{4}\s+([^,()]+?)\s*(?=,|$)", re.I)
_OKRES_TAIL = re.compile(r",\s*(?:o\.|okres)\s+.*$", re.I)
_NON_WORD = re.compile(r"[^\w]+", re.UNICODE)
_CITY_PART = re.compile(r"^.+\s[ivxl]+\s(.+)$")
#: The present-day cities whose parts the database names "City-Part" or "City N-Part"
#: (``Praha-Žižkov``, ``Plzeň 5-Křimice``).  Counted on the 2026-11-11 places table: as the
#: head of a hyphenated name Praha 50, Ostrava 32, Brno 31, Plzeň 28, Ústí nad Labem 3;
#: every other head occurs once and is a compound name (``Rájec-Jestřebí``), not a city part.
CITY_PREFIXES = ("Praha", "Brno", "Ostrava", "Plzeň", "Ústí nad Labem")
_CITY_PREFIX = re.compile(rf"^(?:{'|'.join(CITY_PREFIXES)})(?:\s+\d+)?\s*-\s*(.+)$")


def _strip_notes(name: str) -> str:
    """The name without its parentheticals, ``viz`` tail, former name or okres qualifier."""
    text = _FORMER_NAME.sub("", _VIZ.sub("", _PAREN.sub("", name)))
    return _OKRES_TAIL.sub("", _FORMERLY.sub("", text)).strip(" ,/")


def normalise_name(name) -> str:
    """A place name reduced to what should be equal across the two sources.

    Case-folded; parentheticals, ``X viz Y`` cross-reference tails, the database's
    ``, do 1925 Bračice`` / ``, dříve Bračice`` former-name notes and its ``, o. Svitavy``
    okres qualifiers dropped; punctuation and hyphens turned into single spaces.
    **Diacritics are kept** — in Czech they separate different villages (*Bělá* / *Bílá*).
    """
    if name is None or (isinstance(name, float) and np.isnan(name)):
        return ""
    return _NON_WORD.sub(" ", _strip_notes(str(name))).strip().casefold()


def place_name_keys(name) -> list[str]:
    """Every key a database place may be filed under in 1910, its own name first.

    Besides :func:`normalise_name`: each former name the database prints (``Týnec nad
    Labem, dříve Labská Týnice`` → *labská týnice*; ``Hřivčice, dříve Dřívčice / Řivčice``
    → both), since the former name is often the one of 1910; and a city part's own name
    (``Praha-Žižkov`` → *žižkov*, ``Plzeň 5-Křimice`` → *křimice*, :data:`CITY_PREFIXES`),
    since in 1910 the part was a commune of its own.  Duplicates and empty keys dropped.
    """
    own = normalise_name(name)
    if not own:
        return []
    raw = str(name)
    keys = [own]
    formers = _FORMER_NAME.findall(_PAREN.sub(lambda m: m.group(0).replace("(", ", ").replace(")", ""), raw))
    formers += _UNTIL_YEAR.findall(raw)                 # ", do 1925 Bračice": the name until 1925
    for former in formers:
        keys += [normalise_name(part) for part in former.split("/")]
    part = _CITY_PREFIX.match(_strip_notes(raw))
    if part:
        keys.append(normalise_name(part.group(1)))
    return list(dict.fromkeys(k for k in keys if k))


def city_part_name(name_key: str) -> str | None:
    """The part's own name where the lexikon files it under its city.

    The register heads a village since absorbed by a town as ``HRANICE IV-DRAHOTUŠE`` or
    ``PŘEROV VII-ČEKYNĚ``; the database calls it *Drahotuše*, *Čekyně*.  Returns the part
    after the roman numeral, or None for an ordinary name.
    """
    m = _CITY_PART.match(name_key or "")
    return m.group(1) if m else None


def strip_diacritics(text: str) -> str:
    return "".join(c for c in unicodedata.normalize("NFD", text) if not unicodedata.combining(c))


def haversine_km(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2):
    """Great-circle distance in km (vectorised; broadcasts)."""
    lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2 = (np.radians(np.asarray(v, dtype=float)) for v in (lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2))
    a = np.sin((lat2 - lat1) / 2) ** 2 + np.cos(lat1) * np.cos(lat2) * np.sin((lon2 - lon1) / 2) ** 2
    return 2 * EARTH_RADIUS_KM * np.arcsin(np.sqrt(a))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The 1910 settlement side
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def okres_tokens(okres_all) -> list[str]:
    """The okres timeline of a settlement as a list (stray brackets and spaces removed)."""
    if not isinstance(okres_all, str):
        return []
    return [t for t in (re.sub(r"\s+", " ", tok.strip(" ()")) for tok in okres_all.split("|")) if t]


def settlement_frame(settlements: pd.DataFrame, districts: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """``settlements_1910`` with the columns the join and the tabulation need.

    Adds ``settlement_row`` (row position, the working key inside one build; what is saved
    is keyed by the table's own ``settlement_id``, :data:`AREA_LEVELS`), ``name_key``,
    ``name_key_alt`` (:func:`city_part_name`), ``okres_tokens``, ``okres_now`` (the last
    okres on the timeline), ``in_1910`` (the
    settlement has a resolved 1910 okres and status), ``okres_1910_cs`` (the district's
    name from ``districts_1910``, free of the register's OCR breaks) and ``size_class``.
    """
    out = settlements.reset_index(drop=True).copy()
    out.insert(0, "settlement_row", np.arange(len(out)))
    out["name_key"] = out["cs_name"].map(normalise_name)
    out["name_key_alt"] = out["name_key"].map(city_part_name)
    out["okres_tokens"] = out["okres_all"].map(okres_tokens)
    out["okres_now"] = out["okres_tokens"].map(lambda t: t[-1] if t else None)
    out = _prague_quarters(out)
    out["in_1910"] = out["okres_id"].notna() & out["status_1910"].notna()
    # what the area sums need is the 1910 okres; the status only sizes the place (audit C1:
    # a row whose status the lexicon's OCR broke, "Kosmanosy o bec", still has its okres)
    out["has_okres_1910"] = out["okres_id"].notna()

    seats: set[tuple[int, str]] = set()
    out["okres_1910_cs"] = out["okres_1910"]
    if districts is not None:
        codes = districts["okres_code"].str.split("-", expand=True).astype(int)
        okres_id = codes[0] * 1000 + codes[1]
        names = dict(zip(okres_id, districts["okres_cs"]))
        out["okres_1910_cs"] = out["okres_id"].map(names).fillna(out["okres_1910"])
        seats = set(zip(okres_id, districts["gerichtsbezirk_cs"].map(normalise_name)))

    is_seat = pd.Series([(o, n) in seats for o, n in zip(out["okres_id"], out["name_key"])],
                        index=out.index)
    commune = out["status_1910"].eq("obec")
    out["size_class"] = pd.Series("3 hamlet / part", index=out.index, dtype=object)
    out.loc[commune, "size_class"] = "2 other commune"
    out.loc[commune & is_seat, "size_class"] = "1 court-seat town"
    out.loc[~out["in_1910"], "size_class"] = None
    if "population_1910" in out.columns:
        out["size_class"] = pd.cut(out["population_1910"], POPULATION_BANDS,
                                   labels=POPULATION_LABELS, right=False).astype(object)
    return out


#: Prague's quarters as the lexicon prints them in 1910 (``Praha IV. Hradčany``): the city
#: was quarters I–VIII, and the lexicon gives them no okres (audit 2026-11-11 C1).
_PRAGUE_QUARTER = re.compile(r"^Praha\s+[IVX]+\.", re.I)


def _prague_quarters(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Prague's eight 1910 quarters get okres Praha, the okres of the lexicon's own
    ``Praha`` row (:mod:`utils.parsing.lexikon` adds it), flagged in ``prague_quarter``;
    a frame with no such row is returned unchanged."""
    praha = frame.loc[frame["name_key"].eq("praha") & frame["okres_id"].notna(), "okres_id"].unique()
    if len(praha) != 1:
        return frame
    printed = frame.get("name_1910", pd.Series("", index=frame.index)).fillna("").astype(str)
    headword = frame["cs_name"].fillna("").astype(str)                   # PRAHA VIII. STARÁ LIBEŇ
    quarter = (printed.str.match(_PRAGUE_QUARTER) | headword.str.match(_PRAGUE_QUARTER)) & frame["okres_id"].isna()
    out = frame.copy()
    out.loc[quarter, "okres_id"] = praha[0]
    out.loc[quarter, "okres_1910"] = "Praha"
    out["prague_quarter"] = quarter
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The join
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_TYPE_PREFERENCE = {"Obec": {"obec": 0}, "Místní část": {"osada": 0, "cast": 0},
                    "Část": {"osada": 0, "cast": 0}}


def _type_penalty(place_type, status) -> int:
    """0 where the place's type and the settlement's 1910 status agree, else 1."""
    return _TYPE_PREFERENCE.get(place_type, {}).get(status, 1)


def _point_in_okres(pairs: pd.DataFrame, locator) -> np.ndarray:
    """Whether each pair's place point lies in the pair's settlement's 1910 okres: the
    court polygon containing it, or one of that okres's courts within
    :data:`utils.parsing.spatial.SNAP_TOL_M` (the MPIDR outlines are generalised; D-35)."""
    from utils.parsing import spatial as sp
    if pairs.empty:
        return np.zeros(0, bool)
    xs, ys = sp.laea_forward(pairs["lon"].to_numpy(float), pairs["lat"].to_numpy(float))
    hits, cache = [], {}
    for px, py, okres in zip(xs, ys, pairs["okres_id"].astype(int)):
        key = (round(float(px), 1), round(float(py), 1), okres)
        if key not in cache:
            court, _code, _snapped = locator.locate_snapped(px, py, okres)
            cache[key] = court is not None and int(court) // 1000 == okres
        hits.append(cache[key])
    return np.array(hits, bool)


def join_places_to_settlements(
    places: pd.DataFrame,
    settlements: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    max_km: float = 5.0,
    fuzzy_km: float = 2.0,
    min_similarity: float = 85.0,
    locator=None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Tie each database place to at most one 1910 settlement, by distance with a name check.

    Args:
        places: the scraper's places table (``geo_id, name, type, lat, lon, okres``).
        settlements: :func:`settlement_frame` output.
        max_km: furthest an exact-name pair may be apart.
        fuzzy_km: furthest a near-name pair may be apart.
        min_similarity: rapidfuzz ratio (0–100) on the normalised, de-accented names.
        locator: a :class:`utils.parsing.spatial.CourtLocator`; with it, tier 2b
            (``name+polygon``) runs.  Without it the join is the three tiers above.

    Returns:
        One row per place — ``geo_id, settlement_row, match_method, distance_km,
        name_similarity`` — with ``settlement_row`` missing where nothing matched and
        ``match_method`` saying why (``unmatched: no such name`` / ``… too far`` /
        ``… ambiguous``).  Asserted: one row per place, no settlement used twice.
    """
    P = places[["geo_id", "name", "type", "lat", "lon", "okres"]].copy()
    P["name_key"] = P["name"].map(normalise_name)
    # a place is reachable under its former name and, a city part, its own (place_name_keys)
    P_keys = (P.drop(columns="name_key").assign(name_key=P["name"].map(place_name_keys))
              .explode("name_key").dropna(subset=["name_key"]))
    # only a row with a 1910 okres can carry a place into the area sums; a present-day merged
    # town with none ("BENÁTKY NAD JIZEROU") would otherwise win on distance (audit C1)
    candidates = settlements[settlements["has_okres_1910"]] if "has_okres_1910" in settlements else settlements
    S = candidates[["settlement_row", "name_key", "status_1910", "lat", "lon", "okres_tokens", "okres_id"]]
    # a city part is reachable under its own name as well as under "CITY IV-PART"
    alt = candidates.loc[candidates["name_key_alt"].notna(), S.columns.drop("name_key")].assign(
        name_key=candidates["name_key_alt"].dropna())
    by_name = pd.concat([S, alt[S.columns]], ignore_index=True)

    pairs = P_keys.merge(by_name, on="name_key", suffixes=("", "_s"))
    pairs = pairs[pairs["name_key"] != ""]
    geocoded = pairs["lat_s"].notna()
    pairs["distance_km"] = np.where(
        geocoded, haversine_km(pairs["lat"], pairs["lon"], pairs["lat_s"].fillna(0),
                               pairs["lon_s"].fillna(0)), np.nan)
    pairs["okres_ok"] = [o in toks for o, toks in zip(pairs["okres"], pairs["okres_tokens"])]
    pairs["penalty"] = [_type_penalty(t, s) for t, s in zip(pairs["type"], pairs["status_1910"])]

    used_places: dict[int, tuple] = {}
    used_settlements: set[int] = set()

    def accept(geo_id, row, method, km, similarity) -> None:
        used_places[int(geo_id)] = (int(row), method, km, similarity)
        used_settlements.add(int(row))

    # tier 1 — exact name, both geocoded, close: nearest pair first
    near = pairs[geocoded & (pairs["distance_km"] <= max_km)].sort_values(["distance_km", "penalty"])
    for r in near.itertuples():
        if r.geo_id not in used_places and r.settlement_row not in used_settlements:
            accept(r.geo_id, r.settlement_row, "name+coords", round(float(r.distance_km), 2), 100.0)

    # tier 2 — exact name, settlement not geocoded, okres on its timeline, unique both ways
    loose = pairs[~geocoded & pairs["okres_ok"]
                  & ~pairs["geo_id"].isin(list(used_places))
                  & ~pairs["settlement_row"].isin(used_settlements)]
    loose = loose[loose["penalty"] == loose.groupby("geo_id")["penalty"].transform("min")]
    n_for_place = loose.groupby("geo_id")["settlement_row"].transform("nunique")
    n_for_settlement = loose.groupby("settlement_row")["geo_id"].transform("nunique")
    ambiguous = set(loose.loc[(n_for_place > 1) | (n_for_settlement > 1), "geo_id"])
    for r in loose[(n_for_place == 1) & (n_for_settlement == 1)].itertuples():
        accept(r.geo_id, r.settlement_row, "name+okres", np.nan, 100.0)

    # tier 2b — exact name, settlement not geocoded, and the place's own point lies in the
    # settlement's 1910 okres (MPIDR polygons, near misses of 1 km repaired), unique both ways.
    # Reaches what tier 2 cannot: a city part whose 1910 row has no coordinates and whose
    # okres timeline never names today's okres (Praha-Žižkov → ŽIŽKOV, okres Žižkov; audit C1)
    if locator is not None:
        rest = pairs[~geocoded & pairs["okres_id"].notna() & pairs["lat"].notna()
                     & ~pairs["geo_id"].isin(list(used_places))
                     & ~pairs["settlement_row"].isin(used_settlements)].copy()
        rest["in_okres"] = _point_in_okres(rest, locator)
        rest = rest[rest["in_okres"]]
        rest = rest[rest["penalty"] == rest.groupby("geo_id")["penalty"].transform("min")]
        n_for_place = rest.groupby("geo_id")["settlement_row"].transform("nunique")
        n_for_settlement = rest.groupby("settlement_row")["geo_id"].transform("nunique")
        ambiguous |= set(rest.loc[(n_for_place > 1) | (n_for_settlement > 1), "geo_id"])
        for r in rest[(n_for_place == 1) & (n_for_settlement == 1)].drop_duplicates(
                ["geo_id", "settlement_row"]).itertuples():
            accept(r.geo_id, r.settlement_row, "name+polygon", np.nan, 100.0)

    # tier 3 — near-identical name, very close
    left = P[~P["geo_id"].isin(list(used_places)) & P["lat"].notna() & (P["name_key"] != "")]
    right = S[~S["settlement_row"].isin(used_settlements) & S["lat"].notna()]
    fuzzy_rows = []
    if len(left) and len(right):
        right_lat, right_lon = right["lat"].to_numpy(), right["lon"].to_numpy()
        right_keys = right["name_key"].map(strip_diacritics).to_numpy()
        right_ids = right["settlement_row"].to_numpy()
        for p in left.itertuples():
            km = haversine_km(p.lat, p.lon, right_lat, right_lon)
            key = strip_diacritics(p.name_key)
            for j in np.flatnonzero(km <= fuzzy_km):
                similarity = fuzz.ratio(key, right_keys[j])
                if similarity >= min_similarity:
                    fuzzy_rows.append((float(km[j]), -similarity, p.geo_id, right_ids[j]))
    for km, neg_similarity, geo_id, row in sorted(fuzzy_rows):
        if geo_id not in used_places and row not in used_settlements:
            accept(geo_id, row, "fuzzy+coords", round(km, 2), float(-neg_similarity))

    # why the rest did not match
    has_name = set(pairs["geo_id"])
    too_far = set(pairs.loc[geocoded & (pairs["distance_km"] > max_km), "geo_id"])
    rows = []
    for geo_id in P["geo_id"]:
        if int(geo_id) in used_places:
            rows.append((geo_id, *used_places[int(geo_id)]))
            continue
        reason = ("unmatched: ambiguous" if geo_id in ambiguous
                  else "unmatched: too far" if geo_id in too_far
                  else "unmatched: name elsewhere" if geo_id in has_name
                  else "unmatched: no such name")
        rows.append((geo_id, pd.NA, reason, np.nan, np.nan))
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["geo_id", "settlement_row", "match_method",
                                      "distance_km", "name_similarity"])
    out["settlement_row"] = out["settlement_row"].astype("Int64")

    assert len(out) == len(places) and out["geo_id"].is_unique, "join: not one row per place"
    assert not out["settlement_row"].dropna().duplicated().any(), "join: a settlement matched twice"
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Dates
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_SPAN_OF = {"year": 0, "decade": 9, "century": 99}


def starts_before(year, precision, cutoff: int = PRE_WAR_CUTOFF) -> str:
    """Does a (possibly fuzzy) year fall before ``cutoff``?  ``yes / no / ambiguous / unknown``."""
    if precision not in _SPAN_OF or pd.isna(year):
        return "unknown"
    earliest, latest = int(year), int(year) + _SPAN_OF[precision]
    if latest < cutoff:
        return "yes"
    if earliest >= cutoff:
        return "no"
    return "ambiguous"


_PERIOD_EDGES = [0, 1800, 1850, 1870, 1880, 1890, 1900, 1910, PRE_WAR_CUTOFF, 1920, 1950, 9999]
_PERIOD_LABELS = ["<1800", "1800–49", "1850–69", "1870s", "1880s", "1890s", "1900s",
                  "1910–13", "1914–19", "1920–49", "1950+"]
PERIOD_ORDER = _PERIOD_LABELS + ["191x (decade only)", "century only", "not recorded"]


def first_record_period(year, precision) -> str:
    """The period a place's first report falls in, for the distribution table.

    An exact year goes to its bin.  A decade does too, except ``191x`` — the one decade
    the 1914 line cuts — which is shown as its own row rather than assigned to a side.
    """
    if pd.isna(year) or precision not in _SPAN_OF:
        return "not recorded"
    if precision == "century":
        return "century only"
    if precision == "decade" and int(year) == 1910:
        return "191x (decade only)"
    return _PERIOD_LABELS[int(np.searchsorted(_PERIOD_EDGES, int(year), side="right")) - 1]


def place_dates(places: pd.DataFrame, ensembles: pd.DataFrame,
                cutoff: int = PRE_WAR_CUTOFF) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per place: how many ensembles, and whether theatre is recorded before ``cutoff``.

    ``ensemble_pre`` is True when at least one ensemble certainly starts before the
    cutoff; ``ensemble_ambiguous`` when none certainly does but one may (``191x``);
    ``first_record_pre`` reads the place page's own 'První zpráva'.  Key ``geo_id``.
    """
    E = ensembles.copy()
    E["pre"] = [starts_before(y, p, cutoff) for y, p in zip(E["year_from"], E["year_from_precision"])]
    per_place = E.groupby("geo_id").agg(
        n_ensembles=("ensemble_id", "size"),
        n_pre=("pre", lambda s: int((s == "yes").sum())),
        n_ambiguous=("pre", lambda s: int((s == "ambiguous").sum())),
        n_undated=("pre", lambda s: int((s == "unknown").sum())),
    )
    out = places[["geo_id"]].merge(per_place, on="geo_id", how="left", validate="1:1")
    counts = ["n_ensembles", "n_pre", "n_ambiguous", "n_undated"]
    out[counts] = out[counts].fillna(0).astype(int)
    out["ensemble_pre"] = out["n_pre"] > 0
    out["ensemble_ambiguous"] = (out["n_pre"] == 0) & (out["n_ambiguous"] > 0)
    first = [starts_before(y, p, cutoff) for y, p in
             zip(places["first_record_year"], places["first_record_precision"])]
    out["first_record_pre"] = [f == "yes" for f in first]
    out["first_record_known"] = [f != "unknown" for f in first]
    assert len(out) == len(places)
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What kind of association an ensemble's name points to
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Word-anchored on both sides, with the inflected forms listed: `sokol` must not fire
# inside the town of Sokolov, nor `orel` inside a longer word.  An *Osvětová beseda* is the
# post-1945 state cultural club, not the nineteenth-century reading society, and is left out.
# The first five are the pilot's; the rest were added for the chronicle (0.2.0), from the
# words commonest in its pre-1914 lines that none of the five matched.  "Divadelní spolek"
# is the free-standing amateur dramatic society (SDO, *ochotnická jednota*) — a society of
# its own, not a section of another, so a bare `DS`/`DrO` (which is usually "DS Sokola")
# is not it.  The database's abbreviations are read from its own key
# (``data/raw/theatre/abbreviations.csv``, 0.3.0) and matched **case-sensitively**, so
# `OS` is the *ochotnický spolek* and not the Czech word: SDO, OS, OJ, DJ, JDO, KrDO are
# free-standing dramatic societies; ČOS, ČOJ, ČOB the reading-and-dramatic society
# (*čtenářsko ochotnický spolek / jednota / beseda*), ČOB a beseda too; ČB the Česká
# beseda; NJ, NJS, NJP the national unions.  `ČOS` has a second reading in the key, the
# Sokol union (*Česká / Československá obec sokolská*), so a line naming it is also
# flagged (:data:`AMBIGUOUS_ABBREVIATIONS`).  `DS` (*soubor – skupina – spolek*) and `OB`
# (the post-1945 *osvětová beseda*) stay unread.
ASSOCIATION_PATTERNS: dict[str, re.Pattern] = {
    "Sokol": re.compile(
        r"\bsokol(?:a|u|e|em|ů|ové|sk[áéýou]\w*|stv\w*|ík\w*)?\b", re.I),
    "Hasiči": re.compile(
        r"\bhasič\w*|\bSDH\b", re.I),
    "Beseda": re.compile(
        r"(?<!osvětová\s)(?<!osvětové\s)(?<!osvětovou\s)\bbesed[aáyěou]\b"
        r"|(?-i:\b(?:ČB|ČOB)\b)", re.I),
    "Orel": re.compile(
        r"\borel\b|\borl[aue]\b|\borlem\b|\borelsk\w+", re.I),
    "DTJ": re.compile(
        r"\bDTJ\b|\bD\.\s?T\.\s?J\b|\bdělnick\w+\s+tělo(?:cvičn|výchovn)\w+\s+jednot\w+", re.I),
    "Divadelní spolek": re.compile(
        r"(?-i:\b(?:SDO|OS|OJ|DJ|JDO|KrDO|ČOS|ČOJ|ČOB)\b)"
        r"|\b(?:spol\w*|sdružení|jednot\w*|kroužk?\w*)\s+divadelních\s+ochotník\w*"
        r"|\bochotnick\w*\s+(?:spol\w*|jednot\w*|družstv\w*|sdružení|klub\w*|besed\w*)"
        r"|\bdivadeln\w*\s+(?:spol(?!ečnost)\w*|jednot\w*|družstv\w*|sdružení)"
        r"|\bdramatick\w*\s+(?:spol(?!ečnost)\w*|klub\w*|jednot\w*)", re.I),
    "Čtenářský spolek": re.compile(r"\bčtenářsk\w*|(?-i:\b(?:ČOS|ČOJ|ČOB)\b)", re.I),
    "Pěvecký spolek": re.compile(r"\bpěveck\w*|\bzpěváck\w*", re.I),
    "Vzdělávací spolek": re.compile(r"\bvzdělávac\w*", re.I),
    "Omladina": re.compile(r"\bomladin\w*", re.I),
    # `\b` after the word, so the lookahead cannot be passed by backtracking into it
    "Dělnický spolek": re.compile(r"\bdělnick\w*\b(?!\s+tělo(?:cvičn|výchovn))", re.I),
    "Katolický spolek": re.compile(r"\bkatolick\w*|\btovaryš\w*", re.I),
    "Národní jednota": re.compile(
        r"(?-i:\bNJ[SPV]?\b)|\bnárodní\w*\s+jednot\w*|\bÚMŠ\b|\bmatic\w*\s+školsk\w*", re.I),
    "Škola": re.compile(
        r"\bstudent\w*|\bstuduj\w*|\bgymn[aá][sz]i\w*|\breálk\w*|\bškol\w*|\bžác\w*|\bžák\w*"
        r"|\bučitel\w*|\bpreparand\w*", re.I),
    "Církev": re.compile(
        r"\bjezuit\w*|\bpiarist\w*|\bpremonstr\w*|\bbenediktin\w*|\bminorit\w*|\bkapucín\w*"
        r"|\bklášter\w*|\bkostel\w*|\bfar[aáuyeěo]\b|\bfarní\w*|\bfarář\w*|\bkaplan\w*", re.I),
}


# abbreviations the key reads two ways: labelled by their first reading, and flagged
AMBIGUOUS_ABBREVIATIONS = {
    "ČOS": "čtenářsko ochotnický spolek, or Česká / Československá obec sokolská",
}
_AMBIGUOUS = re.compile(r"\b(" + "|".join(AMBIGUOUS_ABBREVIATIONS) + r")\b")
# membership of the national union of amateur theatres — a union, not a local host
_UMDOC = re.compile(r"\bÚMDOČ\b|(?i:\bústřední\w*\s+matic\w*\s+divadelního)")


def classify_association(name) -> list[str]:
    """Labels of :data:`ASSOCIATION_PATTERNS` a name or a chronicle line matches (possibly none)."""
    if not isinstance(name, str):
        return []
    return [label for label, pattern in ASSOCIATION_PATTERNS.items() if pattern.search(name)]


def association_counts(ensembles: pd.DataFrame, cutoff: int = PRE_WAR_CUTOFF) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series]:
    """Counts of pre-``cutoff`` ensembles by association, and the unclassified names.

    Returns:
        ``(counts, unclassified)`` — counts has one row per label plus *unclassified*,
        *more than one label* and *all pre-1914 ensembles*; ``unclassified`` is the
        frequency table of the names nothing matched, so the remainder can be read.
    """
    E = ensembles.drop_duplicates("ensemble_id").copy()
