    # list of years, each a point of its own (`1905 a 1907 sehráli 10 her` is not 10 a year)
    count = _stated_count(rest, kind)
    # a repertoire line of n plays is at least n performances — unless the clause says its
    # numbers are not this year's (a rate, a running total, another year: the same refusals
    # as a stated number's, second review of D-224) or that the plays were only planned
    # read up to where the line passes to another stretch, as the plays are
    stretch = _OTHER_STRETCH.search(rest)
    scope = rest[:stretch.start()] if stretch else rest
    refused = kind == "point" and (_COUNT_PERIOD.search(scope) or _ALREADY.search(scope)
                                   or _ORDINAL.search(scope) or _another_year_before_count(scope))
    if pd.isna(count) and len(plays) >= 2 and kind in ("point", "span") and not refused \
            and not _PLANNED.search(text):
        count = float(len(plays))
    # a quoted name is a play's title only after a play word (`hru „Loupež“`); an inn's name is not
    play_quotes = [next(g for g in m.groups() if g) for m in _QUOTED_TITLE.finditer(text)
                   if _PLAY_BEFORE_QUOTE.search(text[max(0, m.start() - 30):m.start()])]
    czech = czech_named(text, play_quotes + plays_raw)
    return {"end_inside": int(end.group(1)) if end else np.nan,
            "start_inside": float(min(earlier)) if earlier else np.nan,
            "count_stated": count,
            "titles": "|".join(t for t in titles if t),
            "attendance_n": max(audience) if audience else np.nan,
            "czech_named": czech,
            "bilingual": "german" in types and czech}


#: what :func:`code_clause` returns, in order (an empty frame gets the columns too)
CODE_CLAUSE_FIELDS = ["end_inside", "start_inside", "count_stated", "titles", "attendance_n",
                      "czech_named", "bilingual"]


def code_clauses(clauses: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """:func:`chronicle_clauses` with the rulings applied (D-141): one row per clause, same key.

    Adds :func:`code_clause`'s fields and
    ``czech_activity`` — the clause puts *Czech* amateur theatre in its place: some type
    has an Activity role (a quoted title is a performance), or it is a company's act or end
    (D-221, below); and it is not German or Latin unless it also names Czech players or
    plays (B8 as amended by D-221: a Czech company that also plays in German is Czech
    activity, recorded as bilingual), not puppet theatre, and not school or church theatre
    before 1848 unless the plays are Czech (B6 as amended by D-221; one that may straddle
    1848 counts, and is possible only by its interval);
    ``company`` — it records a company over time (listed, active, founded, statutes), or a
    company's act (D-221: officers, members, a merger, a stage of its own — on the
    company's own page; the first three on a place's chronicle when a theatre company is
    named); ``company_act`` marks a clause that is company evidence by D-221 alone, which
    is a point in time and never open-ended;
    ``hedged`` — read as possible only (B4), and so is a company's end recorded with no
    other activity (D-221: a dissolution is often formal, years after the last play);
    ``needs_model`` — the rules leave it open: an undated clause printing a year inside
    (B11), or a dated one no type reaches.

    As the codebook rulings of D-254 amend it (Q-numbers of
    ``reference/places/theatre_codebook_rulings.csv``):

    * *company, on a place's chronicle* (Q1) — ``active`` is company evidence only when the
      clause names a local theatre body (:func:`names_company`); a founding or statutes
      only when the body founded is not another kind (a DTJ, a choir: :data:`_OTHER_BODY`);
      school, student, church or travelling players and an umbrella union are never a
      company unless a local company is named beside them;
    * *company, on a company's own page* (Q5, Q7, Q13) — every dated note of the page's
      company is its act, a point in its year: a play, a list of titles, a meeting, an
      evening, its end; not one that names another performer (a travelling company, the
      model's ``named_group``); a hired hall alone (``venue``) is the company's act with its
      theatre possible only (``activity_hedged``, rare case 127);
    * *Czech* (Q4) — :func:`czech_named`; pre-1848 school or church theatre of unstated
      language is Czech activity *possible only* and never a company;
    * a ``decline`` is activity, possible only (Q11); ``name_only`` activity, no company (Q8);
    * a body founded and theatre taken up ``postupně`` / ``později`` starts after the
      founding (``after``: possible, certain in no year, Q10);
    * ``needs_model`` also for a dated clause printing other years (Q6) and a ``name_only`` (Q8);
    * the model's readings (:func:`amateur_theatre_model.apply_readings`) add
      ``performer_kind`` (Q1, Q7), ``elsewhere`` — theatre played in another place, which
      counts nowhere here (Q7) — and ``model_titles_raw`` (Q4), when present.
    """
    out = clauses.copy()
    types = out["cues"].fillna("").str.split("|").map(lambda t: [x for x in t if x])
    coded = pd.DataFrame([code_clause(t, d, ty) for t, d, ty in zip(out["text"], out["date_raw"], types)],
                         index=out.index, columns=CODE_CLAUSE_FIELDS)
    out = pd.concat([out.drop(columns=[c for c in coded if c in out]), coded], axis=1)
    has = lambda name: types.map(lambda t, n=name: n in t)                      # noqa: E731
    any_of = lambda names: types.map(lambda t, s=frozenset(names): bool(s & set(t)))   # noqa: E731
    activity = types.map(lambda t: bool(ACTIVITY_TYPES & (set(t) | ({"performance"} if "title" in t else set()))))
    text = out["text"].fillna("")
    blank = pd.Series(False, index=out.index)
    czech = out["czech_named"].astype(bool)
    if "model_titles_raw" in out:
        czech |= out["model_titles_raw"].fillna("").map(lambda s: bool(_CZECH_LETTERS.search(str(s))))
    on_page = (out["ensemble_id"].notna() if "ensemble_id" in out else blank).astype(bool)
    performer = out["performer_kind"].fillna("") if "performer_kind" in out else pd.Series("", index=out.index)
    named = text.map(names_company)
    umbrella = text.str.contains(_UMBRELLA) & ~named
    other_body = text.str.contains(_OTHER_BODY) & ~named
    # Q1: players who are no local company, on a place's chronicle
    not_local = ~on_page & (((has("school_church") | has("travelling") | umbrella) & ~named)
                            | performer.isin(NOT_LOCAL_PERFORMERS))
    # Q7, Q13: on a company's page, a clause that names another performer is not the page's —
    # also plain amateurs on the page of a body that is no theatre company (`zde ochotníci h.
    # operu` on a singing society's page, clause 137 of the blind check)
    ensemble_name = out["ensemble_name"].fillna("") if "ensemble_name" in out else pd.Series("", index=out.index)
    page_not_theatre = on_page & ensemble_name.str.contains(_OTHER_BODY) & ~ensemble_name.map(names_company) \
        & ~ensemble_name.str.contains(r"(?i:\bdivadl\w*|\bdivadeln\w*|\bochotn\w*)")
    # amateurs the clause does not tie to the page's own body (no `spolkoví`, no `ochotnický
    # odbor`, no word of the page's name); the model's `page_ensemble` overrides the text
    tied = pd.Series([_tied_to_page(t, n) for t, n in zip(text, ensemble_name)], index=out.index, dtype=bool)
    amateurs = performer.eq("unnamed_amateurs") | (
        text.str.contains(r"(?i:\bochotn\w*)") & ~tied & ~performer.eq("page_ensemble"))
    # another body organised or gave it, or another kind of body was founded (clause 34; a DTJ founding)
    organiser = pd.Series([_other_organiser(t, n) for t, n in zip(text, ensemble_name)], index=out.index, dtype=bool)
    other_founding = any_of({"founded", "statutes"}) & text.str.contains(_OTHER_BODY) & ~named \
        & ~ensemble_name.str.contains(_OTHER_BODY)
    other_performer = on_page & (performer.isin(OTHER_PERFORMERS) | (has("travelling") & ~named)
                                 | (page_not_theatre & amateurs) | organiser | other_founding)
    # a short line that names only people (`1907 předseda Jan Khom.`) is read as `listed`
    # (D-141), but it records an act, not a company existing on: a point, as D-221's acts are
    named_listing = has("listed") & (has("officers") | has("members"))
    founding = any_of({"founded", "statutes"}) & ~other_body
    place_strict = (has("active") & named) | founding | (has("listed") & ~named_listing)
    # a play, a count or a cast list beside `active` is a dated act, a point — not a company recorded on (Q13)
    page_strict = (has("active") & ~any_of({"performance", "title", "count", "members"})) \
        | any_of({"founded", "statutes"}) | (has("listed") & ~named_listing)
    strict_company = (~on_page & place_strict & ~not_local) | (on_page & page_strict & ~other_performer)
    # D-221 on a place's chronicle; D-254 Q5/Q13 on a company's page: any dated note of it
    typed = types.map(lambda t: bool(set(t) - {"hedged"}))
    dated = out["date_source"].ne("none") | out["start_lo"].notna() | out["start_hi"].notna() | out["end_hi"].notna()
    place_act = ~on_page & named & any_of(PLACE_COMPANY_ACT_TYPES) & ~not_local
    pause_alone = has("pause") & types.map(lambda t: not ((ACTIVITY_TYPES - {"active"}) & set(t)))
    page_act = on_page & typed & dated & ~other_performer & ~pause_alone
    act = place_act | page_act
    ended_alone = has("ended") & (on_page | named) & ~activity
    # Q10: a body founded, then theatre taken up gradually or later — a start after the founding
    later_start = has("founded") & ~named & text.str.contains(_LATER_THEATRE) & out["start_lo"].notna()
    out.loc[later_start, "start_hi"] = np.nan
    out.loc[later_start, "date_form"] = "after"
    # B6 as D-254 Q4 reads it: pre-1848 school or church theatre of unstated language is possible
    early_school = has("school_church") & (out["start_hi"] < SCHOOL_CHURCH_FROM) & ~czech
    # Latin school drama is a thing of the years before 1848; after, `latina` is a play's
    # title (Myslivecká latina), not the language played
    latin = has("latin") & (out["start_hi"] < SCHOOL_CHURCH_FROM)
    foreign = (has("german") | latin) & ~czech
    elsewhere = out["elsewhere"].fillna(False).astype(bool) if "elsewhere" in out else blank
    # Q1: a theatre union of the district (`Divadelní župa Pojizerská, 25 jednot`) is theatre
    # there — activity, never a company
    union_theatre = text.str.contains(_UMBRELLA) & text.str.contains(r"(?i:\bdivadeln\w*|\bochotn\w*)") & dated
    out["czech_activity"] = (activity | act | ended_alone | union_theatre) & ~foreign & ~out["puppet"] & ~elsewhere
    out["company"] = (strict_company | (named_listing & ~not_local & ~other_performer) | act) \
        & ~out["puppet"] & ~foreign & ~early_school & ~has("name_only").where(~on_page, False) & ~elsewhere
    out["company"] &= ~(later_start & ~on_page)
    out["company_act"] = out["company"] & ~strict_company
    out["performance"] = (has("performance") | has("title") | has("count")) & ~elsewhere
    decline_alone = has("decline") & ~any_of({"performance", "title", "count", "founded", "statutes", "listed"})
    out["hedged"] = has("hedged") | ended_alone | decline_alone | early_school
    # rare case 127: a hall the company hired, and nothing else — the company that year, its plays unknown in time
    venue_alone = types.map(lambda t: set(t) - {"hedged"} == {"venue"})
    titled = pd.Series([bool(title_spans(t, d)) for t, d in zip(text, out["date_raw"])], index=out.index, dtype=bool)
    hall_only = venue_alone & text.str.contains(_HALL) & ~text.str.contains(_STAGE_OR_PLAY) & ~titled
    out["activity_hedged"] = hall_only & act
    no_type = types.map(lambda t: not (set(t) - {"hedged", "title"})) | (
        ~on_page & types.map(lambda t: not (set(t) - {"hedged", "title", "company_note"})))
    # Q6: a dated clause that prints other years than its date's — the model reads them
    other_years = [_other_years(y, lo, hi, ehi, elo) for y, lo, hi, ehi, elo in
                   zip(out["years_inside"].fillna(""), out["start_lo"], out["start_hi"], out["end_hi"], out["end_lo"])]
    permit_title = has("permit") & ~has("title") & text.str.contains(r"\bhr[auy]\s+[A-ZČŘŠŽÚ]")
    out["needs_model"] = ((out["date_source"] == "none") & out["years_inside"].fillna("").ne("")) | (
        (out["date_source"] != "none") & (no_type | has("name_only") | permit_title
                                          | pd.Series(other_years, index=out.index)))
    for column in ("founded", "statutes", "permit", "first", "proceeds", "national_theatre",
                   "school_church", "travelling", "german", "latin", "attendance"):
        out[column] = has(column)
    out["elsewhere"] = elsewhere
    # B12 as the audit narrowed it (A2): a pause is a clause that records the pause and no
    # other activity — `činnost přerušena` names the activity it pauses (`active`), but
    # `1885 založen, později přerušena` is a founding first and dates the founding
    out["pause"] = has("pause") & types.map(lambda t: not ((ACTIVITY_TYPES - {"active"}) & set(t)))
    # and such a clause is what the codebook rules a pause, coded only: not activity, not a company
    out.loc[out["pause"], ["czech_activity", "company", "company_act", "activity_hedged"]] = False
    return out


def _other_years(years_inside: str, start_lo, start_hi, end_hi, end_lo=np.nan) -> bool:
    """Does a dated clause print a year outside its own date (D-254 Q6)?  A decade (`188x`)
    counts by its first year; a year inside the date's interval is the date's own — unless
    the date is fuzzy (`koncem 19. stol.`, `kolem 1850`): there an exact year printed inside
    may be the theatre's own and is read too.  An end-only date (`do 1868`) is its end."""
    known = [v for v in (start_lo, start_hi, end_lo, end_hi) if not pd.isna(v)]
    if not known:
        return False
    lo, hi = min(known), max(known)
    fuzzy = not pd.isna(start_lo) and not pd.isna(start_hi) and start_lo != start_hi
    for token in str(years_inside).split("|"):
        if token and token[:4].replace("x", "0").replace("X", "0").isdigit():
            year = int(token[:4].replace("x", "0").replace("X", "0"))
            exact = token[:4].isdigit()
            if not lo <= year <= hi or (fuzzy and exact):
                return True
    return False


# rare case 127: a hall hired — an inn, a hall, a town hall, a Sokol hall, a castle — with no
# stage or equipment of its own (those stay D-221 acts) and no playing, staging or title
_HALL = re.compile(r"\bhostin\w*|\bhospod(?!ář)\w*|\bsál\w*|\bradnic\w*|\bsokolovn\w*|\bzám(?:ek|ku)\b", re.I)
_STAGE_OR_PLAY = re.compile(r"\bjevišt\w*|\bopon\w*|\bdekorac\w*|\bkulis\w*|\bhrán\w*|\bhrál\w*|\buv\.|\buved\w*"
                            r"|\bvystoupen\w*|\bsehrán\w*|\bpředstaven\w*|\baktovk\w*|:\s*[A-ZČŘŠŽÚ]", re.I)
# words by which a clause ties its players to the page's own body (`spolkoví ochotníci`, `jeho ochotníci`)
_TIE_WORDS = re.compile(r"(?i:\bspolkov\w*|\bspolku\b|\bochotnick\w*\s+(?:odbor|soubor|kroužek|družin|spol|sekc)\w*"
                        r"|\bjeho\b|\bjejí\w*|\bsvé\w*|\bsvůj\b)")
# a body named as having organised or given the play
_ORGANISER = re.compile(r"\b(?:pořádal\w*|uspořádal\w*|pořádán\w*|uspořádán\w*|sehrál\w*|sehrán\w*|hrál\w*)\s+"
                        r"(?:\w+\s+){0,1}?(?P<body>(?:[A-ZČŘŠŽÚ]\w*\s+){0,2}(?:spol(?:ek|ku)|jednot\w*|besed\w*|klub\w*"
                        r"|odbor\w*|sbor\w*|Sokol\w*|Orel\w*|DTJ|Matic\w*))")


#: the first five letters of words every kind of body uses: they tell no body from another
_GENERIC_STEMS = {"ochot", "divad", "spole", "jedno", "odbor", "klubu", "kroužk", "soubo", "sdruž", "místn",
                  "zdejš", "česká", "český", "české"}


def _stems(name: str) -> set[str]:
    return {w[:5].casefold() for w in re.findall(r"\w{4,}", name or "")} - _GENERIC_STEMS


def _tied_to_page(text: str, ensemble_name: str) -> bool:
    """Does a clause on a company's page tie its players to the page's own body (Q7, Q13)?"""
    if _TIE_WORDS.search(text or ""):
        return True
    return bool(_stems(ensemble_name) & _stems(text))


def _other_organiser(text: str, ensemble_name: str) -> bool:
    """A body named as having organised or given the play that is not the page's (clause 34)."""
    m = _ORGANISER.search(text or "")
    body = _stems(m.group("body")) if m else set()
    return bool(body) and not (body & _stems(ensemble_name))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The evidence table — every dated record of theatre in one interval form
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
EVIDENCE_COLUMNS = ["evidence_id", "geo_id", "source", "source_key", "company_id",
                    "start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo", "end_hi", "open_end", "hedged", "activity_hedged",
                    "czech_activity", "company", "performance", "count_stated", "titles",
                    "attendance_n", "pause", "puppet", *[c for c in EVENT_COLUMNS if c != "performance"]]


def _span_from_precision(year, precision) -> tuple[float, float]:
    if pd.isna(year) or precision not in _SPAN_OF:
        return np.nan, np.nan
    return float(year), float(year) + _SPAN_OF[precision]


def active_decade_list(value) -> list[int]:
    """``ensemble_pages.active_decades`` (``1880|1890``) as first years of decades."""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return [int(x) for x in value.split("|") if x.strip()]
    if value is None or pd.isna(value):
        return []
    return [int(value)]


def _ensemble_company_id(geo_id, ensemble_id) -> str:
    return f"{int(geo_id)}:e{int(ensemble_id)}"


def _with_pages(ensembles: pd.DataFrame, pages: pd.DataFrame | None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The ensemble list with its page's end and decades (blank where there is no page)."""
    E = ensembles.copy()
    columns = ["ended_year", "ended_precision", "active_decades"]
    if pages is None:
        return E.assign(ended_year=np.nan, ended_precision="missing", active_decades=None)
    n = len(E)
    E = E.merge(pages[["ensemble_id", *columns]], on="ensemble_id", how="left", validate="m:1")
    assert len(E) == n, "ensemble pages: the merge changed the list"
    return E


def _ensemble_evidence(ensembles: pd.DataFrame, pages: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The ensemble list as company evidence: one row per ensemble and place, dated start.

    With the ensemble pages (D-145), a list row with no end takes the page's printed end
    (*Ukončení činnosti / poslední zpráva*), so it is certain from start to end; and a page
    that lists decades (*Působení*) closes the open end — the row becomes its start alone —
    and adds one ``ensemble_decade`` row per decade, a point as wide as the decade
    (possible across it, certain in no year, B10), under the ensemble's ``company_id``.
    """
    E = _with_pages(ensembles, pages)
    start = [_span_from_precision(y, p) for y, p in zip(E["year_from"], E["year_from_precision"])]
    end = [_span_from_precision(y, p) for y, p in zip(E["year_to"], E["year_to_precision"])]
    page_end = [_span_from_precision(y, p) for y, p in zip(E["ended_year"], E["ended_precision"])]
    end = [pe if pd.isna(e[0]) else e for e, pe in zip(end, page_end)]
    decades = E["active_decades"].map(active_decade_list).to_numpy()
    out = pd.DataFrame({
        "geo_id": E["geo_id"].astype(int), "source": "ensemble",
        "source_key": E["ensemble_id"].astype(int).astype(str),
        "start_lo": [s[0] for s in start], "start_hi": [s[1] for s in start],
        "end_lo": [e[0] for e in end], "end_hi": [e[1] for e in end]})
    out["open_end"] = out["end_lo"].isna() & np.array([not d for d in decades], dtype=bool)
    out["puppet"] = E["name"].fillna("").str.contains(_PUPPET).to_numpy()
    out["german"] = E["name"].fillna("").map(lambda n: bool(EVENT_CUES["german"].search(n))).to_numpy()
    out["company"] = ~out["puppet"] & ~out["german"]
    out["czech_activity"] = out["company"]
    flags = ["puppet", "german", "company", "czech_activity"]
    rows = [{"geo_id": r.geo_id, "source": "ensemble_decade", "source_key": f"{r.source_key}.{d}",
             "start_lo": float(d), "start_hi": float(d + 9), "end_lo": np.nan, "end_hi": np.nan,
             "open_end": False, **{f: getattr(r, f) for f in flags},
             "company_id": _ensemble_company_id(r.geo_id, r.source_key) if r.company else pd.NA}
            for r, listed in zip(out.itertuples(index=False), decades) for d in listed]
    decade_rows = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=[*out.columns, "company_id"])
    return pd.concat([out[out["start_lo"].notna()], decade_rows], ignore_index=True)


def ensemble_chronicle_clauses(pages: pd.DataFrame, ensembles: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Each ensemble page's own chronicle, read and cut as a place's is (D-145).

    One block per ensemble and place it is listed under (as :func:`_ensemble_evidence`
    has one row per ensemble and place), read by :func:`read_chronicle` and
    :func:`chronicle_clauses`.  Key ``(ensemble_id, geo_id, line_no, clause_no)``,
    asserted.  A puppet ensemble's clauses are all puppet; ``ensemble_german`` marks a
    German ensemble's, whose evidence never counts as Czech; ``ensemble_name`` is the name it
    is listed under (D-254 Q7: whose page it is decides whose its players are).
    """
    columns = ["ensemble_id", *CLAUSE_COLUMNS, "before_1914", "ensemble_german", "ensemble_name"]
    text = pages.set_index("ensemble_id")["chronicle_text"]
    listed = ensembles[["ensemble_id", "geo_id", "name"]].drop_duplicates(["ensemble_id", "geo_id"])
    parts = []
    for ensemble_id, geo_id, name in listed.itertuples(index=False):
        chronicle = text.get(ensemble_id)
        if not isinstance(chronicle, str):
            continue
        lines = pd.DataFrame(read_chronicle(int(geo_id), chronicle), columns=CHRONICLE_COLUMNS)
        clauses = chronicle_clauses(lines)
        if clauses.empty:
            continue
        name = name if isinstance(name, str) else ""
        clauses.insert(0, "ensemble_id", int(ensemble_id))
        clauses["puppet"] = clauses["puppet"] | bool(_PUPPET.search(name))
        clauses["ensemble_german"] = bool(EVENT_CUES["german"].search(name))
        clauses["ensemble_name"] = name
        parts.append(clauses)
    out = pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True) if parts else pd.DataFrame(columns=columns)
    assert not out.duplicated(["ensemble_id", "geo_id", "line_no", "clause_no"]).any(), \
        "ensemble clauses: key not unique"
    return out[columns]


def _clause_evidence(coded: pd.DataFrame, source: str = "chronicle") -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Chronicle clauses the rulings give a role, in interval form.

    A clause with no printed end takes the end it prints inside (``činný do 1938``).  A
    company clause, or one dated ``od`` / ``po``, with no end at all is open-ended (B1);
    any other clause is a point in time.  An undated clause is no evidence until the
    model pass dates it (B11).  ``source_key`` is ``line_no.clause_no``, led by the
    ``ensemble_id`` for an ensemble's own chronicle.
    """
    if coded.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=["geo_id", "source", "source_key", "company_id"])
    C = coded[coded["start_lo"].notna() | coded["start_hi"].notna() | coded["end_hi"].notna()].copy()
    keep = (C["czech_activity"] | C["company"] | C[[c for c in EVENT_COLUMNS if c in C]].any(axis=1)
            | C["pause"] | C["puppet"])
    C = C[keep]
    # D-254 Q6: a reader that was shown the inner years and kept the leading date has ruled them
    # out; and an end before the clause's start closes nothing
    if "inner_read" in C:
        ruled = C["inner_read"].fillna(False).astype(bool)
        C.loc[ruled, ["end_inside", "start_inside"]] = np.nan
    no_end = C["end_lo"].isna() & C["end_hi"].isna() & ~(C["end_inside"] < C["start_lo"])
    C.loc[no_end, "end_lo"] = C.loc[no_end, "end_inside"]
    C.loc[no_end, "end_hi"] = C.loc[no_end, "end_inside"]
    # D-254 Q6: an earlier start the clause prints for its theatre (`1868 … působí již od roku
    # 1860`) pushes the start back, and the leading date, when nothing else closes it, is the end
    if "start_inside" in C:
        from_model = C["date_source"].eq("model") if "date_source" in C else False
        earlier = C["start_inside"].notna() & (C["start_inside"] < C["start_lo"]) & ~from_model
        still_no_end = earlier & C["end_lo"].isna() & C["end_hi"].isna()
        lead_lo, lead_hi = C.loc[still_no_end, "start_lo"], C.loc[still_no_end, "start_hi"]
        C.loc[still_no_end, "end_lo"] = lead_lo.where(lead_lo.notna(), lead_hi)
        C.loc[still_no_end, "end_hi"] = lead_hi.where(lead_hi.notna(), lead_lo)
        C.loc[earlier, "start_lo"] = C.loc[earlier, "start_inside"]
        C.loc[earlier, "start_hi"] = C.loc[earlier, "start_inside"]
    still_open = C["end_lo"].isna() & C["end_hi"].isna() & C["start_lo"].notna()
    # D-221: a company's act alone (officers, members …) is a point, not an open end
    act_only = C["company_act"].fillna(False).astype(bool) if "company_act" in C else False
    C["open_end"] = still_open & ((C["company"] & ~act_only) | C["date_form"].isin(["from", "after"]))
    C["source"] = source
    C["source_key"] = C["line_no"].astype(int).astype(str) + "." + C["clause_no"].astype(int).astype(str)
    if "ensemble_id" in C:
        C["source_key"] = C["ensemble_id"].astype(int).astype(str) + "." + C["source_key"]
    return _list_points(C)


def _list_points(C: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """A clause dated by a list of years (``1902, 1914 DS SDH``, ``1683, 1685 a 1687``) is a
    point in each year it lists, not a span from the first to the last (D-140; audit A7).
    The first year keeps the clause's ``source_key`` (so its ``evidence_id`` is still the
    clause's key); each later year is a row of its own, ``source_key~year``.  None is open."""
    if "date_form" not in C or "date_raw" not in C:
        return C
    is_list = C["date_form"].eq("list")
    years = C.loc[is_list, "date_raw"].map(lambda s: sorted({int(y) for y in re.findall(_YEAR4, str(s))}))
    years = years[years.map(len) >= 2]
    if years.empty:
        return C
    points = []
    for idx, listed in years.items():
        row = C.loc[idx]
        for k, year in enumerate(listed):
            point = row.copy()
            point["start_lo"] = point["start_hi"] = float(year)
            point["end_lo"] = point["end_hi"] = np.nan
            point["open_end"] = False
            if k:
                point["source_key"] = f"{row['source_key']}~{year}"
            points.append(point)
    added = pd.DataFrame(points)[C.columns]
    for column, dtype in C.dtypes.items():               # rows built from Series come back object
        try:
            added[column] = added[column].astype(dtype)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            pass
    return pd.concat([C.drop(index=years.index), added], ignore_index=True)


def _ensemble_chronicle_evidence(coded: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """An ensemble's own chronicle as evidence (D-145): like a place's, but about one company.

    Its company clauses carry that ensemble's ``company_id`` (no B2 matching); where the
    page lists decades, :func:`evidence_table` closes their open end with the company's.
    A German ensemble's clauses are German, never Czech activity.
    """
    C = _clause_evidence(coded, source="ensemble_chronicle")
    german = C["ensemble_german"].astype(bool)
    C.loc[german, "german"] = True
    C.loc[german, ["czech_activity", "company"]] = False
    C["company_id"] = [_ensemble_company_id(g, e) if c else pd.NA
                       for g, e, c in zip(C["geo_id"], C["ensemble_id"], C["company"])]
    return C


def _first_report_evidence(places: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The place page's *první zpráva*: activity certain in its year (B3)."""
    spans = [_span_from_precision(y, p) for y, p in
             zip(places["first_record_year"], places["first_record_precision"])]
    out = pd.DataFrame({"geo_id": places["geo_id"].astype(int), "source": "first_report",
                        "source_key": "", "start_lo": [s[0] for s in spans],
                        "start_hi": [s[1] for s in spans]})
    out["end_lo"] = out["end_hi"] = np.nan
    out["open_end"] = False
    out["czech_activity"] = True
    return out[out["start_lo"].notna()]


def _ends_agree(a_lo, a_hi, b_lo, b_hi, slack: int = MATCH_START_YEARS) -> bool:
    if pd.isna(a_lo) or pd.isna(b_lo):
        return True
    return a_lo - slack <= b_hi and b_lo - slack <= a_hi


def assign_companies(evidence: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """One ``company_id`` per company, across the ensemble list and the chronicle (B2).

    Within a place, a chronicle company clause joins the ensemble row whose start lies
    within :data:`MATCH_START_YEARS` and whose end does not contradict it — the closest
    start first, each ensemble row taken at most once, names not used.  The chronicle
    clauses left over join one another by the same rule, so ``1887 zal. SDO`` and
    ``1887-1934 SDO`` are one company.  Rows that are no company get <NA>.
    """
    company_id = pd.Series(pd.NA, index=evidence.index, dtype="string")
    companies = evidence[evidence["company"]]
    for geo_id, group in companies.groupby("geo_id"):
        anchors: list[tuple] = []          # (company_id, start_lo, end_lo, end_hi, from_ensemble, used)
        for idx, r in group[group["source"] == "ensemble"].iterrows():
            cid = f"{geo_id}:e{r['source_key']}"
            company_id[idx] = cid
            anchors.append([cid, r["start_lo"], r["end_lo"], r["end_hi"], True, False])
        clauses = group[group["source"] == "chronicle"].sort_values("start_lo", na_position="last")
        for idx, r in clauses.iterrows():
            best, best_gap = None, None
            for anchor in anchors:
                if anchor[4] and anchor[5]:
                    continue                    # an ensemble row already matched
                gap = abs(anchor[1] - r["start_lo"]) if pd.notna(r["start_lo"]) else np.inf
                if gap <= MATCH_START_YEARS and _ends_agree(anchor[2], anchor[3], r["end_lo"], r["end_hi"]):
                    if best_gap is None or gap < best_gap:
                        best, best_gap = anchor, gap
            if best is None:
                best = [f"{geo_id}:c{r['source_key']}", r["start_lo"], r["end_lo"], r["end_hi"], False, False]
                anchors.append(best)
            elif best[4]:
                best[5] = True
            company_id[idx] = best[0]
    return company_id


def _repeat_key(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Place, clause text (lower case, punctuation as spaces) and date interval: what makes two
    clause records the same printed note."""
    words = frame["text"].fillna("").str.lower().str.replace(r"\W+", " ", regex=True).str.strip()
    # "string" + fillna: pandas 3 turns a missing year into NaN under astype(str), not "<NA>"
    dates = (frame[["start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo", "end_hi"]].astype("Float64").astype("string")
             .fillna("<NA>").agg("|".join, axis=1))
    return frame["geo_id"].astype(int).astype(str) + "|" + words + "|" + dates


def drop_copied_place_clauses(place_ev: pd.DataFrame, ensemble_ev: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The place-chronicle evidence less the clauses an ensemble page of the same place
    prints again (D-213): the same text and the same dates, matched one for one, so ``k``
    place copies against ``m`` page copies lose ``min(k, m)`` (earliest line first).

    The page's copy is kept: it belongs to its company (D-145), where the place copy would
    be matched by B2 or stand alone, and both were being counted.  A text repeated *within*
    the place chronicle is left alone — ``2014 aktivní.`` under each of four companies is
    four records — and so is one printed on two companies' pages (a joint performance, or
    two records of one company: a lineage question for the settlement check, not this rule).
    ``attrs["copied_place_clauses"]`` holds the number dropped.
    """
    if place_ev.empty or ensemble_ev.empty:
        out = place_ev.copy()
        out.attrs["copied_place_clauses"] = 0
        return out
    page_copies = _repeat_key(ensemble_ev).value_counts()
    key = _repeat_key(place_ev)
    order = place_ev.assign(_k=key.values).sort_values(["_k", "line_no", "clause_no"])
    rank = order.groupby("_k").cumcount()
    copied = rank < order["_k"].map(page_copies).fillna(0).astype(int)
    out = place_ev.drop(index=order.index[copied.values])
    out.attrs["copied_place_clauses"] = int(copied.sum())
    return out


def evidence_table(places: pd.DataFrame, ensembles: pd.DataFrame, coded: pd.DataFrame,
                   pages: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
                   ensemble_coded: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Ensemble spans, chronicle clauses and first reports as one table of dated evidence.

    Key ``evidence_id`` (``source:geo_id:source_key``), asserted unique.  Every row has
    a start or an end interval.  Columns as :data:`EVIDENCE_COLUMNS`.  With the ensemble
    pages (``pages``, scraper step C) and their coded chronicles (``ensemble_coded``,
    :func:`code_clauses` of :func:`ensemble_chronicle_clauses`), sources
    ``ensemble_decade`` and ``ensemble_chronicle`` join, both under the ensemble's own
    ``company_id`` (D-145).  A place-chronicle clause that an ensemble page of the same
    place prints again is dropped in favour of the page's copy (D-213,
    :func:`drop_copied_place_clauses`); ``attrs["copied_place_clauses"]`` holds the count.
    """
    place_ev = _clause_evidence(coded)
    parts = [_ensemble_evidence(ensembles, pages), place_ev, _first_report_evidence(places)]
    copied = 0
    if ensemble_coded is not None and len(ensemble_coded):
        assert pages is not None, "evidence: an ensemble chronicle needs its pages"
        page_ev = _ensemble_chronicle_evidence(ensemble_coded)
        kept = drop_copied_place_clauses(place_ev, page_ev)
        copied = kept.attrs.get("copied_place_clauses", 0)
        parts = [_ensemble_evidence(ensembles, pages), kept, _first_report_evidence(places), page_ev]
    ev = pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True, sort=False)
    preset = (ev["company_id"] if "company_id" in ev else pd.Series(pd.NA, index=ev.index)).astype("string")
    for column in EVIDENCE_COLUMNS:
        if column not in ev:
            ev[column] = np.nan
    flags = ["open_end", "hedged", "activity_hedged", "czech_activity", "company", "performance", "pause", "puppet",
             *[c for c in EVENT_COLUMNS if c not in ("performance", "attendance")], "attendance"]
    ev[flags] = ev[flags].astype("boolean").fillna(False).astype(bool)
    ev["titles"] = ev["titles"].fillna("")
    ev["evidence_id"] = ev["source"] + ":" + ev["geo_id"].astype(int).astype(str) + ":" + ev["source_key"]
    ev["company_id"] = preset.where(preset.notna(), assign_companies(ev))
    # D-145: a company whose page lists decades is possible in those decades only, so no
    # record of it — a place-chronicle clause matched to it by B2 included — stays open;
    # unless its own page records it after its last listed decade (D-214), which the
    # listing cannot then be the whole of: B1's open end stands
    listed = set(ev.loc[ev["source"] == "ensemble_decade", "company_id"].dropna().unique())
    outlived = outlived_listings(ev, pages) if pages is not None else set()
    ev.loc[ev["company_id"].isin(listed - outlived), "open_end"] = False
    reopen = (ev["source"] == "ensemble") & ev["company_id"].isin(outlived) & ev["end_lo"].isna() & ev["end_hi"].isna()
    ev.loc[reopen, "open_end"] = True
    bridges = company_bridges(ev, pages) if pages is not None else pd.DataFrame(columns=EVIDENCE_COLUMNS)
    ev = pd.concat([ev[EVIDENCE_COLUMNS], bridges[EVIDENCE_COLUMNS]], ignore_index=True)
    assert ev["evidence_id"].is_unique, "evidence: key not unique"
    assert (ev[["start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo", "end_hi"]].notna().any(axis=1)).all()
    ev.attrs.update(copied_place_clauses=copied, outlived_listings=len(outlived), company_bridges=len(bridges))
    return ev


def _page_records(ev: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The ensemble pages' own dated Czech-activity clauses, with their ``ensemble_id`` and
    the company they are about (the page's ensemble, D-145)."""
    page = ev[(ev["source"] == "ensemble_chronicle") & ev["czech_activity"] & ~ev["puppet"]].copy()
    page["ensemble_id"] = page["source_key"].str.split(".").str[0].astype(int)
    page["page_company"] = [_ensemble_company_id(g, e) for g, e in zip(page["geo_id"], page["ensemble_id"])]
    return page


def outlived_listings(ev: pd.DataFrame, pages: pd.DataFrame) -> set[str]:
    """Companies whose page lists decades but whose own page chronicle records them in a later
    decade (D-214, the narrow R2): the listing is contradicted by the page itself, so it does
    not close the company's open end."""
    page = _page_records(ev)
    if page.empty:
        return set()
    last = {e: max(d) for e, d in zip(pages["ensemble_id"], pages["active_decades"].map(active_decade_list)) if d}
    page["last_listed"] = page["ensemble_id"].map(last)
    first_year = page["start_lo"].fillna(page["start_hi"])
    later = page["last_listed"].notna() & (first_year >= page["last_listed"] + 10)
    return set(page.loc[later, "page_company"])


def company_bridges(ev: pd.DataFrame, pages: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One ``company_bridge`` record per company that its own records pin to two or more
    years (D-214, R4): certain from the first to the last of them, as a span.

    A record pins a year when it is printed to the year and not hedged: a Czech-activity
    clause on the company's own page (a performance there attests that the company
    existed), or any record already under its ``company_id`` (the list row's start, a
    place clause matched by B2).  The bridge is drawn only when the page lists every decade
    between the two years, so a company whose page leaves a decade out is not carried across
    it; a recorded pause still turns its years possible (B12).
    """
    page = _page_records(ev)
    # a hall the company hired (rare case 127) leaves its plays possible only: it pins no year
    exact = lambda f: f["start_lo"].notna() & (f["start_lo"] == f["start_hi"]) & ~f["hedged"] \
        & ~(f["activity_hedged"].astype(bool) if "activity_hedged" in f else False) \
        & (f["end_lo"].isna() | (f["end_lo"] == f["start_lo"]))  # noqa: E731
    pins = page.loc[exact(page), ["geo_id", "page_company", "start_lo"]].rename(columns={"page_company": "company_id"})
    own = ev[ev["company_id"].isin(set(pins["company_id"])) & exact(ev) & (ev["source"] != "ensemble_decade")]
    pins = pd.concat([pins, own[["geo_id", "company_id", "start_lo"]]], ignore_index=True)
    decades = {_ensemble_company_id(g, e): set(active_decade_list(d)) for g, e, d in
               zip(ev.loc[ev["source"] == "ensemble", "geo_id"], ev.loc[ev["source"] == "ensemble", "source_key"].astype(int),
                   ev.loc[ev["source"] == "ensemble", "source_key"].astype(int).map(
                       pages.set_index("ensemble_id")["active_decades"]))}
    rows = []
    for (geo_id, company_id), group in pins.groupby(["geo_id", "company_id"]):
        years = sorted(set(group["start_lo"].astype(int)))
        listed = decades.get(company_id, set())
        if len(years) < 2 or not listed:
            continue
        lo, hi = years[0], years[-1]
        if not all(d in listed for d in range(lo // 10 * 10, hi // 10 * 10 + 1, 10)):
            continue
        rows.append({"evidence_id": f"company_bridge:{int(geo_id)}:{company_id.split(':e')[1]}",
                     "geo_id": int(geo_id), "source": "company_bridge", "source_key": company_id.split(":e")[1],
                     "company_id": company_id, "start_lo": float(lo), "start_hi": float(lo),
                     "end_lo": float(hi), "end_hi": float(hi)})
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["evidence_id", "geo_id", "source", "source_key", "company_id",
                                      "start_lo", "start_hi", "end_lo", "end_hi"])
    for column in EVIDENCE_COLUMNS:
        if column not in out:
            out[column] = False if column in ev and ev[column].dtype == bool else np.nan
    out["titles"] = ""
    out["czech_activity"] = out["company"] = True
    return out[EVIDENCE_COLUMNS]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The place × year panel
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def year_bounds(start_lo, start_hi, end_lo, end_hi, open_end: bool, hedged: bool,
                last_year: int = PANEL_LAST_YEAR) -> tuple[tuple | None, tuple | None]:
    """The years a record makes theatre *certain* and *possible*, as closed ranges or None.

    A span with an end is certain from its latest possible start to its earliest
    possible end, and possible over its whole width.  Open-ended (B1): certain only in a
    start year printed exactly, possible from there to ``last_year``.  A point is certain
    only when printed to the year; a decade or a ``kolem`` is possible across its width
    and certain in none (B10).  Known only by its end (``do 1910``): possible in the end
    year, certain in none.  A start with one bound missing — ``před 1880`` (no earliest),
    ``po 1900`` (no latest) — is printed to no year, so certain in none (audit A5).
    Hedged (B4): never certain.
    """
    has_start = not pd.isna(start_lo) or not pd.isna(start_hi)
    has_end = not pd.isna(end_lo) or not pd.isna(end_hi)
    if not has_start:
        if not has_end:
            return None, None
        lo, hi = (end_lo if not pd.isna(end_lo) else end_hi), (end_hi if not pd.isna(end_hi) else end_lo)
        return None, (int(lo), int(hi))
    exact = not pd.isna(start_lo) and not pd.isna(start_hi) and start_lo == start_hi
    s_lo = start_lo if not pd.isna(start_lo) else start_hi
    s_hi = start_hi if not pd.isna(start_hi) else start_lo
    if has_end:
        e_lo = end_lo if not pd.isna(end_lo) else end_hi
        e_hi = end_hi if not pd.isna(end_hi) else end_lo
        # `po 1882` to an end: the start may be as late as the end, so the end year alone
        latest_start = e_lo if pd.isna(start_hi) else s_hi
        certain = (int(latest_start), int(e_lo)) if latest_start <= e_lo else None
        possible = (int(s_lo), int(max(e_hi, s_hi)))
    elif open_end:
        certain = (int(s_lo), int(s_lo)) if exact else None
        possible = (int(s_lo), max(int(s_hi), last_year))
    else:
        certain = (int(s_lo), int(s_lo)) if exact else None
        possible = (int(s_lo), int(s_hi))
    return (None if hedged else certain), possible


PANEL_KEY = ["geo_id", "year"]


def place_year_panel(evidence: pd.DataFrame, geo_ids, first_year: int = PANEL_FIRST_YEAR,
                     last_year: int = PANEL_LAST_YEAR) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Every place × year, ``first_year``–``last_year``: Czech amateur theatre, certain and possible.

    Balanced: one row per place of ``geo_ids`` and year, key ``(geo_id, year)`` asserted.
    Columns, each ``_certain`` and ``_possible``:
    ``any_activity`` (some Czech-activity record, the first report included, B3);
    ``ensembles_active`` (distinct companies whose span covers the year);
    ``performances_min`` (certain: performance records printed to one year, each counting
    the number it states or 1; possible: records whose interval covers the year); one
    count per :data:`EVENT_COLUMNS` (German, bilingual and Latin are
    counted, never activity, B8).  Also ``performances_period_avg`` (a count stated over
    a span, ``1883-1910 173 her``, spread evenly over its certain years — an average, so
    kept apart from the minimum), ``plays_distinct_certain``, ``attendance_max``
    (largest audience stated in a record certain in the year), and
    ``activity_decade_certain`` (Czech activity certainly inside this year's decade, B10).
    A recorded pause (B12) turns certain activity and companies into possible for its
    certain years — but never a performance printed to its year, nor the company that gave
    it, in that year (D-254 Q11).  A hall a company hired is the company's act with its
    activity possible only (``activity_hedged``, D-254).  Puppet theatre is ``puppet_*`` only.
    """
    geo_ids = pd.Index(sorted(set(int(g) for g in geo_ids)))
    years = np.arange(first_year, last_year + 1)
    shape = (len(geo_ids), len(years))
    row_of = {g: i for i, g in enumerate(geo_ids)}
    arrays: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}

    def add(name: str, i: int, bounds, amount: float = 1.0, mask=None) -> None:
        """Add ``amount`` over ``bounds``, except in the years ``mask`` (a pause) holds."""
        if bounds is None:
            return
        a, b = max(bounds[0], first_year) - first_year, min(bounds[1], last_year) - first_year
        if a <= b:
            keep = 1.0 if mask is None or mask is False else ~np.asarray(mask)[a:b + 1]
            arrays.setdefault(name, np.zeros(shape))[i, a:b + 1] += amount * keep

    ev = evidence[evidence["geo_id"].isin(geo_ids)]
    titles: dict[tuple[int, int], set] = {}
    attendance = np.full(shape, np.nan)
    decade = np.zeros(shape, dtype=bool)
    companies_seen: dict[tuple[int, str], tuple] = {}
    place_pause, company_pause = _pauses(ev, row_of, shape, first_year, last_year)

    performed = _performed_years(ev, row_of, len(years), first_year, last_year)

    def paused(i: int, owner) -> np.ndarray:
        """The years a record of ``owner`` (a company, or None) in place ``i`` is paused."""
        return place_pause[i] | company_pause.get((i, owner), False)

    for r in ev.itertuples(index=False):
        i = row_of[int(r.geo_id)]
        certain, possible = year_bounds(r.start_lo, r.start_hi, r.end_lo, r.end_hi,
                                        bool(r.open_end), bool(r.hedged), last_year)
        prefix = "puppet_" if r.puppet else ""
        if r.czech_activity and not r.puppet:
            # rare case 127: a hall the company hired — the company certain, its plays possible
            hall_only = bool(getattr(r, "activity_hedged", False))
            # D-254 Q11: a pause never turns a performance dated to its year possible
            dated_play = bool(r.performance) and certain is not None and certain[0] == certain[1]
            add("any_activity_certain", i, None if hall_only else certain,
                mask=None if dated_play else paused(i, _owner(r)))
            add("any_activity_possible", i, possible)
            # audit A6: a hedged record is never certain (B4), of its decade neither
            if possible is not None and possible[0] // 10 == possible[1] // 10 and not r.hedged \
                    and not hall_only:
                d0 = possible[0] // 10 * 10
                add("_decade", i, (d0, d0 + 9))
        if r.puppet and (r.czech_activity or r.company):
            add("puppet_activity_certain", i, certain)
            add("puppet_activity_possible", i, possible)
        if r.company and isinstance(r.company_id, str) and not r.puppet:
            seen = companies_seen.setdefault((i, r.company_id), [None, []])
            seen[0] = _hull(seen[0], certain)
            if possible is not None:
                seen[1].append(possible)
        if r.performance and r.czech_activity:
            single = certain is not None and certain[0] == certain[1]
            stated = not pd.isna(r.count_stated)
            if single:
                add(f"{prefix}performances_min_certain", i, certain, r.count_stated if stated else 1.0)
            elif certain is not None and stated and not r.puppet:
                # `1883-1910 173 her`: an average over the span, not a minimum in any year
                add("performances_period_avg", i, certain, r.count_stated / (certain[1] - certain[0] + 1))
            add(f"{prefix}performances_min_possible", i, possible)
            if single and r.titles and not r.puppet:
                titles.setdefault((i, certain[0]), set()).update(r.titles.split("|"))
        for column in EVENT_COLUMNS:
            if column != "performance" and getattr(r, column):
                add(f"{column}_certain", i, certain)
                add(f"{column}_possible", i, possible)
        if not pd.isna(r.attendance_n) and certain is not None and certain[0] == certain[1]:
            j = certain[0] - first_year
            if 0 <= j < len(years):
                attendance[i, j] = np.nanmax([attendance[i, j], r.attendance_n])
    for (i, company_id), (certain, possibles) in companies_seen.items():
        # a company that performed in a paused year was active that year (D-254 Q11)
        played = performed.get((i, company_id))
        mask = paused(i, company_id)
        add("ensembles_active_certain", i, certain, mask=mask if played is None else mask & ~played)
        covered = np.zeros(len(years), dtype=bool)
        for bounds in ([certain] if certain else []) + possibles:
            a, b = max(bounds[0], first_year) - first_year, min(bounds[1], last_year) - first_year
            if a <= b:
                covered[a:b + 1] = True
        arrays.setdefault("ensembles_active_possible", np.zeros(shape))[i] += covered
    for (i, year), found in titles.items():
        if first_year <= year <= last_year:
            arrays.setdefault("plays_distinct_certain", np.zeros(shape))[i, year - first_year] = len(found)
    decade = arrays.pop("_decade", np.zeros(shape)) > 0
    any_company_pause = np.zeros(shape, dtype=bool)
    for (i, _), years_paused in company_pause.items():
        any_company_pause[i] |= years_paused
    return _panel_frame(arrays, attendance, decade, geo_ids, years, place_pause | any_company_pause)


def _owner(r) -> str | None:
    """The company a record is about: its ``company_id``, or for a clause on an ensemble's own
    page that is not company evidence (a performance there), the page's company (D-145)."""
    if isinstance(r.company_id, str):
        return r.company_id
    if r.source == "ensemble_chronicle":
        return _ensemble_company_id(r.geo_id, str(r.source_key).split(".")[0])
    return None


def _performed_years(ev: pd.DataFrame, row_of: dict, n_years: int, first_year: int, last_year: int) -> dict:
    """``{(place row, company_id): years mask}``: the years a company's Czech performance is
    printed to the year and not hedged (D-254 Q11: a recorded pause does not turn them
    possible).  The company is the record's :func:`_owner`; records of no company are left out."""
    out: dict[tuple[int, str], np.ndarray] = {}
    plays = ev[ev["performance"] & ev["czech_activity"] & ~ev["puppet"] & ~ev["hedged"]]
    for r in plays.itertuples(index=False):
        certain, _ = year_bounds(r.start_lo, r.start_hi, r.end_lo, r.end_hi, bool(r.open_end), False, last_year)
        owner = _owner(r)
        if certain is None or certain[0] != certain[1] or owner is None or not first_year <= certain[0] <= last_year:
            continue
        out.setdefault((row_of[int(r.geo_id)], owner), np.zeros(n_years, dtype=bool))[certain[0] - first_year] = True
    return out


def _pauses(ev: pd.DataFrame, row_of: dict, shape: tuple, first_year: int, last_year: int):
    """B12 as the audit narrowed it (A2): the years a recorded pause makes certain only possible.

    Only a clause that is a pause and nothing else counts (``pause`` as :func:`code_clauses`
    sets it: not one that also records a founding or a play, whose leading date is that
    event's — ``1885 založen, později přerušena``), not puppet or German theatre.  On an ensemble's own page (or matched to a company) it
    pauses that company; on a place's chronicle, naming none, the whole place.  Returns the
    place masks (``places × years``) and ``{(place row, company_id): years mask}``.
    """
    place = np.zeros(shape, dtype=bool)
    company: dict[tuple[int, str], np.ndarray] = {}
    alone = ev[ev["pause"] & ~ev["puppet"] & ~ev["german"]]          # `pause`: alone (code_clauses)
    for r in alone.itertuples(index=False):
        certain, _ = year_bounds(r.start_lo, r.start_hi, r.end_lo, r.end_hi, bool(r.open_end), bool(r.hedged), last_year)
        if certain is None:
            continue
        a, b = max(certain[0], first_year) - first_year, min(certain[1], last_year) - first_year
        if a > b:
            continue
        i, owner = row_of[int(r.geo_id)], _owner(r)
        target = place[i] if owner is None else company.setdefault((i, owner), np.zeros(shape[1], dtype=bool))
        target[a:b + 1] = True
    return place, company


def _hull(a, b):
    """Two certain ranges of one company as one: from the earliest certain start to the
    latest certain end, since the company existed in between.  Its *possible* years are
    the union of its records' ranges and the certain hull, not their hull (D-145): a gap
    between two listed decades is not evidence."""
    if a is None or b is None:
        return a if b is None else b
    return min(a[0], b[0]), max(a[1], b[1])


PANEL_COUNT_COLUMNS = (
    [f"{base}_{bound}" for base in ("any_activity", "ensembles_active", "performances_min")
     for bound in ("certain", "possible")]
    + ["plays_distinct_certain"]
    + [f"{c}_{bound}" for c in EVENT_COLUMNS if c != "performance" for bound in ("certain", "possible")]
    + [f"puppet_{base}_{bound}" for base in ("activity", "performances_min") for bound in ("certain", "possible")])


def _panel_frame(arrays: dict, attendance: np.ndarray, decade: np.ndarray, geo_ids, years,
                 pause: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The arrays as the panel frame.  ``pause`` (B12, :func:`_pauses`) is already applied to
    the certain counts; it is kept as ``pause_recorded`` (a pause of the place or of a company in it)."""
    shape = (len(geo_ids), len(years))
    out = pd.DataFrame({"geo_id": np.repeat(geo_ids.to_numpy(), len(years)),
                        "year": np.tile(years, len(geo_ids))})
    for name in PANEL_COUNT_COLUMNS:
        values = arrays.get(name, np.zeros(shape)).ravel()
        if name.startswith(("any_activity", "puppet_activity")):
            out[name] = values > 0
        else:
            out[name] = values.astype("int32")
    out["performances_period_avg"] = arrays.get("performances_period_avg", np.zeros(shape)).ravel().round(2)
    out["attendance_max"] = attendance.ravel()
    out["activity_decade_certain"] = decade.ravel() | out["any_activity_certain"].to_numpy()
    out["activity_decade_certain"] = out.groupby(["geo_id", out["year"] // 10])[
        "activity_decade_certain"].transform("any")
    out["pause_recorded"] = pause.ravel()
    assert not out.duplicated(PANEL_KEY).any(), "panel: key not unique"
    assert (out["any_activity_possible"] | ~out["any_activity_certain"]).all(), "panel: certain ⊄ possible"
    return out


#: The saved settlement table is keyed by ``settlement_id``, the settlement table's own key:
#: ``settlement_row`` is a row position, valid only inside one build, and a later rebuild of
#: ``settlements_1910`` would put a reader's counts on other villages.  ``census_okres`` is
#: the okres as the census pools it (D-18: a Statutarstadt and the rural okres around it are
#: one census unit), keyed by ``census_okres_id`` — merge persons on ``birth_okres_id`` with
#: the ``okres`` table and on ``birth_census_okres_id`` with the ``census_okres`` table, never
#: across (audit 2026-11-11 C3: across gives a city-born man the ring's theatre).
AREA_LEVELS = {"settlement": "settlement_id", "court": "court_id", "okres": "okres_id",
               "census_okres": "census_okres_id"}

#: Which edition's court the register's two Bohemian volumes settle on, first first: the
#: Czech volume is the register's route of record for Bohemia (D-112); Moravia and Silesia
#: have only their German volume.
_REGISTER_EDITION_ORDER = {"cz": 0, "de-moravia": 0, "de-silesia": 0, "de-bohemia": 1}


def register_courts(register_places: pd.DataFrame, courts=None) -> pd.Series:
    """``settlement_id`` → its 1910 court as the 1910 register prints it
    (``data/final/register_rechecked/register_places``).  Where a settlement is anchored
    twice — a detached part filed under its town (``Škarez … viz Prachatice``) or the two
    Bohemian volumes differing — the municipality row wins, then the edition of record.

    ``courts``, given (the 1910 backbone's court ids, ``districts_1910``), drops a register court
    outside it: Zlabings (Slavonice, ``302006900``) and Triesch (Třešť, ``302012900``) were set up
    after 1910 and keep ids of their own in the register only to keep their numbering apart
    (D-205). Their municipalities were in a 1910 court (D-122, D-208), which the settlement's own
    point then gives, as it does for a person's ``birth_court_id`` (D-255)."""
    r = register_places.dropna(subset=["settlement_id", "court_id"])
    if courts is not None:
        r = r[r["court_id"].astype("int64").isin(pd.Series(courts).astype("int64"))]
    r = r.assign(_part=r["place_level"].ne("municipality"),
                 _edition=r["edition"].map(_REGISTER_EDITION_ORDER).fillna(2))
    r = r.sort_values(["settlement_id", "_part", "_edition"], kind="stable")
    return r.drop_duplicates("settlement_id").set_index("settlement_id")["court_id"].astype("int64")


def _okres_of_court(court: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
    """A court's okres: its id is ``okres_id * 1000 + court number`` (``districts_1910``)."""
    return court.astype("Int64") // 1000


def place_units(join: pd.DataFrame, settlements: pd.DataFrame, *,
                places: pd.DataFrame | None = None, register_places: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
                locator=None, districts: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Each database place's 1910 settlement, okres and court, and where each came from.

    One row per place of ``join`` (:func:`join_places_to_settlements`):

    ``okres_id`` — the tied settlement's 1910 okres (``okres_source = "settlement"``, the
    name-based key, as for the persons); for a place tied to none, the okres whose MPIDR
    court polygon holds the place's own point (``"polygon"``, needs ``places`` and
    ``locator``; agrees with the name on 89 % of the places that have both, 2026-11-11).
    ``court_id`` — always inside ``okres_id`` (audit C2: courts did not nest in okresy):
    the register's court for the tied settlement (``court_source = "register"``,
    :func:`register_courts`); else the settlement's own point-in-polygon court; else the
    place's point snapped into the okres (1 km, D-35); else the okres's only court
    (``districts``); else missing, and the place reaches the okres sum but no court's.
    """
    S = settlements[settlements["has_okres_1910"]] if "has_okres_1910" in settlements else settlements
    S = S[["settlement_row", "settlement_id", "okres_id", "court_id"]].rename(columns={"court_id": "_s_court"})
    out = (join[["geo_id", "settlement_row"]].astype({"settlement_row": "Int64"})
           .merge(S, on="settlement_row", how="left", validate="m:1"))
    assert len(out) == len(join), "place_units: the join gained or lost rows"
    out["okres_id"] = out["okres_id"].astype("Int64")
    out["okres_source"] = np.where(out["okres_id"].notna(), "settlement", None).astype(object)
    out["court_id"] = pd.array([pd.NA] * len(out), dtype="Int64")
    out["court_source"] = pd.Series([None] * len(out), dtype=object)

    def fill(candidate, source: str) -> None:
        """Take ``candidate`` as the court where none is set yet and it lies in the okres."""
        candidate = pd.Series(candidate, index=out.index, dtype="Int64")
        ok = out["court_id"].isna() & candidate.notna() & _okres_of_court(candidate).eq(out["okres_id"]).fillna(False)
        out.loc[ok, "court_id"] = candidate[ok]
        out.loc[ok, "court_source"] = source

    backbone = None if districts is None else districts["court_id"]
    if register_places is not None:
        fill(out["settlement_id"].map(register_courts(register_places, backbone)), "register")
    fill(out["_s_court"], "settlement_polygon")
    if places is not None and locator is not None:
        from utils.parsing import spatial as sp
        pts = out[["geo_id"]].merge(places[["geo_id", "lat", "lon"]], on="geo_id", how="left", validate="1:1")
        # a place tied to no settlement: its okres from its own point (no okres to snap toward)
        bare = sp.add_court_ids(pts.assign(okres_id=out["okres_id"]), locator, okres_col="okres_id")
        lone = out["okres_id"].isna() & bare["court_id"].notna()
        out.loc[lone, "okres_id"] = _okres_of_court(bare.loc[lone, "court_id"])
        out.loc[lone, "okres_source"] = "polygon"
        fill(bare["court_id"], "place_polygon")
    if districts is not None:
        courts = districts["court_id"].astype("int64")
        per_okres = courts.groupby(courts // 1000).agg(["size", "first"])
        only = per_okres.loc[per_okres["size"] == 1, "first"]
        fill(out["okres_id"].map(only), "only_court")
    out = out.drop(columns=["settlement_row", "_s_court"])
    assert out["geo_id"].is_unique, "place_units: geo_id not unique"
    nested = out["court_id"].isna() | (_okres_of_court(out["court_id"]) == out["okres_id"])
    assert nested.all(), "place_units: a court outside its okres"
    return out


def place_units_report(units: pd.DataFrame, panel: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    """Print where the places' okresy and courts came from, by places and by certain
    place-years of Czech activity, and how much of the panel reaches no okres or no court."""
    certain = panel.groupby("geo_id")["any_activity_certain"].sum().rename("certain_place_years")
    U = units.merge(certain, left_on="geo_id", right_index=True, how="left").fillna({"certain_place_years": 0})
    total = U["certain_place_years"].sum()
    for column in ("okres_source", "court_source"):
        table = U.assign(**{column: U[column].fillna("none")}).groupby(column).agg(
            places=("geo_id", "size"), certain_place_years=("certain_place_years", "sum"))
        table["share"] = (table["certain_place_years"] / total).round(3) if total else 0.0
        print(f"\n── {column}\n" + table.to_string())


def area_year_tables(panel: pd.DataFrame, units: pd.DataFrame, settlements: pd.DataFrame,
                     crosswalk: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
                     register_places: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
                     districts: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """The place panel summed to 1910 settlement, court, okres and census okres × year.

    ``units`` is :func:`place_units` (one row per place); ``settlements`` is
    :func:`settlement_frame`; ``crosswalk`` is ``data/final/geo/okres_census_crosswalk``
    (``okres_id`` → ``census_okres_id``) and, given, adds the ``census_okres`` table;
    ``register_places``, given, adds the register's courts of the settlements to the court grid
    (only courts of ``districts``, the 1910 backbone, where that is given: D-255).
    Every 1910 settlement with a 1910 okres gets every year, and so does every okres and
    court any of them or any place falls in — a unit with no database place is a row of
    zeros (D-141: the treatment's zero, memory of the German areas).  Counts are summed;
    ``any_activity_*`` becomes ``places_active_*`` (places with activity) and
    ``any_activity_*`` (any); ``attendance_max`` the maximum.  ``places_in_database`` is
    the number of database places in the unit.  A place with an okres but no settlement
    (``okres_source = "polygon"``) counts in its court and okres, not in the settlement
    table; one with neither is in no table.  Keys asserted; the courts of an okres asserted
    to sum to the okres, less the places with no court.
    """
    S = settlements[settlements["has_okres_1910"]] if "has_okres_1910" in settlements else settlements
    assert S["settlement_id"].is_unique, "settlements: settlement_id not unique"
    U = units[["geo_id", "settlement_id", "court_id", "okres_id"]].copy()
    U["okres_id"] = U["okres_id"].astype("Int64")
    grids = {"settlement_id": S["settlement_id"],
             "okres_id": pd.concat([S["okres_id"], U["okres_id"]]).astype("Int64"),
             "court_id": pd.concat([S["court_id"].astype("Int64").where(
                                        _okres_of_court(S["court_id"]).eq(S["okres_id"].astype("Int64")).fillna(False)),
                                    U["court_id"]]).astype("Int64")}
    if register_places is not None:
        backbone = None if districts is None else districts["court_id"]
        reg = S["settlement_id"].map(register_courts(register_places, backbone)).astype("Int64")
        reg = reg.where(_okres_of_court(reg).eq(S["okres_id"].astype("Int64")).fillna(False))
        grids["court_id"] = pd.concat([grids["court_id"], reg]).astype("Int64")
    levels = dict(AREA_LEVELS)
    if crosswalk is not None:
        pooled = crosswalk.set_index("okres_id")["census_okres_id"]
        missing = set(grids["okres_id"].dropna()) - set(pooled.index)
        assert not missing, f"okres not in the census crosswalk: {sorted(missing)}"
        U["census_okres_id"] = U["okres_id"].map(pooled).astype("Int64")
        grids["census_okres_id"] = grids["okres_id"].map(pooled)
    else:
        levels.pop("census_okres")
    P = panel.merge(U, on="geo_id", how="inner", validate="m:1")
    assert len(P) <= len(panel)
    bools = [c for c in panel.columns if panel[c].dtype == bool]
    counts = [c for c in panel.columns if c not in bools + PANEL_KEY + ["attendance_max"]]
    years = np.sort(panel["year"].unique())
    tables = {}
    for level, key in levels.items():
        agg = P.dropna(subset=[key]).groupby([key, "year"]).agg(
            **{c: (c, "sum") for c in counts},
            **{c: (c, "any") for c in bools},
            **{c.replace("any_activity", "places_active"): (c, "sum")
               for c in ("any_activity_certain", "any_activity_possible")},
            attendance_max=("attendance_max", "max"))
        ids = pd.Series(grids[key]).dropna().unique()
        grid = pd.MultiIndex.from_product([np.sort(ids), years], names=[key, "year"])
        assert set(agg.index) <= set(grid), f"{level}: a unit outside the grid"
        out = agg.reindex(grid).reset_index()
        filled = [c for c in out.columns if c not in (key, "year", "attendance_max")]
        for c in filled:
            out[c] = (out[c].astype("boolean").fillna(False).astype(bool) if c in bools
                      else out[c].fillna(0).astype(agg[c].dtype))
        per_unit = U.dropna(subset=[key]).groupby(key).size().rename("places_in_database")
        out = out.merge(per_unit, left_on=key, right_index=True, how="left", validate="m:1")
        out["places_in_database"] = out["places_in_database"].fillna(0).astype(int)
        assert not out.duplicated([key, "year"]).any(), f"{level} panel: key not unique"
        tables[level] = out
    _assert_courts_sum_to_okresy(tables, P)
    if "census_okres" in tables:
        t, o = tables["census_okres"], tables["okres"]
        assert t["places_active_certain"].sum() == o["places_active_certain"].sum(), "census okres ≠ okres sum"
    return tables


def _assert_courts_sum_to_okresy(tables: dict[str, pd.DataFrame], P: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    """The courts of each okres sum to the okres, less the places with no court (audit C2)."""
    measure = "places_active_certain"
    court = tables["court"].assign(okres_id=lambda t: t["court_id"] // 1000).groupby(["okres_id", "year"])[measure].sum()
    no_court = P[P["court_id"].isna()].groupby(["okres_id", "year"])["any_activity_certain"].sum()
    okres = tables["okres"].set_index(["okres_id", "year"])[measure]
    rebuilt = court.reindex(okres.index, fill_value=0) + no_court.reindex(okres.index, fill_value=0)
    assert (rebuilt == okres).all(), "courts do not sum to their okres"


def panel_report(panel: pd.DataFrame, evidence: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    """Print what the panel holds: evidence by source, places and place-years active."""
    print("\n── evidence by source\n" + evidence.groupby("source").agg(
        rows=("evidence_id", "size"), czech_activity=("czech_activity", "sum"),
        companies=("company_id", "nunique")).to_string())
    if "copied_place_clauses" in evidence.attrs:
        print(f"place-chronicle clauses dropped as copies of an ensemble page's (D-213): "
              f"{evidence.attrs['copied_place_clauses']:,}")
    if "company_bridges" in evidence.attrs:
        print(f"companies bridged between their own records (D-214): {evidence.attrs['company_bridges']:,}; "
              f"listings their own page outlives, left open: {evidence.attrs['outlived_listings']:,}")
    active = panel.groupby("geo_id")[["any_activity_certain", "any_activity_possible"]].any()
    print(f"\nplaces with Czech activity {PANEL_FIRST_YEAR}–{PANEL_LAST_YEAR}: certain "
          f"{int(active['any_activity_certain'].sum()):,}, possible {int(active['any_activity_possible'].sum()):,}"
          f" of {panel['geo_id'].nunique():,}")
    by_decade = panel.assign(decade=panel["year"] // 10 * 10).groupby("decade")[
        ["any_activity_certain", "any_activity_possible", "ensembles_active_certain",
         "performances_min_certain", "german_certain"]].sum()
    print("\n── place-years by decade (sums over place-years)\n" + by_decade.to_string())


def ensemble_page_summary(pages: pd.DataFrame, ensembles: pd.DataFrame,
                          cutoff: int = PRE_WAR_CUTOFF) -> dict[str, int]:
    """What the ensemble pages add to the list's start (D-145), one count per ensemble.

    ``end_year``: the page prints an end or last report as a year or decade.
    ``decades``: it lists a decade.  ``decade_after_start``: a listed decade after the
    start's decade and before ``cutoff``.  ``closes_before_cutoff``: its last listed decade
    ends before ``cutoff`` (the open end it replaces ran to the cutoff).
    ``decade_before_start``: it lists a decade before the start's (kept as printed).
    ``chronicle_after_start``: its own chronicle has a dated line after the start and
    before ``cutoff``.  ``uninformative``: none of the end, a later decade or a later line.
    """
    start = ensembles.groupby("ensemble_id")["year_from"].min()
    P = pages.set_index("ensemble_id")
    P = P.assign(start=start.reindex(P.index))
    decades = P["active_decades"].map(active_decade_list)
    start_decade = P["start"] // 10 * 10
    later = [any(s < d < cutoff for d in ds) for ds, s in zip(decades, start_decade)]
    before = [any(d < s for d in ds) for ds, s in zip(decades, start_decade)]
    closes = [bool(ds) and max(ds) + 9 < cutoff - 1 for ds in decades]
    line_year = re.compile(rf"^\s*{_DAY_MONTH}(1[5-9]\d\d)\b")
    chron = [isinstance(t, str) and any(s < int(m.group(1)) < cutoff for m in map(line_year.match, t.splitlines()) if m)
             for t, s in zip(P["chronicle_text"], P["start"])]
    end = P["ended_precision"].isin(["year", "decade"]).to_numpy()
    informative = end | np.array(later) | np.array(chron)
    return {"pages": len(P), "end_year": int(end.sum()), "decades": int(decades.map(bool).sum()),
            "decade_after_start": int(sum(later)), "closes_before_cutoff": int(sum(closes)),
            "decade_before_start": int(sum(before)), "chronicle_after_start": int(sum(chron)),
            "uninformative": int((~informative).sum())}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tabulation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _share_table(frame: pd.DataFrame, by: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    table = frame.groupby(by, dropna=False).agg(
        settlements=("settlement_row", "size"),
        in_database=("geo_id", lambda s: int(s.notna().sum())),
        ensemble_pre1914=("ensemble_pre", "sum"),
        ambiguous_191x=("ensemble_ambiguous", "sum"),
        first_record_pre1914=("first_record_pre", "sum"),
    ).reset_index()
    for col in ("in_database", "ensemble_pre1914", "first_record_pre1914"):
        table[f"share_{col}"] = (table[col] / table["settlements"]).round(3)
    return table


def _documentation_table(paged: pd.DataFrame, by: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """How much the database records per place, grouped by ``by``."""
    return paged.groupby(by, dropna=False).agg(
        places=("geo_id", "size"),
        with_first_record=("first_record_known", "mean"),
        first_record_pre1914=("first_record_pre", "mean"),
        with_any_ensemble=("n_ensembles", lambda s: (s > 0).mean()),
        ensembles_per_place=("n_ensembles", "mean"),
        with_ensemble_pre1914=("ensemble_pre", "mean"),
        with_archive_citation=("archive_chars", lambda s: (s > 0).mean()),
        with_bibliography=("bibliography_chars", lambda s: (s > 0).mean()),
        median_chronicle_chars=("text_chars", "median"),
    ).round(3).reset_index()


def coverage_tables(
    places: pd.DataFrame,
    ensembles: pd.DataFrame,
    settlements: pd.DataFrame,
    districts: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    *,
    okresy: list[str] | None,
    census: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    cutoff: int = PRE_WAR_CUTOFF,
) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Every table of the pilot, for the scraped sample and (from step A) the country.

    Args:
        places: scraper ``places.csv`` (all places; page fields filled for the sample).
        ensembles: scraper ``ensembles.csv``.
        settlements: ``data/final/geo/settlements_1910``.
        districts: ``data/final/geo/districts_1910`` (district names + court seats).
        okresy: the present-day okresy that were scraped; ``None`` once all of them are,
            in which case the denominator is every 1910 settlement rather than those whose
            okres timeline ends in a sample okres.
        census: ``census_okres_1910`` — if given, each 1910 okres gets its Czech-speaking
            share, the first thing coverage of a *Czech* theatre database depends on.

    Returns:
        A dict of DataFrames; :func:`coverage_report` prints them.
    """
    S = settlement_frame(settlements, districts)
    whole_country = okresy is None
    okresy = sorted(places["okres"].dropna().unique()) if whole_country else list(okresy)
    sample = places.copy() if whole_country else places[places["okres"].isin(okresy)].copy()
    missing_pages = int((~sample["page_cached"]).sum())
    tables: dict[str, pd.DataFrame] = {}

    # ── the join, on the sample ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    join = join_places_to_settlements(sample, S)
    n_before = len(sample)
    sample = sample.merge(join, on="geo_id", how="left", validate="1:1")
    assert len(sample) == n_before, "place ↔ join merge changed the row count"
    dates = place_dates(sample, ensembles[ensembles["geo_id"].isin(sample["geo_id"])], cutoff)
    sample = sample.merge(dates, on="geo_id", how="left", validate="1:1")
    assert len(sample) == n_before
    sample["matched"] = sample["settlement_row"].notna()
    # a place's crown land is that of the 1910 settlement it ties to
    sample = sample.merge(S[["settlement_row", "land"]].astype({"settlement_row": "Int64"}),
                          on="settlement_row", how="left", validate="m:1")
    assert len(sample) == n_before

    tables["join_by_method"] = (sample.groupby(["type", "match_method"]).size()
                                .unstack("type", fill_value=0).assign(all=lambda t: t.sum(axis=1)))
    tables["join_rate"] = sample.groupby("okres").agg(
        places=("geo_id", "size"), matched=("matched", "sum"),
        match_rate=("matched", "mean")).round(3).reset_index()
    tables["unmatched_places"] = sample.loc[~sample["matched"],
                                            ["geo_id", "name", "type", "okres", "match_method",
                                             "n_ensembles", "first_record_year"]]

    # ── the 1910 settlements of the sample area ─────────────────────────────
    in_scope = S["in_1910"] if whole_country else S["in_1910"] & S["okres_now"].isin(okresy)
    scope = S[in_scope]
    n_scope = len(scope)
    tied = sample.loc[sample["matched"], ["settlement_row", "geo_id", "ensemble_pre",
                                          "ensemble_ambiguous", "first_record_pre",
                                          "n_ensembles"]].astype({"settlement_row": "int64"})
    outside_scope = int((~tied["settlement_row"].isin(scope["settlement_row"])).sum())
    cover = scope.merge(tied, on="settlement_row", how="left", validate="1:1")
    assert len(cover) == n_scope, "settlement ↔ place merge changed the row count"
    for col in ("ensemble_pre", "ensemble_ambiguous", "first_record_pre"):
        cover[col] = cover[col].eq(True)          # no database place → not recorded
    by_okres = _share_table(cover, ["okres_now", "land", "okres_id", "okres_1910_cs"])
    if census is not None:
        by_okres = by_okres.merge(census[["okres_id", "lang_czech_share"]], on="okres_id",
                                  how="left", validate="m:1")
        by_okres["lang_czech_share"] = by_okres["lang_czech_share"].round(3)
    tables["settlements_by_okres_1910"] = by_okres
    tables["settlements_by_land"] = _share_table(cover, ["land"])
    tables["settlements_by_size"] = _share_table(cover, ["size_class"])
    tables["settlements_by_land_and_size"] = _share_table(cover, ["land", "size_class"])
    if census is not None:
        # a database of *Czech* theatre: coverage has to be read within language bands
        banded = cover.merge(census[["okres_id", "lang_czech_share"]], on="okres_id",
                             how="left", validate="m:1")
        assert len(banded) == n_scope, "settlement ↔ census merge changed the row count"
        banded["okres_language"] = pd.cut(
            banded["lang_czech_share"], LANGUAGE_BANDS, right=False,
            labels=LANGUAGE_LABELS).astype(object).fillna("no census row")
        czech = banded[banded["okres_language"] == LANGUAGE_LABELS[-1]]
        tables["settlements_by_land_and_language"] = _share_table(banded, ["land", "okres_language"])
        tables["settlements_czech_okresy_by_land_and_size"] = _share_table(czech, ["land", "size_class"])
        spread = _share_table(czech, ["land", "okres_id", "okres_1910_cs"])
        spread = spread[spread["settlements"] >= MIN_OKRES_SETTLEMENTS]
        tables["czech_okresy_spread_by_land"] = spread.groupby("land")["share_ensemble_pre1914"].describe(
            percentiles=[0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9]).round(3).reset_index()
    tables["scope_note"] = pd.DataFrame({
        "what": ["1910 settlements in the denominator (whole country: all; a sample: those "
                 "whose latest okres is a sample okres)",
                 "sample okres on the timeline but not its latest okres (left out)",
                 "sample places tied to a settlement outside that denominator",
                 "sample places whose page is not cached"],
        "n": [n_scope,
              int((S["in_1910"] & ~in_scope
                   & S["okres_tokens"].map(lambda t: bool(set(t) & set(okresy)))).sum()),
              outside_scope, missing_pages]})

    # ── how the database documents a place, by okres ────────────────────────
    paged = sample[sample["page_cached"]]
    tables["documentation_by_okres"] = _documentation_table(paged, "okres")
